BURHAN:v1p29/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p29/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURHAN:v1p29/r3.claim: A report in both Ṣaḥīḥs places the question about the Spirit in Medina, although its surah is Makkan; the account of the Jews directing the polytheists to ask such questions is reconciled by a second descent.
BURHAN:v1p29/r3.anchor: ومثله ما في الصحيحين عن ابن مسعود فى قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v1p29/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p29/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p29/r6.claim: A new question or incident can prompt the Prophet to receive an ayah that had already descended; its repetition reminds people of the text and shows that it encompasses the new event's ruling.
BURHAN:v1p29/r6.anchor: والحكمة فى هذا كله أنه قد يحدث سبب من سؤال أو حادثة تقتضى نزول آية وقد نزل قبل ذلك ما يتضمنها

ITQAN:v1p104/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p104/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
ITQAN:v1p104/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr lists the verse about the Spirit among verses revealed more than once.
ITQAN:v1p104/r2.anchor: وذكر ابن كثير منه آية الروح

ITQAN:v1p104/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p104/r6.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v1p104/r6.claim: Al-Zarkashī resolves the apparent clash between the Meccan status of al-Isrāʾ and Hūd and Medinan reports about their occasions by saying the verses descended twice.
ITQAN:v1p104/r6.anchor: قال فإن سورة الإسراء وهود مكيتان وسبب نزولهما يدل على أنهما نزلتا بالمدينة ولهذا أشكل ذلك على بعضهم

DURR-FULL:v5p358/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r3.claim: The Prophet explained that the Spirit being from his Lord's command meant its knowledge belonged to God, not to him.
DURR-FULL:v5p358/r3.anchor: الروح من أمر ربي يقول: من علم ربي لا علم لي به

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The closing section answers opponents’ objections and demands for signs, while reassuring the Prophet that knowledgeable people believe and sign-demanders will not.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: those objections of the opponents of the Prophet (sws) are responded to

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Here rūḥ means divine revelation, the life of the heart and intellect as spirit is life for the body; the Qur’an also calls revelation rūḥ in 16:2, 40:15, and 42:52.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the life of our heart and intellect is divine revelation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Jesus similarly taught that human life depends on every word from God, not bread alone.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The disbelievers’ question about the spirit was ridicule rather than sincere inquiry; only one who experiences it understands, and they need not be told every divine secret.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: their question was not an actual inquiry: it was to ridicule and make fun of it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Their concealed question was why revelation did not come to them; the cited language says God chooses particular servants, since not everyone is worthy, and its reality is known only to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: In other words, not every person is worthy of this

BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r2.claim: The reported occasion is that Quraysh sent Nadr ibn al-Harith, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt to consult Jews at Yathrib; they suggested asking about travelers, ancient youths, and the spirit, then judged silence on the spirit with answers to the first two as prophetic proof.
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r2.anchor: كفار عرب نضر بن حارث وأبي بن خلف وعقبة بن أبي معيط را بمدينه فرستادند

BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r3.claim: The spirit is the human body's spirit and source of life; its reality is among hidden matters God alone knows, beyond human intellect. “Command” means affair, and the possessive marks exclusive knowledge, not creation.
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r3.anchor: {عن الروح} الذي هو روح البدن الإنساني ومبدأ حياته

BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r4.speaker: البيضاوي
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r4.claim: Al-Baydawi calls the spirit an originated immaterial entity brought into being by “Be,” without matter or derivation from the body's elements.
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r4.anchor: وقال البيضاوي من الإبداعيات الكائنة بكن من غير مادة

BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r5.speaker: داوود القيصري
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r5.claim: Al-Qaysari divides existence into immaterial beings without matter or duration, material composites arising over time, and a disputed immaterial creation over time; one view has the rational soul arise with the body.
BURSEVI:v5p150#3/r5.anchor: وهذه الأقسام الباقية مظاهر الأسماء المتغيرة الأحكام

BURSEVI:v5p151/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r1.speaker: صدر الدين القنوي
BURSEVI:v5p151/r1.claim: The account in Qunawi's commentary distinguishes creation—sensible, temporal, and bodily or spiritual—from command, divine knowledge and necessity; creation follows command as its source.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r1.anchor: في شرح تفسير الفاتحة للشيخ صدر الدين القنوي قدس سره الخلق عالم العين

BURSEVI:v5p151/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r2.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v5p151/r2.claim: Al-Kawashi says the address “you were given” includes believers and unbelievers.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r2.anchor: أيها المؤمنون والكافرون كما في "تفسير الكواشي"

BURSEVI:v5p151/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p151/r3.claim: Human knowledge is slight because reasoning depends on sensory routes and necessary principles acquired by sensing particulars; losing a sense means losing some knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r3.anchor: إلا علما قليلا تستفيدونه من طرق الحواس فإن اكتساب العقل للمعارف النظرية

BURSEVI:v5p151/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p151/r4.claim: Many things escape the senses; the spirit's essence is not known directly, only through attributes distinguishing it from similar things.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r4.anchor: وهو إشارة إلى أن الروح مما لم يمكن معرفة ذاته إلا بعوارض تميزه

BURSEVI:v5p151/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r5.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v5p151/r5.claim: Bahr al-Ulum says the address is universal; when asked whether it included them, the Prophet answered that he and they had received only a little knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r5.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" الخطاب في {ومآ أوتيتم} عام

BURSEVI:v5p151/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p151/r6.claim: Finite human knowledge is little compared with God's infinite knowledge, like a drop beside a limitless ocean, answering the objection that wisdom is called abundant good.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r6.anchor: فإن علم الحادث في جنب علم القديم قليل إذ علم العباد متناه

BURSEVI:v5p151/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r7.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v5p151/r7.claim: A mystic compares saints' knowledge to a drop in seven seas, prophetic knowledge to the Prophet's likewise, and the Prophet's knowledge to God's; even much created knowledge is little beside God.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r7.anchor: قال بعض الكبار : علم الأولياء من علم الأنبياء بمنزلة قطرة

BURSEVI:v5p151/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p151/r8.speaker: أبو مدين المغربي
BURSEVI:v5p151/r8.claim: Abu Madyan says the knowledge God grants is a loan, not ours; despite receiving much we remain ignorant, and the ignorant should not claim knowledge.
BURSEVI:v5p151/r8.anchor: شيخ أبو مدين مغربي قدس سره فرمودكه اين اندكى كه خداى تعالى داده است

BURSEVI:v5p153/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p153/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p153/r1.claim: Some reports count 360,000 worlds, which God encompasses in two realms: creation and command; the first is sensible worldly life, the second the inward and unseen realm.
BURSEVI:v5p153/r1.anchor: إن الله تعالى خلق العوالم الكثيرة ففي بعض الروايات خلق ثلاثمائة وستين ألف عالم

BURSEVI:v5p153/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p153/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p153/r2.claim: The command realm consists of primordial enduring realities created directly by the command “Be”; the creation realm is mediated from existing things and is destined to perish.
BURSEVI:v5p153/r2.anchor: عالم الأمر هو الأوليات العظائم التي خلقها الله تعالى للبقاء من الروح والعقل والقلم

BURSEVI:v5p153/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p153/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p153/r3.claim: “The spirit is of my Lord’s command” identifies the spirit with the enduring command realm, rather than saying God withheld its knowledge from creation.
BURSEVI:v5p153/r3.anchor: إنما هو لتعريف الروح معناه أنه من عالم الأمر والبقاء لا من عالم الخلق والفناء

BURSEVI:v5p153/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p153/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p153/r4.claim: The view that God kept the spirit unknowable even to the Prophet is rejected: the Prophet was taught what he did not know and could not be ignorant of the spirit while knowing God.
BURSEVI:v5p153/r4.anchor: أن النبي عليه السلام لم يكن عالما به جل منصب حبيب الله عن أن يكون جاهلا بالروح

BURSEVI:v5p153/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p153/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p153/r5.claim: The Prophet's silence while awaiting revelation answered the Jews' question reflected the subtlety of a reply their dullness and hardened hearts could not grasp.
BURSEVI:v5p153/r5.anchor: فأما سكوته عن جواب سؤال الروح وتوقفه انتظارا للوحي

BURSEVI:v5p153/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p153/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p153/r6.claim: Sufi wayfarers understand the stages inwardly: the heart's light reveals the self, then the secret, spirit, hidden realm, and finally the spirit through divine witnessing.
BURSEVI:v5p153/r6.anchor: لما عبروا عن النفس وصفاتها ووصلوا إلى حريم القلب عرفوا النفس بنور القلب

BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r1.claim: The passage identifies the spirit breathed into Adam as the spirit associated with God, interpreted here as the Prophet's spirit; Adam's and his descendants' spirits derive from it.
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r1.anchor: ونفخ فيه من روحه أي : من الروح المضاف إلى نفسه

BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r2.claim: The same interpretation is applied to Jesus: Gabriel performed the blowing, while the spirit was from the Prophet's spirit associated with the divine presence.
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r2.anchor: فكانت النفخة لجبريل وروحها من روح النبي عليه السلام المضاف إلى الحضرة

BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r3.claim: This is offered as one secret behind the saying that Adam and those after him will be beneath the Prophet's banner on Judgment Day.
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r3.anchor: وهذا أحد أسرار قوله : "آدم ومن دونه تحت لوائي

BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r4.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r4.claim: “You were given little knowledge” addresses the Jews: they received an answer about the unseen but, as people of sensory worldly knowledge, scarcely understand the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v5p154#2/r4.anchor: راجع إلى اليهود الذين سألوا النبي عليه السلام عن الروح يعني أنكم سألتموني

ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi says the question most plausibly asks about the nature of the human spirit that animates the body, a subtle matter minds cannot grasp without revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر عند المنصف أن السؤال كان عن حقيقة الروح الذي هو مدار البدن الانساني ومبدأ حياته

ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r2.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says they asked about the heavenly Spirit mentioned as standing with angels on Judgment Day, a hidden matter known only by revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r2.anchor: وزعم ابن القيم أن المسؤول عنه الروح الذي أخبر الله تعالى عنه في كتابه أنه يقوم يوم القيامة مع الملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r3.claim: Al-Alusi says the human-spirit interpretation is the majority view; Ibn al-Qayyim's interpretation is nevertheless attributed to some early authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r3.anchor: والحق ما ذكرنا وهو الذي عليه الجمهور كما نص عليه في البحر وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Spirit is a creature shaped like humans, accompanying every angel who descends, and cites 78:38.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال : الروح خلق من خلق الله تعالى وصورهم على صورة بني آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r5.claim: Another report through Ata describes one Spirit-angel with ten thousand wings, vast reach, and many faces, tongues, eyes, and lips praising God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r5.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ وغيره من طريق عطاء عنه رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال في الروح المسؤل عنه : هو ملك واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r6.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r6.claim: A report attributed to Ali describes an angel with seventy thousand faces and tongues; each glorification creates an angel, but the report is rejected as unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r6.anchor: وأخرج هو وغيره أيضا عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه قال فيه : هو ملك من الملائكة له سبعون ألف وجه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r7.claim: The Imam criticizes the report attributed to Ali as unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p151#2/r7.anchor: وتعقب هذا بأنه لا يصح عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وطعن الإمام في ذلك بما طعن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Spirit is an angelic creature that angels cannot see, just as humans cannot see angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد أنه قال : الروح خلق من الملائكة عليهم السلام لا يراهم الملائكة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r2.speaker: سلمان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r2.claim: Salman gives a hierarchy in which humans are one part and jinn nine; jinn one part and angels nine; angels one part and Spirit nine; Spirit one part and cherubim nine.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r2.anchor: عن سلمان أنه قال : الإنس والجن عشرة أجزاء فالإنس جزء والجن تسعة أجزاء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r3.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r3.claim: Hasan identifies the Spirit as Gabriel, called the trustworthy Spirit in 26:193; the question would concern how he descended and conveyed revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة : الروح هو جبرائيل عليه السلام وقد سمي روحا في قوله تعالى ( نزل به الروح الأمين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r4.claim: Qatada likewise identifies the Spirit as Gabriel and takes the question to concern his descent and delivery of revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن وقتادة : الروح هو جبرائيل عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r5.speaker: some
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r5.claim: Some identify the Spirit as the Qur'an, which is called a spirit in 42:52; other interpretations are also mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم هو القرآن وقد سمي روحا في قوله تعالى ( وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r6.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the claim that the question concerns the spirit's origination.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r6.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن السؤال عن حدوث الروح بالمعنى الأول وقدمه وليس بشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r7.claim: A Bukhari-Muslim report says Jews in Medina asked the Prophet about the Spirit while he leaned on a palm stem; revelation then gave this answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في خرب المدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r8.claim: Another report says Quraysh asked Jews for a question to test Muhammad, and the Jews suggested asking about the Spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r8.anchor: أخرج أحمد والنسائي والترمذي والحاكم وصححه وابن حبان وجماعة عن ابن عباس قال قالت قريش لليهود

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r9.claim: A sira account says Quraysh sent al-Nadr and Uqba to Jewish scholars, who proposed questions about the Cave Companions, Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the Spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r9.anchor: أن قريشا بعثت النضر بن الحرث وعقبه بن أبي معيط إلى أحبار يهود بالمدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r10.claim: The sira account makes the verse Meccan, whereas the canonical report makes it Medinan; some reconcile them by saying it was revealed twice.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا وما قبله مكية وعلى خبر الصحيحين مدنية وجمع بعضهم بين ذلك بأن الآية نزلت مرتين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r11.claim: If Spirit means Qur'an or Gabriel, the verse connects closely to the preceding healing passage and the preservation of revelation; on the majority view it interrupts to expose wrongdoers' distraction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r11.anchor: فوجه تعقيب ما تقدم بها أن فسر الروح بالقرآن ظاهر ملائم لقوله تعالى ( وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفاء ورحمة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r12.claim: The answer repeats 'the Spirit' instead of using a pronoun to show emphasis and special concern.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r12.anchor: قل الروح ( أظهر في مقام الإضمار إظهارا لكمال الاعتناء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r13.claim: Min in 'from my Lord's command' may be partitive or explanatory; amr means affair, and the relation denotes special knowledge rather than creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r13.anchor: كلمة ( من ) تبعيضية وقيل : بيانية والأمر واحد الأمور بمعنى الشأن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r14.claim: The phrase honors both the Spirit and the Lord: the Spirit belongs to secrets God reserves from human intellect.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p152/r14.anchor: الإضافة للإختصاص العلمي لا الإيجادي إذ ما من شيء إلا وهو مضاف إليه عز وجل بهذا المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r1.claim: Al-Alusi says the clause about little knowledge cannot attach to the preceding examples; he notes a proposed reading as deliberate non-disclosure and a prohibition on further questioning.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r1.anchor: لا يمكن تعلقه بأمثال ذلك وهذا على ما قيل ترك للبيان ونهي لهم عن السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r2.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq and al-Tabari report from Ata that the verse was revealed in Mecca; after the Hijra Jewish scholars asked whether its warning addressed them or Muslims, and the Prophet said both.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r2.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار قال : نزلت هذه الآية بمكة فلما هاجر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r3.claim: In the same report, the Prophet explains that the Torah's religious guidance is little beside God's limitless knowledge, though useful when followed; this rejects a literally universal reading of its contents.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r3.anchor: هي في علم الله تعالى قليل وقد آتاكم الله تعالى ما إن عملتم به انتفعتم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r4.speaker: اليهود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r4.claim: A report authenticated by al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Hakim says Jews called their Torah great knowledge and its possession a great good, prompting the verse about the sea.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r4.anchor: وفي رواية النسائي وابن حبان والترمذي والحاكم وصححاها أن اليهود قالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r5.claim: The reports do not conflict: knowledge is relatively little beside God's knowledge and relatively abundant beside something below it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r5.anchor: فالشيء يكون قليلا بالنسبة إلى ما فوقه وكثيرا بالنسبة إلى ما تحته

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r6.speaker: عكرمة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r6.claim: Ibn Mardawayh reports that Jews claimed the address was theirs; the Prophet answered that it included both communities, and they contrasted it with the promise of abundant good through wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قال ذلك قال اليهود : نحن مختصون بهذا الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r7.claim: The contrast between abundant wisdom and little knowledge is also relative: human wisdom comprises what human capacity can grasp for worldly and afterlife order, little beside God's knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r7.anchor: الحكمة الإنسانية أن يعلم من الخير ما تسعه القوة البشرية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r8.speaker: ابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes the address about limited knowledge as universal, applying to all people.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r8.anchor: وإلى تعميم الخطاب بحيث يشمل الناس أجمعين ذهب ابن جريج

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود والأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r9.claim: Their reading وما أوتوا, together with the report explicitly addressing the questioners, points instead to a restricted audience; al-Iraqi calls the latter report unsound and Al-Alusi is unsure about the first report's status.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r9.anchor: ظاهر قراءة ابن مسعود والأعمش ( وما أوتوا ) فإنه يقتضي الإختصاص بالسائلين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r10.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r10.claim: They explain the spirit as an originating creation brought into being by God's creative command كن, without material or derivation from another source; the answer gives a summary rather than the essence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r10.anchor: معنى كون الروح من أمره تعالى أنه من الإبداعيات الكائنة بالأمر التكويني

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r11.claim: The concise answer redirects an inquiry into the spirit's essence: it is originated without matter, beyond human comprehension, and only this general description fits the stated limit of knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r11.anchor: فالمراد من الأمر واحد الأوامر أعني كن والسؤال عن الحقيقة والجواب إجمالي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r12.claim: Al-Alusi compares this wise redirection to Moses answering Pharaoh's question about the Lord of the worlds, since the divine reality exceeds human apprehension.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p153/r12.anchor: كجواب موسى عليه السلام سؤال فرعون إياه ما رب العالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r1.claim: The little knowledge humans receive is largely gained through the senses, since abstract reasoning usually begins from sensed particulars; absent, imperceptible, or obscured things and their essences escape this route.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r1.anchor: علما قليلا تستفيدونه من طرق الحواس فإن تعقل المعارف النظرية إنما هو في الأكثر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r2.claim: Some hold that the spirit's essence cannot be known, making the two proposed answers effectively alike.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r2.anchor: ظاهر كلام بعضهم أن الوقوف على كنه الروح غير ممكن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r3.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r3.claim: Al-Khafaji distinguishes the spirit, whose essence may be known, from the divine essence, which cannot be known.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r3.anchor: وفرق الخفاجي بأن بيان كنه الروح ممكن بخلاف كنه الذات الأقدس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r4.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r4.claim: Al-Kashf says the spirit is known by removing veils from the heart's sight through the jewels of divine speech: clear to mystics, hidden from those occupied with other concerns.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r4.anchor: سبيل معرفة الروح إزالة الغشاء عن أبصار القلوب باجتلاء كحل الجواهر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits his statement that the Prophet died without knowing the spirit; Al-Alusi suggests Ibn Burayda may have meant its knowledge is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بريدة قال : لقد قبض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يعلم الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r6.claim: Al-Alusi argues that otherwise the Prophet would not have died before learning everything knowable, citing the report of Muadh's night vision and disclosure of all things.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r6.anchor: فلم يقبض رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى علم كل شيء يمكن العلم به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r7.speaker: معاذ
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r7.claim: A report from Muadh, called sound by al-Tirmidhi and hasan-sahih by al-Bukhari, describes God placing His hand between the Prophet's shoulders, after which everything became clear to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r7.anchor: عن معاذ رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : إني قمت من الليل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r8.claim: Some books vocalize the vision report with رأيت in the passive and الروح nominative; that reading weakens the objection but is less apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r8.anchor: و ( رأيت ) يعلم في الخبر السابق في بعض الكتب مضبوطا بالبناء للمفعول والروح مضبوطا بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r9.speaker: بعض متأخري الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r9.claim: Some later Sufis say the spirit's essence, and indeed the essences of all things, cannot be grasped; Al-Alusi leaves acceptance or rejection to the reader.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r9.anchor: أنه يمتنع الوقوف على حقيقة الروح بل ذكر هذا البعض أن حقيقة جميع الأشياء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r10.claim: Al-Alusi questions treating command and creation as established Arab categories for immaterial and material things, and says the appeal to the verse about creation and command is weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r10.anchor: إطلاق عالم الأمر على الكائن من غير تحصل من مادة وتولد من أصل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r11.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r11.claim: Al-Razi says the question could concern many things, but the answer fits either the spirit's essence or whether it is eternal or originated.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r11.anchor: ليس في قوله تعالى : ( ويسألونك عن الروح ) ما يدل على وجه منها إلا أن الجواب المذكور

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r12.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r12.claim: On the essence reading, the spirit is a simple, immaterial, originated substance whose effect is to give life to the body; ignorance of its specific essence does not negate its existence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r12.anchor: أنها جوهر بسيط مجرد محدث بأمر الله تعالى وتكوينه وتأثيره إفادة الحياة للجسد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r13.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r13.claim: On the origination reading, the spirit is created by God; its initially empty state and later acquisition of knowledge would signal change and therefore origination.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r13.anchor: الأرواح في مبدأ الفطرة تكون خالية عن العلوم والمعارف ثم يحصل فيها ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r14.claim: Al-Alusi finds the origination argument a poor fit: the questioners could already know what they asked, so their limited knowledge does not suit this proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p154/r14.anchor: لا يساعده التعرض لبيان قلة علمهم فإن ما سألوا عنه مما يفي به علمهم حينئذ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r1.claim: Al-Razi appears to distinguish disagreement about the human being's essence from disagreement about the spirit, though Al-Alusi is uncertain about that distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r1.anchor: وظاهر كلام الإمام أن الاختلاف في حقيقته غير الاختلاف في حقيقة الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r2.speaker: جمهور المتكلمين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r2.claim: Most theologians identify the human being with the perceptible bodily structure; Al-Razi refutes this with seventeen transmitted and rational arguments.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r2.anchor: فذهب جمهور المتكلمين إلى أنه عبارة عن هذه البنية المحسوسة والهيكل المجسم المحسوس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r3.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r3.claim: Al-Razi argues that bodily parts change through growth, decline, and loss while the person is necessarily understood to persist through life.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r3.anchor: أجزاء البنية متغيرة زيادة ونقصانا وذبولا ونموا والعلم الضروري قاض بأن الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r4.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r4.claim: Even when attention is absorbed by some or all bodily parts, a person remains aware of the self and says I acted or left something undone; the self is therefore not those parts.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r4.anchor: ولا يغفل عن نفسه المعينة بدليل أنه يقول مع ذلك الشاغل فعلت وتركت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r5.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r5.claim: The human essence can appear without its usual body, as with Gabriel in Dihya's form, or persist after its form changes, as in metamorphosis into an ape.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r5.anchor: جبريل عليه السلام كثيرا ما رؤي في صورة دحية الكلب وإبليس عليه اللعنة رؤي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r6.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r6.claim: A report says the deceased person's spirit flutters above the bier and warns family not to be deceived by worldly life or wealth, implying the human is something beyond the carried body.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r6.anchor: أن الميت إذا حمل على النعش رفرف روحه فوق النعش ويقول : يا أهلي ويا ولدي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r7.speaker: أقوال مختلفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r7.claim: Other definitions identify the human as a spirit in the heart, an indivisible brain-part, innate heat from fiery elements, or blood; the source says nearly a thousand views exist.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r7.anchor: وقيل : إن الانسان هو الروح الذي في القلب وقيل إنه جزء لا يتجزأ في الدماغ

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r8.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r8.claim: One of two positions favored by investigators defines the human as a luminous, upper-world body distinct in essence from the perceptible body, permeating it and supplying life while it can receive its influence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r8.anchor: جسم نوراني علوي حي متحرك مخالف بالماهية لهذا الجسم المحسوس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r9.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r9.claim: Al-Razi calls this corporeal-spirit position strong and noble because it closely matches scriptural accounts of life and death.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r9.anchor: مذهب قوي وقول شريف يحب التأمل فيه فإنه شديد المطابقة لما ورد في الكتب الإلهية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r10.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r10.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim calls this position correct and the only sound one, claiming support from scripture, Sunna, the Companions' consensus, reason, innate disposition, and 105 proofs.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p155/r10.anchor: إنه الصواب ولا يصح غيره وعليه دل الكتاب والسنة وإجماع الصحابة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r1.speaker: أكثر الإلهيين من الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r1.claim: A second position says the spirit is neither body nor bodily, inside nor outside the world, connected nor separate; it relates to the body by governing and acting upon it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r1.anchor: أنه ليس بجسم ولا جسماني وهو الروح وليس بداخل العالم ولا خارجه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r2.speaker: أبو القاسم الراغب الأصفهاني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r2.claim: Al-Raghib, al-Ghazali, Ma'mar, al-Mufid, some Karramiyya, and most mystics and ascetics are listed among Muslim proponents of the immaterial-spirit view.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r2.anchor: منهم الشيخ أبو القاسم الراغب الأصفهاني وحجة الإسلام أبو حامد الغزالي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r3.speaker: ابن سينا
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r3.claim: Ibn Sina wrote a separate treatise defending this view; Al-Alusi particularly commends its argument from the soul's awareness of itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r3.anchor: وللشيخ الرئيس رسالة مفردة في ذلك سماها بالحجج الغر أحكمها وأتقنها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r4.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r4.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim refutes the arguments for an immaterial spirit in his beneficial book al-Ruh.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r4.anchor: وابن القيم زيف حججه في كتابه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r5.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r5.claim: Al-Razi argues from the verse that a bodily spirit would require an account of its material stages; the answer instead says it enters existence by God's creative command, indicating a holy immaterial substance.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r5.anchor: فلما لم يقل ذلك وقال هو من أمر ربي بمعنى أنه لا يحدث ولا يدخل في الوجود

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r6.claim: Al-Alusi calls this and similar scriptural or hadith arguments rhetorical persuasion rather than decisive proof; the spirit's divine attribution and related texts indicate its nobility and detachment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى أن ذلك من الاقناعيات الخطابية وهي كثيرة في هذا الباب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r7.claim: Other suggestive proofs include the Prophet's descriptions as the naked warner and as one fed and sustained by his Lord, which imply spiritual distinction and nearness.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r7.anchor: أنا النذير العريان ففيه إلى تجرد الروح عن علائق الأجرام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r8.speaker: ثابت بن قرة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r8.claim: Thabit ibn Qurra says the spirit is attached to subtle, luminous celestial bodies that permeate the human body and govern it while present; Al-Alusi calls this a composite view but does not rule it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r8.anchor: ن قرة يقول : إن الروح متعلق بأجسام سماوية نورانية لطيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r9.speaker: المسلمون
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r9.claim: Muslims agree the spirit is temporally originated like the rest of the world, but differ on whether it predates the body or arises afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r9.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أنه حادث حدوثا زمانيا كسائر أجزاء العالم إلا أنهم اختلفوا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r10.speaker: محمد بن نصر المروزي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r10.claim: A group including al-Marwazi and Ibn Hazm holds that spirits were created before bodies; Al-Alusi says Ibn Hazm falsely claims consensus for this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r10.anchor: فذهب طائفة إلى الحدوث قبل منهم محمد بن نصر المروري وأبو محمد بن حزم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r11.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r11.claim: The sound hadith in both Sahih collections says spirits are gathered troops: those that recognize one another become harmonious and those that do not remain at odds.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r11.anchor: بما في الصحيحين من حديث عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : الأرواح جنود مجندة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r12.speaker: الخطابي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r12.claim: Al-Khattabi interprets the hadith of spirits as evidence that souls were created before bodies; Ibn Hazm imagines them in a separate barzakh, descending to prepared bodies and returning after death, without scriptural proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156/r12.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الخطابي معنى هذا الحديث الإخبار عن كون الأرواح مخلوقة قبل الأجساد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r1.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r1.claim: Some cite a report that God created spirits two thousand years before bodies, but Ibn al-Qayyim says its chain is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r1.anchor: خبر خلق الله تعالى الأرواح قبل الأجساد بألفي عام وتعقبه ابن القيم بأنه لا يصح إسناده

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r2.speaker: حجة الإسلام الغزالي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r2.claim: Others, including al-Ghazali, hold that the spirit is created after the body begins forming; Ibn al-Qayyim cites the authentic fetal-development report in which an angel breathes in the spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r2.anchor: وذهب آخرون منهم حجة الإسلام الغزالي إلى الحدوث بعد ومن أدلة ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r3.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim argues that if the spirit already existed, the report would say the angel brings it and inserts it, rather than breathing it into the fetus.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r3.anchor: أن الروح لو كان مخلوقا قبل لقيل ثم يرسل إليه الملك بالروح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r4.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r4.claim: In Rawdat al-Muhibbin, Ibn al-Qayyim calls pre-created spirits a plainly false view and says spirit and body are created together when the angel breathes into the fetus after four months.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r4.anchor: القول بأن الأرواح خلقت قبل الأجساد قول فاسد وخطأ صريح والقول الصحيح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says there is room for reflection on Ibn al-Qayyim's claim, while the verse about forming humans as another creation supports origination.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r5.anchor: انتهى وفيه تأمل ويوافق مذهب الحدوث قوله تعالى : ( ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر )

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r6.speaker: أفلاطون
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r6.claim: Plato and earlier philosophers held the spirit eternal; Aristotle instead held it arises with the body's preparedness, as some Muslim thinkers did.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r6.anchor: وذهب أفلاطون ومن تقدمه الفلاسفة إلى قدم الروح وذهب المعلم الأول إلى حدوثها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r7.claim: Al-Alusi prefers explaining that the body's particular temperament calls for a governing principle, and the Giver bestows an immaterial cognizer; the soul is immaterial in essence but dependent on the body in action.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p156#2/r7.anchor: فالنفس الإنسانية مجردة ذاتا مادية فعلا فهي من حيث الفعل من التدبير والتحريك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r1.speaker: بعض صدور المتأخرين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r1.claim: A later eminent scholar suggests that Plato's statements about the soul's eternity can be given a subtle interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r1.anchor: ويمكن تأويل ما نقل عن أفلاطون في باب قدم النفس إلى هذا بوجه لطيف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says most scholars treat spirit and soul as one thing, and reports use each term for the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r2.anchor: فحكى ابن زيد عن أكثر العلماء أنهما شيء واحد فقد صح في الأخبار إطلاق كل منهما على الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r3.claim: A sound raised report from Abu Hurayra describes a believer wishing for the soul to leave at death and the believer's spirit ascending to heaven, supporting the terms' interchangeability.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رفعه أن المؤمن ينزل به الموت ويعاين ما يعاين يود لو خرجت نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r4.speaker: ابن حبيب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r4.claim: Ibn Habib distinguishes them: spirit is the breath moving in a person, while the soul has limbs and feels pleasure, pain, joy, and grief; it leaves during sleep and returns to the living body.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r4.anchor: وقال ابن حبيب : هما شيئان فالروح هو النفس المتردد في الإنسان والنفس أمر غير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r5.speaker: ابن منده
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r5.claim: Ibn Mandah transmits views that the soul is earthy-fiery and spirit luminous, or that the soul is human while spirit is divine; hadith scholars also distinguish them, with spirit sustaining the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r5.anchor: وحكى ابن منده عن بعضهم أن النفس طينية نارية والروح نورية روحانية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r6.speaker: أهل الأثر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r6.claim: The hadith scholars' distinction makes the soul the human form, desire, and trial, drawn to this world, while the spirit calls toward and prefers the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r6.anchor: وذكر أن أهل الأثر على المغايرة وأن قوام النفس بالروح والنفس صورة العبد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r7.speaker: المحقق الفرغاني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r7.claim: Al-Farghani defines the soul as a life-bearing vapor from the inner heart, shaped by the spiritual spirit, which governs the body and can incline toward either higher or lower qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r7.anchor: أن النفس المضافة إلى الإنسان عبارة عن بخار ضبابي منبعث من باطن القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r8.claim: Al-Alusi's conclusion is that spirit and soul may be identical in some uses and distinct in others.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r8.anchor: والحق أنهما قد يتحدان إطلاقا وقد يتغيران

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r9.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r9.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim follows the majority in treating spirit and soul as one in essence; Sufis say the soul, after discipline and remembrance, becomes spirit and can rise to God's secret.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r9.anchor: وابن القيم اعتمد ما عليه الأكثرون من الاتحاد ذاتا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r10.speaker: الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r10.claim: Sufis describe four stages of ascent: purifying outward practice, cleansing inward character, adorning the soul with sacred forms, and effacing self-awareness before divine majesty.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r10.anchor: الأولى تهذيب الظاهر باستعمال النواميس الإلهية من القيام والصيام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r11.claim: The seeker begins animal-like, gradually acquiring appetite, anger, greed, and envy; awakening to higher pleasures leads to repentance, turning to God, and leaving worldly excess for afterlife perfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r11.anchor: أن الإنسان أول ما يولد فهو كباقي الحيوانات لا يعرف إلا الأكل والشرب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r12.claim: On entering the path, the seeker renounces distractions, adopts piety and true asceticism, and continually audits and distrusts the self because it loves desires and hidden snares.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p157/r12.anchor: ثم إذا دخل في الطريق يزهد عن كل ما يعوقه عن مقصوده

ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r1.speaker: بعض الأكابر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r1.claim: An unnamed spiritual elder realized that his soul urged jihad only to escape the toil of prayer and fasting through death, so he refused its suggestion.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r1.anchor: يحكى عن بعض الأكابر أن نفسه لم تزل تأمره بالجهاد وتحثه عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r2.claim: As the seeker is purified, inner illumination reveals unseen flashes and imaginal realities, drawing him to retreat, remembrance, worship, watchfulness, and freedom from sensory pleasures.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r2.anchor: يتنور باطنه ويظهر له لوامح أنوار الغيب وينفتح له باب الملكوت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r3.claim: The seeker becomes absorbed in longing and ecstasy, witnesses hidden realities through unveiling, and eventually gains stable spiritual tranquility and visions of angels and higher realms.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r3.anchor: فيتحقق بالمشاهدة والمعاينة والمكاشفة ويظهر له أنوار حقيقية تارة وتختفي أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r4.claim: At annihilation, the seeker's sense of self collapses before divine majesty; remaining absorbed in unity veils him from creation, while a higher station returns him to sobriety and sees detail within unity.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r4.anchor: وهذا مقام الفناء والمحو وهو غاية السفر الأول للسالكين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r5.claim: The returned knower sees God in everything and everything through God without multiplicity or corporeality, in a state beyond ordinary reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r5.anchor: ويرى كل شيء بالحق على وجه لا يوجب التكثر والتجسم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r6.claim: Some describe the knower as truly assuming God's attributes; Al-Alusi rejects any idea that divine attributes become accidents in a human soul and allows only an ineffable relation beyond bodily qualities.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r6.anchor: لا بمعنى صيرورة صفاته تعالى عرضا قائما بالنفس فإن هذا مما لا يتصور أبدا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r7.claim: The Sufi station described as becoming a secret of God may refer to this highest state, but it requires the path of the righteous, not speculation alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p158/r7.anchor: ولعل مرادهم بالمرتبة التي تترقى إليها النفس فتكون سرا من أسرار الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r1.speaker: طائفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r1.claim: One group says the spirit dies because every soul tastes death, only God remains, angels also die, and the two deaths in the afterlife verse require death of both body and spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r1.anchor: لأنها نفس وكل نفس ذائقة الموت وقد دل الكتاب على أنه لا يبقى إلا الله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r2.speaker: طائفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r2.claim: Another group says the spirit does not die, since its reward or punishment continues after separation from the body until God restores it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r2.anchor: إنها لا تموت للأحاديث الدالة على نعيمها وعذابها بعد المفارقة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r3.claim: Al-Alusi defines the spirit's death as separation from the body; it tastes death in that sense but is not annihilated, returning for everlasting reward or punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r3.anchor: موت الروح هو مفارقتها الجسد فإن أريد بموتها هذا القدر فهي ذائقة الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r4.claim: The spirit is excepted from the trumpet's shock; shock need not mean death, and destruction can mean loss of function rather than annihilation; he rejects the proposed reading of the two deaths.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r4.anchor: وهي مستثناة ممن يصعق عند النفخ في الصور على أن الصعق لا يلزم منه الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r5.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r5.claim: Philosophers also say the soul survives bodily death, and Ibn Sina begins an argument that body and soul have no necessary causal dependence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r5.anchor: وإلى أنها لا تموت بموت البدن ذهبت الفلاسفة أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r6.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r6.claim: The philosophical proof says that if body and soul coexist without dependence, losing one need not destroy the other; if one depends on the other, neither can be the other's necessary cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r6.anchor: وإن كانت المعية في الوجود فقط من غير أن يكون لأحدهما حاجة في ذلك الوجود إلى الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r7.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r7.claim: The body cannot cause the immaterial soul: corporeal causes act through position, matter is weaker than an immaterial substance, and the body is neither its receptive, formal, nor final cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r7.anchor: كل ما لا يفعل إلا بواسطة الوضع استحال أن يفعل أفعالا مجردة عن الحيز والوضع

ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r8.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r8.claim: Since body and soul have no necessary relation, the body's destruction from poor temperament, composition, or disintegration does not entail the soul's destruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p159/r8.anchor: فإذا ليس بين البدن والنفس علاقة واجبة الثبوت أصلا فلا يكون عدم أحدهما علة لعدم الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r1.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r1.claim: In reply to the objection that the body causes the soul's beginning, philosophers say a condition may trigger origination without being needed for continued existence, so its loss cannot cause the soul's destruction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r1.anchor: كان شرطا للحدوث فقط وكان غنيا في وجوده عن ذلك الشيء

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r2.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r2.claim: The body is an instrument through which the naturally perfection-seeking soul gains completion and governance; losing that instrument does not destroy the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r2.anchor: ذلك الشرط مستعدا لأن يكون آلة للنفس في تحصيل الكمالات

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r3.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r3.claim: Philosophers prove the soul's impossibility of annihilation, while Al-Alusi says that from his own theological position its annihilation is not impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160/r3.anchor: ذهب الفلاسفة إلى استحالة انعدام النفس وبرهنوا على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r1.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says each soul takes an image from its former body and is more distinguishable from other souls than bodies are; he doubts individuation on the immaterialist account.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r1.anchor: أن كل روح تأخذ من بدنها صورة تتميز بها عن غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r2.claim: Al-Alusi disagrees that immaterial spirits cannot be distinguished: immaterialists can explain their differences by bodily attachment or another mode of individuation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r2.anchor: فإن القائلين بذلك قائلون بالتمايز أيضا باعتبار ما يحصل لها من التعلق بالبدن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم الكوراني
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r3.claim: Al-Kurani says departed spirits attach to fitting imaginal bodies, as suggested by reports that martyrs' spirits dwell in green birds and believers' children in sparrows.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r3.anchor: أن الأرواح بعد مفارقتها أبدانها المخصوصة تتعلق بأبدان أخر مثالية

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r4.claim: Sahih Muslim reports from Ibn Masud that martyrs' spirits dwell in the bellies of green birds; related reports describe them as green or white birds and children of believers as sparrows.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r4.anchor: في صحيح مسلم عن ابن مسعود أن أرواح الشهداء في أجواف طير خضر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r5.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r5.claim: Some theologians reject reports placing spirits inside birds because two spirits cannot occupy one body; Al-Alusi says the objection overlooks that the bird could have only the martyr's spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r5.anchor: لما في ذلك من تعلق روحين في بدن واحد وقد قالوا باستحالته

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r6.claim: Even if the reports mean a spirit is literally inside a bird, Al-Alusi says no impossibility follows, just as a fetus is inside its mother's body.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r6.anchor: لجواز أن تكون الروح في جوف الطير على نحو كون الجنين في بطن أمه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r7.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r7.claim: Reports indicate that spirits have different abodes after death: prophets are in the highest Illiyyin, martyrs in Paradise, and children's spirits are described similarly.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r7.anchor: الذي دلت عليه الأخبار أن مستقر الأرواح بعد المفارقة مختلف

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r8.claim: The Prophet's last words were a prayer for the highest companion, supporting the claim that prophets' spirits dwell in the highest Illiyyin.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r8.anchor: وصح أن آخر كلمة تكلم بها صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم الرفيق الأعلى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r9.speaker: ابن المبارك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak transmits Ka'b's account of martyrs' souls grazing as green birds by a river at Paradise's gate under a green dome, receiving food morning and evening; Ibn Rajab assigns this perhaps to ordinary or afterlife martyrs.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r9.anchor: جنة فيها طير خضر ترعى فيها أرواح الشهداء على بارق نهر بباب الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r10.speaker: الإمام الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r10.claim: Al-Shafi'i says ordinary believers' spirits also reside in Paradise, supported by the report that a believer's soul is like a bird in its trees until resurrection and by Umm Bishr's report.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p160#2/r10.anchor: وأما مستقر أرواح سائر المؤمنين فقيل في الجنة أيضا وهو نص الإمام الشافعي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r1.claim: Wahb says a white house in the seventh heaven is where the spirits of believers gather.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r1.anchor: إن لله تعالى في السماء السابعة دار يقال لها البيضاء يجتمع فيها أرواح المؤمنين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r2.speaker: أم بشر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r2.claim: A report from Umm Bishr places unbelievers' spirits in black birds' crops, eating and drinking fire and dwelling in Hell, where they plead not to be joined by their brothers.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r2.anchor: أن أرواح الكفار في حواصل طير سود تأكل من النار وتشرب من النار

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r3.speaker: عامة أهل الحديث
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r3.claim: Ibn Hazm attributes to most hadith scholars the view that the dead spirits reside in the courtyards of their graves, citing the displayed seat and the greeting to the inhabitants of believing graves.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r3.anchor: وقيل : مستقر أواح الموتى أفنية قبورهم وحكى هذا ابن حزم عن عامة أهل الحديث

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r4.speaker: ابن عبد البر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r4.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr prefers grave courtyards as the abode of spirits other than martyrs; Al-Alusi rejects permanent confinement there but accepts that spirits may be present temporarily.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r4.anchor: ورجح ابن عبد البر أن مستقر أرواح ما عدا الشهداء بأفنية القبور

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r5.claim: Mujahid says spirits are above their graves for seven days after burial; Al-Alusi accepts this as temporary presence, not proof that the grave courtyard is their permanent abode.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r5.anchor: كما روي عن مجاهد الأرواح على القبور سبعة أيام من يوم دفن الميت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r6.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r6.claim: Some investigators say a spirit has an unknowable connection wherever it is, allowing it to return greetings, recognize visitors, and be shown its future seat.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r6.anchor: أن الأرواح حيث كانت لها اتصال لا يعلم حقيقته إلا الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r7.claim: Others allow spirits to move from their abode and return rapidly wherever God wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r7.anchor: لامانع من انتقالها من مستقرها وعودها إليه في أسرع وقت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r8.speaker: ابن رجب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r8.claim: The Bara ibn Azib report says a believer's spirit is returned to the earth after its record is written in Illiyyin; Ibn Rajab says this alone cannot outweigh many reports placing spirits in Paradise, and the cited earth verse concerns bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r8.anchor: إن حديث البراء وحده لا يعارض الأحاديث الكثيرة المصرحة بأن الأرواح في الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r9.speaker: طائفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r9.claim: A group places all spirits in the lowest heaven, to Adam's right or left, based on the Mi'raj report of people on either side whom he greets as destined for Paradise or Hell.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p161/r9.anchor: مستقر الأرواح مطلقا في السماء الدنيا عن يمين آدم عليه السلام وعن شماله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r1.claim: Al-Alusi says seeing the two groups beside Adam does not prove their permanent abode is there; the Prophet saw Paradise and Hell from other locations too.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r1.anchor: فقد رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الجنة والنار في صلاة الكسوف وهو في الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r2.speaker: النسفي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r2.claim: Al-Nasafi divides spirits into four abodes: prophets in Paradise, martyrs in green birds, obedient believers looking at Paradise, and sinful believers in the air between heaven and earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r2.anchor: جعل الأرواح على أربعة أقسام أرواح الأنبياء عليهم السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r3.speaker: النسفي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r3.claim: Al-Nasafi places unbelievers' spirits in black birds in Sijjin beneath the seventh earth, still connected to bodies so both spirit and body suffer.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r3.anchor: وأما أرواح الكفار ففي سجين في جوف طير سود تحت الأرض السابعة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r4.claim: Al-Alusi says al-Nasafi's claim that obedient believers do not enjoy Paradise conflicts with sound reports that their spirits do enjoy it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r4.anchor: وما ذكره في أرواح المطيعين مخالف لما صح من أنها تتمتع في الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r5.speaker: الإفصاح
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r5.claim: Al-Ifsah reconciles reports by assigning blessed spirits varied forms and roles: in trees or birds, in Paradise forms, visiting their bodies, meeting new spirits, or under Adam's or Abraham's care.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r5.anchor: أن المنعم من الأرواح على جهات مختلفة منها ما هو طائر في شجر الجنة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r6.speaker: القرطبي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls this a good synthesis that reconciles reports, and al-Suyuti accepts it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r6.anchor: وهذا قول حسن يجمع الأخبار حتى لا تتدافع وارتضاه الجلال السيوطي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r7.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r7.claim: A report reaching Malik says the spirit is released to go wherever it wishes; Al-Alusi says that, if sound, it cannot be unrestricted.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي الدنيا عن مالك قال : بلغني أن الروح مرسلة تذهب حيث شاءت

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r8.claim: Some claim the spirit's abode is sheer nonexistence because it is an accident identified with life; Al-Alusi condemns this as false and contrary to revelation, consensus, and sound reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r8.anchor: حتى زعم بعضهم أن مستقرها لعدم المحض وهو مبني على أنها من الإعراض

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r9.speaker: ابن برجان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r9.claim: Ibn Barjan distinguishes the soul, formed from the body's hidden essence, from spirit, formed from the soul's hidden essence; spirit's life is God's gift and its death is stillness, while bodily death is spirit's departure.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r9.anchor: والنفس مبرأة من باطن ما خلق منه الجسم وأوجد تبارك وتعالى الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r10.speaker: ابن برجان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r10.claim: For a believer, heaven opens and the spirit rises, while the soul's reality inhabits the lower region and the spiritual reality the heavens; this explains Moses praying in his grave and Abraham beneath a tree before ascent.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r10.anchor: فإن كان مؤمنا فتحت له أبواب السماء حتى يصعد إلى ربه عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r11.speaker: ابن برجان
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r11.claim: For an evildoer, heaven does not open and the soul is cast down; Al-Alusi says this distinction resolves many apparent conflicts about spirit, soul, and bodily location.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r11.anchor: وإن كان شقيا لم يفتح له فرمي من علو إلى الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r12.claim: The report that a person recognizes a believing brother who passes his grave does not prove the spirit sits at the grave; the entity there may be the soul connected to spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p162/r12.anchor: ليس نصا في أن الروح على القبر إذ يفهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r1.claim: Spirits pass through states known only to God, including absorption in witnessing divine beauty; the hadith about the Prophet's spirit being returned means he awakens from that absorption to answer greetings.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r1.anchor: والذي ينبغي أن يعول عليه مع ما ذكر أن الأرواح وإن اختلف مستقرها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r2.claim: Though spirits have different reward-given abodes, they may roam God's kingdom by permission according to their nearness; some appear to living people while awake, and spirits meet, visit, and converse.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r2.anchor: لكن لها جولانا في ملك الله تعالى حيث شاء جل جلاله ولا يكون إلا بعد الإذن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r3.claim: Living and dead spirits may meet in dreams; only those who dismiss dreams as baseless fantasies deny this, but no legal ruling should rest on a dream because its truth remains uncertain.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r3.anchor: ولا يمكن ذلك إلا من يجعل الرؤيا خيالات لا أصل لها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r4.speaker: ثابت بن قيس بن شماس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r4.claim: In a report accepted as sound by Ibn Abd al-Barr and others, the slain Thabit appeared in a soldier's dream, identified his stolen armor and location, and requested payment of debts and emancipation of a slave.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r4.anchor: وكان عليه درع نفيسة فمر به رجل من المسلمين فأخذها فبينا رجل من الجند نائم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r5.claim: Al-Alusi explains that Abu Bakr's execution of Thabit's testament was allowed by his daughter as heir because circumstances supported the dream; alternatively, payment came from public funds.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r5.anchor: بأن ذلك كان بإجازة الوارث وهي بنته لغلبة ظن صدق الرؤيا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r6.speaker: ابن القيم
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r6.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim records similar, even more remarkable, dream accounts concerning Mus'ab ibn Jaththama and Awf ibn Malik.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r6.anchor: ومثل هذه القصة قصة مصعب بن جثامة وعوف بن مالك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r7.speaker: بعض الآثار
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r7.claim: Some reports say spirits may be permitted to visit their families; spirits of those who die owing prohibited loans may be detained, a restriction Al-Alusi says is not true of every debt.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r7.anchor: وربما يؤذن لأرواح بعض الناس في زيارة أهليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r8.claim: Spirit illuminates every bodily part, even if the body is scattered; perhaps this applies to the original parts from which the person is resurrected.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r8.anchor: إن اتصال الروح بالبدن لا يختص بجزء دون جزء بل هي متصلة مشرقة على سائر أجزائه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r9.claim: If the spirit is immaterial, it has no location inside or outside the world; only the body it governs has an abode.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r9.anchor: أن الروح على القول بتجردها لا مستقر لها بل لا يقال أنها داخل العالم أو خارجه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r10.speaker: بعض الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r10.claim: Some Sufis allow one spirit to govern multiple bodies, one original and another imaginal or an extraordinary manifestation, like Gabriel appearing as Dihya or Quran as a pale man.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r10.anchor: ذكر بعضهم أن أحد البدنين هو البدن الأصلي والآخر مثالي يظهر للعيان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r11.speaker: الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r11.claim: Philosophers reject one soul inhabiting multiple bodies because all the bodies would share the same knowledge; Al-Alusi says the argument also implies that any two differently informed people have different souls and proves too little.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r11.anchor: لأنه يلزم أن يكون معلوم أحدها معلوم الآخر ومجهول أحدها مجهول الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r12.claim: The Sufi theory would allow one spirit to appear in several places, as Gabriel could appear to the Prophet as Dihya without leaving the Lote Tree; they also invoke divine manifestation in forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r12.anchor: في حال ظهوره في صورة دحية أو أعرابي غيره بين يدي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يفارق سدرة المنتهى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r13.speaker: أقوال مختلفة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r13.claim: Animal spirits are said either to remain in the air after death or to cease; if animals are resurrected, Al-Alusi favors their continued existence, but if not, he favors their extinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p163/r13.anchor: فالأولى أن يقال ببقاء أرواحها في الهواء أو حيث شاء الله تعالى وإن لم يكن لها حشر

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r8.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r8.claim: Al-Suyuti says Jews prompted the polytheists to ask about the spirit, the Cave companions, and Dhu al-Qarnayn; the spirit's answer ends the previous surah and the other two answers occur here, while the spirit was separated because its reality was not explained.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r8.anchor: عن ثلاثة أشياء عن الروح وعن قصة أصحاب الكهف وعن قصة ذي القرنين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r9.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r9.claim: Al-Suyuti offers another link: both the Night Journey and spirit exceed ordinary rational comprehension, or the Journey ascends from the higher realm while the spirit descends from it; he quotes Ibn Sina's poem about the spirit's descent.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r9.anchor: وقيل : إنما ذكر هناك لما أن الإسراء متضمن العروج إلى المحل الأرفع والروح متصفة بالهبوط من ذلك المحل

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r10.speaker: جلال السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r10.claim: Because Jews heard that human knowledge is little, this surah's story of Moses and Khidr demonstrates God's immeasurable knowledge and supports the preceding judgment; a report says the Jews claimed the Torah contained all knowledge before the sea-as-ink verse answered them.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r10.anchor: استظهر على ذلك بقصة موسى نبي بني إسرائيل مع الخضر عليهما السلام التي كان سبب ذكر العلم والأعلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r9.speaker: عبد الله عن النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r9.claim: Ibn Masud recounts that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he walked in a Medina field; after revelation he recited the answer in the verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: بينا أنا أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث (2) المدينة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r10.speaker: الأعمش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r10.claim: Al-Aʿmash says the wording is as it appears in their recitation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts Quraysh consulting Jews, who proposed questions about the youths of the Cave, a traveler reaching east and west, and the spirit as a test of prophethood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r11.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: إن قريشا قد اجتمعوا وقالوا: إن محمدا نشأ فينا بالأمانة والصدق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r12.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r12.claim: The revelation delay lasted twelve nights according to Mujahid, fifteen days according to another report, and forty days according to Ikrima; the Prophet was distressed, having promised an answer without saying “if God wills.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r12.anchor: فلبث الوحي -قال مجاهد: اثني عشرة ليلة وقيل: خمسة عشر يوما وقال عكرمة: أربعين يوما-وأهل مكة يقولون: وعدنا محمد غدا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r13.claim: The delayed revelation included the reminder not to promise a future action unless God wills, the account of the Cave companions, the story of Dhu al-Qarnayn, and the answer about the spirit.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p124/r13.anchor: نزل جبريل بقوله: "ولا تقولن لشيء إني فاعل ذلك غدا إلا أن يشاء الله" ونزل في قصة الفتية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r1.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r1.claim: One interpretation says the spirit is part of God's knowledge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r2.claim: Human knowledge is little compared with God's knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r2.anchor: {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} أي: في جنب علم الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r3.claim: The address about little knowledge may be directed to the Prophet, or to the Jews who claimed that the Torah gave them extensive knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r3.anchor: وقيل: خطاب لليهود لأنهم كانوا يقولون أوتينا التوراة وفيها العلم الكثير.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r4.claim: Another view says the Prophet knew the spirit's meaning but concealed it, with his silence serving as evidence of prophethood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r4.anchor: وقيل: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعلم معنى الروح ولكن لم يخبر به أحدا لأن ترك إخباره به كان علما لنبوته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r5.claim: The first view is sounder because God reserved knowledge of the spirit to Himself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p126/r5.anchor: والأول أصح لأن الله عز وجل استأثر بعلمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r1.claim: The spirit is what gives the human body life and governs it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r1.anchor: الذي يحيا به بدن الإنسان ويدبره

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r2.claim: 'From my Lord's command' may mean a created thing brought into existence by 'Be' without material or derivation from bodily organs, or simply something produced by God's command; the question may concern whether it is eternal or created.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r2.anchor: من الإبداعيات الكائنة ب { كن } من غير مادة وتولد من أصل كأعضاء جسده، أو وجد بأمره

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r3.claim: Another view says the spirit's nature is among what God has kept to Himself.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r4.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r4.claim: Other views identify the spirit as Gabriel, a creation greater than an angel, or the Qur'an; on the last view, God's command means His revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r4.anchor: وقيل الروح جبريل وقيل خلق أعظم من الملك وقيل القرآن، ومن أمر ربي معناه من وحيه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r5.claim: Human knowledge is acquired through the senses; theoretical reasoning builds on necessary knowledge drawn from particular perceptions, so loss of a sense entails loss of some knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r5.anchor: تستفيدونه بتوسط حواسكم، فإن اكتساب العقل للمعارف النظرية. إنما هو من الضروريات المستفادة من إحساس الجزئيات، ولذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r6.claim: Most things and their intrinsic conditions elude sense; the spirit can therefore be known only by distinguishing accidents, which explains this limited answer, as Moses answered 'what is the Lord of the worlds?' with some attributes.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r6.anchor: ولعل أكثر الأشياء لا يدركه الحس ولا شيئا من أحواله المعروفة لذاته، وهو إشارة إلى أن الروح مما لا يمكن معرفة ذاته

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r7.claim: A report says Jews told Quraysh to ask about the Cave people, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the spirit, arguing that complete answers or silence would disprove prophethood; the Prophet answered two matters but left the spirit ambiguous, as it also is in the Torah.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r7.anchor: لما روي: أن اليهود قالوا لقريش سلوه عن أصحاب الكهف وعن ذي القرنين وعن الروح، فإن أجاب عنها أو سكت فليس بنبي،

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r8.claim: A report says the audience asked if the warning addressed only them; the Prophet said it addressed them all, and they contrasted this with the praise of wisdom in 2:269, prompting 31:27. Their objection reflected no misunderstanding: human wisdom gives the good and truth within human capacity for worldly and afterlife life, little beside God's endless knowledge yet enough for both lives.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:85/r8.anchor: روي: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لما قال لهم ذلك قالوا: أنحن مختصون بهذا الخطاب؟ فقال: بل نحن وأنتم، فقالوا: ما أعجب شأنك ساعة تقول

QASHANI:17:85-87/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:85-87/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:85-87/r1.claim: The spirit belongs to the divine command, the realm of immaterial essences, beyond bodily people's sensory categories of shape, color, direction, and place; the veiled cannot grasp it.
QASHANI:17:85-87/r1.anchor: الذوات المجردة عن الهيولى والجواهر المقدسة عن الشكل واللون والجهة والأين

QASHANI:17:85-87/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:85-87/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:85-87/r2.claim: The little knowledge people receive is sensory knowledge, insignificant beside God's knowledge and that of those firmly rooted in knowledge.
QASHANI:17:85-87/r2.anchor: هو علم المحسوسات وذلك شيء نزر حقير بالنسبة إلى علم الله تعالى والراسخين في العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r5.claim: The question about the spirit is posed as a test and asks what it is, whether bodily or not, whether caused by bodily mixtures, and whether eternal or created.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p419/r5.anchor: ماهي ؟ هل هي جسم أم لا ؟ وهل هي متولدة من امتزاج الطبائع

BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r1.claim: The spirit belongs to God’s direct command: creation through stages is called khalq, while bringing something from nonbeing without mediation is called amr; the spirit is created but not developed through causes.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r1.anchor: إن الخلق قسمان : ما كان بتسبيب وتنمية وتطوير

BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r2.speaker: أهل السنة
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r2.claim: The preferred Sunni view is that the spirit is a subtle created body flowing through the body like rosewater through a rose.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r2.anchor: وهي جسم لطيف سار في البدن كماء الورد في الورد على الصحيح عند أهل السنة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r3.speaker: السلف
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r3.claim: The early generations refrained from probing the spirit out of proper etiquette, seeing silence as more appropriate than further speculation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r3.anchor: وأمسك السلف عن الإمعان في الكلام على الروح أدبا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r4.claim: The questioners neglect the useful spiritual Qur’an for an obscure physical spirit, whose many questions admit no proof; ignorance of a thing’s precise nature does not mean it does not exist.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r4.anchor: ولا يلزم من عدم العلم بحقيقته المخصوصة نفيه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r5.claim: The changing spirit’s progress from ignorance to knowledge proves it is created; human knowledge is little relative to God’s, including among scriptural scholars.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r5.anchor: فإنه يكون في المبدإ جاهلا ثم يحدث له العلم شيئا بعد شيء , وكل متغير حادث

BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r6.speaker: author
