BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r6.claim: The question wastes effort on a difficult matter with no benefit while ignoring clear religious and worldly guidance whose neglect causes ruin.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r6.anchor: أن تسألوا عما لا يضركم الجهل به , ويتوقف إثباته على أمور دقيقة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r7.claim: In an authentic report, Ibn Masud says Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he walked with him in Medina; revelation came and he recited this verse.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p420/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه أنه كان يمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم في المدينة , فسأله اليهود عن الروح

BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that before the Hijra Quraysh asked Jews how to test the Prophet; they suggested questions about the spirit, the Companions of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r1.anchor: أن قريشا أرسلت إلى اليهود قبل الهجرة تسألهم عن النبي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r2.claim: In this report the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying “if God wills”; revelation was delayed fifteen nights, with other reports saying forty or twelve, causing him grief amid Meccan rumors.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r2.anchor: فمكث فيما يذكرون خمس عشرة ليلة , لا يحدث الله إليه في ذلك وحيا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r3.claim: A report in Musnad Abi Yaʿla likewise says Quraysh asked Jews for a test and then asked the Prophet about the spirit.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r3.anchor: وفي مسند أبي يعلى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : قالت قريش ليهود : أعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r4.claim: The apparently conflicting accounts are reconciled by taking the first as the occasion of revelation and later questioning as a repeated revelation confirming the same sufficient answer.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r4.anchor: فإنه محمول على أنه نزل للسبب الأول , فلما سئل عنه النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم ثانيا لم يجب فيه بالجواب الأول

BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r5.claim: The delayed answer proves the Qur’an is from God: the Prophet could not compose a reply himself despite the serious damage the delay did to his reputation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r5.anchor: وفي تأخير الجواب في هذا الأمر برهان قاطع لقريش وكل من له أدنى لب على صدق النبي صلى الله عليه وعلى آله وسلم في أن هذا القرآن من عند الله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r6.claim: The spirit belongs to the hidden realm of command, so its question is placed in al-Isra, linked to the hidden mystery of the ascent, and separated from worldly questions about the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p421/r6.anchor: ولذلك فصلت عن السؤالين الآخرين , لأنهما من عالم الملك , وسيأتي بقية الكلام على هذا في سورة الكهف

DURR-FULL:v5p330/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r4.claim: Mujahid says the questioners about the Spirit were Jews.
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} قال: يهود يسألونه

DURR-FULL:v5p330/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r5.claim: Ibn Masud recounts Jews asking about the Spirit while the Prophet walked in a ruined part of Medina; revelation supplied the answer.
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في خرب المدينة وهو متكئ على عسيب

DURR-FULL:v5p330/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Quraysh asked Jews for a question to pose; they chose the Spirit, then argued the Torah gave much knowledge, prompting the link to 18:109.
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: قالت قريش لليهود: أعطونا شيئا نسأل هذا الرجل

DURR-FULL:v5p330/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r7.claim: In an account through al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, Jews ask what the Spirit is and how it is punished; Gabriel tells the Prophet to answer it is from God's command, and the Jews call Gabriel their enemy, linked to 2:97.
DURR-FULL:v5p330/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما إن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أخبرنا ما الروح وكيف تعذب الروح

DURR-FULL:v5p331/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r1.claim: The continuation of Ibn Abbas's report says the Jews called Gabriel their enemy after the answer and connects their claim to 2:97.
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r1.anchor: قالوا: والله ما قاله لك إلا عدو لنا فأنزل الله تعالى (قل من كان عدوا لجبريل

DURR-FULL:v5p331/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r2.claim: Ali describes the Spirit as an angel with seventy thousand faces, each with seventy thousand tongues and languages, each glorifying God and generating an angel that flies with the angels until Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} قال: هو ملك من الملائكة له سبعون

DURR-FULL:v5p331/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, describes one angel with ten thousand wings, a span from east to west, and a thousand faces, glorifying God until Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} قال: هو ملك واحد له عشرة آلاف جناح

DURR-FULL:v5p331/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Spirit is a command and creation of God, shaped like humans and accompanying every angel descending from heaven; he cites 78:38.
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: الروح أمر من أمر الله وخلق من خلق الله وصورهم على صور بني آدم

DURR-FULL:v5p331/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas counsels not to pursue knowledge of the Spirit beyond God's wording and the statement that human knowledge is little.
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r5.anchor: عن عكرمة رضي الله عنه قال: سئل ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي}

DURR-FULL:v5p331/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r6.claim: Abd Allah ibn Burayda says the Prophet died without knowing the Spirit.
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بريدة رضي الله عنه قال: لقد قبض النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يعلم الروح

DURR-FULL:v5p331/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r7.speaker: يزيد بن زياد
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r7.claim: Yazid ibn Ziyad reports disagreement over whether the little knowledge refers only to the People of the Book or also to Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v5p331/r7.anchor: عن يزيد بن زياد أنه بلغه أن رجلين اختلفا في هذه الآية {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا}

DURR-FULL:v5p332/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r1.claim: Ibn Masud resolves the reported disagreement by saying the verse means the People of the Book: no knowledge is absent from al-Baqara.
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r1.anchor: فانطلق أحدهما إلى ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه فسأله فقال: ألست تقرأ سورة البقرة

DURR-FULL:v5p332/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the Spirit as an angel.
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} قال: {الروح} ملك

DURR-FULL:v5p332/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r3.claim: A report attributed by Ibn Asakir to a narrator said possibly to have been a Companion recounts Jews asking the Prophet about the Spirit in a Medina street, after which he recited the verse.
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r3.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن عبد الله بن أم الحكم الثقفي رضي الله عنه قال: بينما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض سكك المدينة

DURR-FULL:v5p332/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r4.claim: Mujahid gives a view that the Spirit is a created being among angels, unseen by them just as angels are unseen by humans.
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: {الروح} خلق مع الملائكة لا يراهم الملائكة كما لا ترون أنتم الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v5p332/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r5.claim: Mujahid also reports a view that the Spirit is a matter whose knowledge God kept to Himself and disclosed to no creature.
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه قال: {الروح} خلق مع الملائكة لا يراهم الملائكة كما لا ترون أنتم الملائكة

DURR-FULL:v5p332/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r6.speaker: سلمان
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r6.claim: Salman gives a cosmological hierarchy: humans are one part of ten among jinn, jinn one among angels, angels one among the Spirit, and the Spirit one among the cherubim.
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r6.anchor: عن سلمان رضي الله عنه قال: الإنس والجن عشرة أجزاء: فالانس جزء والجن تسعة أجزاء

DURR-FULL:v5p332/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r7.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r7.claim: Ata ibn Yasar says the knowledge-limitation verse came down in Mecca; in Medina Jews asked whether it meant them or Muhammad, and he said everyone, while Torah knowledge is little relative to God's and benefits those acting on it.
DURR-FULL:v5p332/r7.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار قال: نزلت بمكة {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} فلما هاجر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v5p333/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r1.claim: The continuation of Ata ibn Yasar's report compares human knowledge with God's inexhaustible words, citing 31:27–28.
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله (ولو أن ما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

DURR-FULL:v5p333/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r2.claim: The report glosses the little knowledge as applying to Muhammad and all people.
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r2.anchor: عن ابن جرير في قوله: {وما أوتيتم من العلم} قال: يا محمد والناس أجمعون

DURR-FULL:v5p333/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r3.claim: Qatada says the people meant by the little knowledge are the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v5p333/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} يعني اليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r1.claim: The surrounding pronouns point to Quraysh as the questioners; a Tirmidhi report from Ibn Abbas says they asked Jews for a question, were told to ask about the spirit, and this verse was revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r1.anchor: وقد روى الترمذي عن ابن عباس قال : قالت قريش ليهود أعطونا شيئا نسأل هذا الرجل عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r2.claim: On Ibn Abbas’s account they asked about the spirit alone and the verse was revealed for that question, so its placement among other material poses no problem; its timing may reflect a separate revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r2.anchor: وظاهر هذا أنهم سألوه عن الروح خاصة وأن الآية نزلت بسبب سؤالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r3.claim: Mecca and Yathrib had extensive marriage, trade, and personal ties; people from each town lodged with local friends, as with Umayya ibn Khalaf and Saʿd ibn Muʿadh.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r3.anchor: وكان لكل يثربي صاحب بمكة ينزل عنده إذا قدم الآخر بلده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Quraysh sent al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayṭ to Jewish scholars, who proposed questions about the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the spirit; the first two were answered in al-Kahf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r4.anchor: روى ابن إسحاق أن قريشا بعثوا النضر بن الحارث ، وعقبة بن أبي معيط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r5.claim: The three-question account raises a chronology problem because the spirit answer appears here in al-Isra, revealed before al-Kahf; perhaps the spirit was asked separately first, or this verse was inserted into the surah later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r5.anchor: ويدفع الإشكال أنه يجوز أن يكون السؤال عن الروح وقع منفردا أول مرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r6.claim: The majority hold that all these passages were revealed in Mecca; al-Tabari transmits from ʿAta ibn Yasar that the statement about receiving little knowledge was revealed there.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r6.anchor: والجمهور على أن الجميع نزل بمكة ، قال الطبري عن عطاء بن يسار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r7.claim: The narrator says this account makes the insertion’s place depend on the verse having been revealed between the surrounding passages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p194/r7.anchor: وبذلك يكون موقع هذه الآية بين الآيات التي قبلها والتي بعدها مسببا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit in Medina; he paused until revelation came, then recited this verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r1.anchor: وأما ما روي في ( صحيح البخاري ) عن ابن مسعود أنه قال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r2.claim: He reconciles Ibn Masud’s Medina report with Ibn Abbas’s Quraysh report by proposing that the question first came from Quraysh and later from Jews; the Prophet expected the Jews to understand better, but the same answer was repeated or ordered again.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r2.anchor: فالجمع بينه وبين حديث ابن عباس المتقدم : أن اليهود لما سألوا النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r3.claim: He prefers that historical accounts conflated matters: Quraysh drew questions from both Jews and Christians, while the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn accounts had Christian associations, leaving the spirit question from Jews.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r3.anchor: والذي يترجح عندي : أن فيما ذكره أهل السير تخليطا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r4.claim: Questioning may recur in different settings, as people with limited knowledge repeat their few questions at each gathering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r4.anchor: على أنه يجوز أن يتكرر السؤال في مناسبات وذلك شأن الذين معارفهم محدودة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r5.claim: The question seeks the nature of what Arabic calls the spirit, whose general presence is intuitively known.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r5.anchor: وسؤالهم عن الروح معناه أنهم سألوا عن بيان ماهية ما يعبر عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r6.claim: One sense of spirit is the hidden entity diffused through the human body, inferred from perception and thought, which enters the fetus after 120 days; it is also called the soul.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r6.anchor: والروح : يطلق على الموجود الخفي المنتشر في سائر الجسد الإنساني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r7.claim: This spirit is the one mentioned in the account of God breathing His spirit into the human, and the same entity may be called النفس.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p195/r7.anchor: وهذا الإطلاق هو الذي في قوله تعالى : { فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r1.claim: On one analysis من is partitive and أمر means divine command or affair, as in the description of revelation as a spirit from God’s command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r1.anchor: و ( من ) للتبعيض ، فيكون هذا الإطلاق كقوله : { وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r2.claim: If أمر is the creative command, من can mark origin: the spirit proceeds from God’s act of creation, as in His command “Be.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r2.anchor: وتكون ( من ) ابتدائية كما في قوله : إنما قولنا لشيء إذا أردناه أن نقول له كن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r3.claim: Alternatively, أمر is a verbal noun used for its object and من is partitive; روح then means Gabriel, one of God’s creatures commanded to convey revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r3.anchor: أو يراد بالمصدر معنى المفعول مثل الخلق و ( من ) تبعيضية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r4.claim: Ibn al-Arabi transmits from Ibn Wahb that Malik said no answer came to the Prophet on this question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r4.anchor: وروى ابن العربي في الأحكام عن ابن وهب عن مالك أنه قال : لم يأته في ذلك جواب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r5.claim: The phrase is not a direct account of the spirit’s nature but redirects the inquiry and tells the questioners that this knowledge was withheld; all the possibilities are intended as a comprehensive, genus-level definition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r5.anchor: أي أن قوله : قل الروح من أمر ربي } ليس جوابا ببيان ما سألوا عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r6.claim: The statement about little knowledge may address Quraysh or their Jewish informants, serve as a general concluding comment, or address Muslims; “little” is relative to all knowable facts and God’s knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r6.anchor: يجوز أن تكون مما أمر الله رسوله أن يقوله للسائلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r7.speaker: اليهود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r7.claim: A Tirmidhi report says the Jews claimed they possessed much knowledge through the Torah; the verse in the Cave chapter was then revealed about the inexhaustibility of God’s words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r7.anchor: وفي ( جامع الترمذي ) قالوا ( أي اليهود ) : ( أوتينا علما كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r8.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r8.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Ata that the little-knowledge verse was Meccan; when Jewish scholars later challenged its scope, the Prophet answered that it addressed both them and his own people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r8.anchor: وأوضح من هذا ما رواه الطبري عن عطاء بن يسار قال : نزلت بمكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r9.claim: The report continues that the Prophet said Torah knowledge is little relative to God’s knowledge, though acting on what they received could benefit them; a verse in Luqman was then revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p198/r9.anchor: هي في علم الله قليل ، وقد آتاكم ما إن عملتم به انتفعتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p434/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p434/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p434/r2.claim: Muqatil is cited in connection with the verse about those given knowledge before it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p434/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل وقوله عز وجل إن الذين أوتوا العلم من قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud’s Medina account says Jews asked about the spirit because their Torah reserved its knowledge to God; some warned against asking lest the answer displease them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r1.anchor: وروى عبد الله بن مسعود، أنه كان مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فمر على حرث بالمدينة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r2.claim: The Prophet paused leaning on a palm stalk, then recited the verse; Ibn Masʿud thought revelation had come.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r2.anchor: قال فسألوه فوقف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم متوكئا على عسيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r3.claim: Another account makes the verse Meccan: Quraysh sent al-Nadr and ʿUqba to consult Jews, who suggested three test questions including the spirit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r3.anchor: وقيل الآية مكية والضمير لقريش، وذلك أنهم قالوا: نسأل عن محمد أهل الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r4.claim: In that account the Prophet promised a reply next day without saying if God wills; revelation paused fifteen days as correction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r4.anchor: فيروى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لهم «غدا أخبركم به»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r5.claim: The majority identify the spirit as the life-giving spirit in living beings, a difficult matter with no explanation; the author calls this correct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r5.anchor: فقالت فرقة هي الجمهور: وقع السؤال عن الروح التي في الأشخاص الحيوانية ما هي؟

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r6.claim: Qatada identifies the spirit as Gabriel and says Ibn Abbas concealed the view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: الروح المسئول عنه جبريل، قال وكان ابن عباس يكتمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r7.claim: Other views identify the spirit as Jesus, an angel described in an elaborate report attributed to Ali, or the Qurʾān; the author doubts the report from Ali.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p481#2/r7.anchor: وقالت فرقة عيسى ابن مريم، وقال علي بن أبي طالب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r1.claim: Min amr rabbī may mean the spirit is a divine matter reserved to God or that it came to be by His command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r1.anchor: وقوله من أمر ربي يحتمل تأويلين: أحدهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r2.claim: A report attributed to ʿAli describes an angel with immense numbers of faces, tongues, and languages; Ibn ʿAṭiyya doubts that it truly comes from ʿAli.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r2.anchor: ذكره الطبري، وما أظن هذا القول يصح عن علي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r3.claim: One group identifies the spirit as the Qurʾān; the author says the human-spirit explanation is clearest and most correct.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة الروح القرآن، وهذه كلها أقوال مفسرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r4.claim: The author prefers the first, human-spirit interpretation among the explanations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482/r4.anchor: وهذه كلها أقوال مفسرة، والأول أظهرها وأصوبها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud and al-Aʿmash read wa-mā ūtū in third person; Ibn Masʿud also reports it from the Prophet, unlike the majority reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود والأعمش «وما أوتوا» ، ورواها ابن مسعود عن النبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r3.claim: Al-Tabari’s heading takes the address as questioners and cites Qatada that they were Jews.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r3.anchor: فقالت فرقة: السائلون فقط، ترجم الطبري بذلك ثم أدخل تحت الترجمة عن قتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r4.claim: Others take the address as Jews collectively, matching Ibn Masʿud’s reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r4.anchor: وقال قوم: المراد اليهود بجملتهم، وعلى هذا هي قراءة ابن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r5.claim: The author prefers that all people are addressed: the command to say the spirit is from God’s command addresses the whole world.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة: العالم كله، وهذا هو الصحيح لأن قول الله له قل الروح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r6.claim: The address may include the Prophet and all people, whose knowledge is little compared with God’s.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أيضا أن تكون مخاطبة من الله للنبي ولجميع الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r7.speaker: الخضر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r7.claim: Al-Khidr compares created knowledge relative to God’s to a bird’s sip from the sea; Ibn ʿAṭiyya considers an alternate reading but calls it questionable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r7.anchor: كما قال الخضر عليه السلام لموسى عليه السلام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r8.claim: When Jews asked whether you meant them or the Prophet’s people, he replied no, indicating all people; al-Tabari relates it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r8.anchor: وقد نص رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله في بعض الأحاديث «كلا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r9.claim: The author says this answered Jews who claimed the Torah gave great wisdom by comparing human learning to God’s knowledge.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r9.anchor: وقد قالت اليهود لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، كيف لم نؤت من العلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r10.claim: The point is linked to 31:27, where trees as pens would not exhaust God’s words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p482#2/r10.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى نزلت ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r1.claim: The spirit is a ray of reality whose effects vary among bodies.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : الروح شعاع الحقيقة يختلف آثارها في الأجساد

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r2.claim: The spirit is worship, while the Real alone sustains things.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : الروح عبادة ، والقائم بالأشياء هو الحق

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r3.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r3.claim: The spirits find bliss in divine disclosure and suffer in concealment.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r3.anchor: وقيل : إن الأرواح نعيمها في التجلي وعذابها في الاستتار

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r4.claim: The spirit is a subtle reality seen from God toward known places, expressible only as existence brought into being by another.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : الروح لطيفة يرى من الله عز وجل إلى أماكن معروفة لا يعبر عنه بأكثر من وجود بإيجاد غيره

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r5.claim: The spirit passes through love, fear, hope, and truthfulness, but the greatest spirits' gnosis is God's knowledge of them; their knowledge and will are likewise grounded in His knowing and willing them.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : الروح يمر بشيء من الأحوال من محبة وخوف ، ورجاء ، وصدق ، والمعرفة أنفت هذه المعاني كلها

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r6.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r6.claim: The gentleness of divine favors makes spirits forget, while direct contact of spirits makes the favors manifest.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r6.anchor: قيل : مباسطة الألطاف تنسي الأرواح ، ومباشرة الأرواح تظهر عليها الألطاف

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r7.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r7.claim: The spirit is joined to divine knowledge by its delicacy and is drawn toward that knowledge, where it moves and surges through God's regard.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r7.anchor: قيل في قوله : ﴿ قل الروح من أمر ربي ﴾ قال : قارن العلم بالروح لرقة لطافته بحملها

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r8.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r8.claim: The spirit did not leave the created cosmos, which would debase it; it came from between divine beauty and holiness and was enveloped in beauty, peace, and speech.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r8.anchor: وقيل : الروح لم تخرج من الكون لأنها لو خرجت من الكون لكان عليها الذل

SULAMI:v1p395#4/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r9.speaker: أبو سعيد الحداد
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r9.claim: The spirit is created, affirmed God's lordship at the primordial covenant, gives the body life, establishes intellect, and makes accountability possible.
SULAMI:v1p395#4/r9.anchor: وسئل أبو سعيد الحداد عن الروح مخلوقة هي ، قال : نعم فلولا ذلك لما أقرت بالربوبية حين قال : ' بلى '

SULAMI:v1p396/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p396/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p396/r1.claim: The spirit is created before bodies, uniquely honored in God's hand, and is the subtlest, purest, brightest creature; it perceives the unseen and enables unveiling, while its concealment from the soul makes the limbs lapse in proper conduct.
SULAMI:v1p396/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ قل الروح من أمر ربي ﴾ إن الله ستر الروح على جميع خلقه

SULAMI:v1p396/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p396/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p396/r2.claim: God created and seized spirits before bodies; for spirits, what was hidden became visible and this world and the next are alike.
SULAMI:v1p396/r2.anchor: وسئل الواسطي رحمه الله عن الأرواح أين كان مكانها حين أظهرها ؟ قال : إن الأرواح خلقها وقبضها قبل الأجساد

SULAMI:v1p396/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p396/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p396/r3.claim: Muhammad was the wisest of creatures because his spirit was created first, giving him established companionship; the report that he was a prophet while Adam was between spirit and body means Adam was neither yet a spirit nor a body.
SULAMI:v1p396/r3.anchor: وسئل لأي علة كان محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أحكم الخلق ؟ قال : لأنه خلق روحه أولا

SULAMI:v1p396/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p396/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p396/r4.claim: Spirits do not desire or regard created things as great, since witnessing the Real makes them reject every incoming hidden reality.
SULAMI:v1p396/r4.anchor: وقيل : معرفة الأشباح عقوله بها زمن عظيم ما ورد عليها والأرواح لا تهواها شيء ولا يستعظم كونا

SULAMI:v1p396/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p396/r5.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p396/r5.claim: Spirits are freed from the cosmos and were greeted directly by God, remaining safe in eternity and the afterlife; this earns them the name of peace.
SULAMI:v1p396/r5.anchor: وقيل : الأرواح معتقة من رق الكون أظهر فيها من خفايا المخبات المصونات والمكونات بأعجب أعجوبة

SULAMI:v1p396/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p396/r6.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p396/r6.claim: Spirits illuminate and adorn bodies through the bliss of their meeting and proper conduct; when the spirit is veiled from the body, the limbs behave improperly.
SULAMI:v1p396/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : نور بالأرواح الأجساد ورفق بها وزينها بنعيم مشاهدة الأرواح وملاقاتها

SULAMI:v1p397/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p397/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد القرشي
SULAMI:v1p397/r1.claim: There are two spirits: the spirit of death, whose departure makes the living body dead, and the spirit of life, which supplies breathing and powers eating and drinking.
SULAMI:v1p397/r1.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد القرشي : الروح روحان : روح الممات ، وروح الحياة

SULAMI:v1p397/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p397/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p397/r2.claim: Prophets' spirits feed on subtle divine address and disdain creaturely boasts and devotional adornment; the spirits of the truthful and righteous grow in light through God's regard, while ordinary spirits feed on food and drink.
SULAMI:v1p397/r2.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : الأرواح في ثلاثة أشياء : أرواح الأجلة الأنبياء غذاها بلطائف خطابها

SULAMI:v1p397/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p397/r3.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p397/r3.claim: The spirit is worship, and the Real alone sustains all things; things stand through His care and preservation.
SULAMI:v1p397/r3.anchor: وقال بعض البغداديين : الروح عبادة ، والقائم بالأشياء الحق لا غير

SULAMI:v1p397/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p397/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p397/r4.claim: An anonymous poem depicts the spirit rising beyond the constellations like stars and says divine conversation with inner secrets overwhelms bodily impurities.
SULAMI:v1p397/r4.anchor: وأنشد بعضهم : ( تراعى الروح مطلعها فتعلو … عن الأبراج تسري كالنجوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r1.claim: A group of Jews prompted a question about the spirit; some cautioned against asking, then they asked the Prophet, who fell silent and received this verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r1.anchor: ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم مر بناس من اليهود فقالوا سلوه عن الروح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r2.claim: Jews told Quraysh to ask about three matters—lost youths, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the spirit—as a test of prophethood; after answers to the first two and silence on the spirit, this verse came.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r2.anchor: أن اليهود قالت لقريش سلوا محمدا عن ثلاث فان اخبركم عن اثنتين وامسك عن الثالثة فهو نبي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r3.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r3.claim: One view says the spirit is what gives life to the body.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r3.anchor: أحدها انه الروح الذي يحيا به البدن روى هذا المعنى العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r4.claim: There is no proof for theories about whether spirit and soul are one or two things; people took such theories from medicine and philosophers, while the early Muslims withheld judgment because the spirit belongs to God’s command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r4.anchor: وقد اختلف الناس في ماهية الروح ثم اختلفوا هل الروح النفس أم هما شيئان فلا يحتاج إلى ذكر اختلافهم لأنه لا برهان على شيء من ذلك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r5.speaker: علي وابن عباس ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r5.claim: Another view says the spirit is a huge angel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r5.anchor: والثاني أن المراد بهذا الروح ملك من الملائكة على خلقه هائلة روي عن علي عليه السلام وابن عباس ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r6.claim: Another view says the spirit is a creature God made in human form.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r6.anchor: والثالث ان الروح خلق من خلق الله عز وجل صورهم على صور بني آدم رواه مجاهد عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r7.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r7.claim: Another view identifies the spirit as Gabriel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r7.anchor: والرابع أنه جبريل عليه السلام قاله الحسن وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r8.claim: Another view identifies the spirit as the Quran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r8.anchor: والخامس أنه القرآن روي عن الحسن ايضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r9.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r9.claim: Another view identifies the spirit as Jesus son of Mary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r9.anchor: والسادس أنه عيسى بن مريم حكاه الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r10.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r10.claim: Al-Dimashqī thinks the intended spirit is the one that gives life to Adam’s child; interpreters likely transferred glosses from other Quranic contexts where “spirit” occurs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r10.anchor: قد ذكر الله تعالى الروح في مواضع من القرآن فغالب ظني أن الناقلين نقلوا تفسيره من موضعه إلى موضع لا يليق به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r11.claim: The spirit is “from my Lord’s command,” meaning it belongs to God’s work, whose reality He has withheld from human knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p81#2/r11.anchor: وقوله ﴿ من أمر ربي ﴾ أي من عمله الذي منع إن يعرفه أحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r1.claim: Most say the audience told that their knowledge is little is the Jews.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r2.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r2.claim: Another view takes the audience as all people, whose knowledge is little relative to God’s knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r2.anchor: والثاني أنهم جميع الخلق علمهم قليل بالإضافة إلى علم الله عز وجل ذكره الماوردي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r3.claim: There is no contradiction with 2:269: whatever knowledge people receive, even if substantial, is little beside God’s knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p82/r3.anchor: أن ما أوتيه الناس من العلم وان كان كثيرا فهو بالإضافة إلى علم الله قليل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews in Medina asked Muhammad about the spirit; revelation then instructed him to say that it belongs to God's command and human knowledge is slight.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله -هو ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه -قال: كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r2.claim: The report's apparent Medina setting would make the verse Medinan despite the Meccan surah; Ibn Kathir suggests it may have been revealed again there or that an earlier verse was given as the answer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r2.anchor: وهذا السياق يقتضي (8) فيما يظهر بادي الرأي: أن هذه الآية مدنية، وأنها إنما نزلت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews what to ask Muhammad, and the Jews proposed the spirit; after his answer they boasted of the Torah, and God revealed that even the seas cannot exhaust his words.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قالت قريش ليهود: أعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه هذا الرجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir takes the Quraysh-to-Jews report as evidence for a Meccan revelation, despite the Medina setting in Ibn Masud's report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p113#3/r4.anchor: ومما يدل على نزول هذه الآية بمكة ما قال الإمام أحمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r1.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r1.claim: Ikrima reports that the People of the Book objected that they possessed the Torah and wisdom; the response was that knowledge saving them from Hell is much yet little relative to God's knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة قال: سأل أهل الكتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r2.speaker: عطاء بن يسار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r2.claim: Ata ibn Yasar reports that the verse was revealed in Mecca; after migration Jewish scholars ask whether it means them or Muhammad's people, and he replies that it includes them all and their knowledge is little before God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r2.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار قال: نزلت بمكة: {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r3.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's view that the spirit means human souls; Jews asked how a soul from God could be punished, and Gabriel brought the answer, provoking their claim that he was their enemy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p114/r3.anchor: قال العوفي، عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} الآية، وذلك أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r1.claim: Qatada says the spirit here is Gabriel and that Ibn Abbas used to conceal this interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r1.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالروح هاهنا: جبريل. قاله قتادة، قال: وكان ابن عباس يكتمه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r2.claim: A report through Ali ibn Talha attributes to Ibn Abbas the view that the spirit is an angel; another report describes an immense angel able to swallow the heavens and earth in one bite, which Ibn Kathir grades strange and munkar.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r2.anchor: قال (4) علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} يقول: الروح: ملك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r3.claim: Ali is reported to describe the spirit as an angel with 70,000 faces, tongues and languages, whose glorifications each create an angel; Ibn Kathir calls the report strange and wondrous.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه، أنه قال في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} قال: هو ملك من الملائكة، له سبعون ألف وجه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r4.speaker: السهيلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r4.claim: Al-Suhayli also transmits from Ali a description of an angel with 100,000 heads, faces, mouths and tongues praising God in varied languages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r4.anchor: قال السهيلي: روي عن علي أنه قال: هو ملك، له مائة ألف رأس، لكل رأس مائة ألف وجه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r5.speaker: السهيلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r5.claim: Al-Suhayli reports a view that the spirit is a group of angels in human form.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد بذلك: طائفة من الملائكة على صور بني آدم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r6.speaker: السهيلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r6.claim: Al-Suhayli reports a group that sees angels while angels do not see them, standing to angels as angels stand to human beings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p115/r6.anchor: وقيل: طائفة يرون الملائكة ولا تراهم (1) فهم للملائكة كالملائكة لبني آدم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r1.claim: The spirit is of God's affair, meaning a matter reserved to his knowledge; people receive only a little of what God knows, and this question was not disclosed to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r1.anchor: أي: من شأنه، ومما استأثر بعلمه دونكم؛ ولهذا قال: {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r2.claim: The bird's sip from the sea illustrates that Moses, Khidr and all creatures know only an infinitesimal amount beside God's knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r2.anchor: ما علمي وعلمك وعلم الخلائق في علم الله إلا كما أخذ هذا العصفور من هذا البحر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r3.speaker: السهيلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r3.claim: Al-Suhayli says either the question was left unanswered because it was asked in obstinacy, or it was answered as an invitation to follow divine law, since reason and philosophy cannot reveal the spirit; Ibn Kathir finds the latter reasoning questionable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r3.anchor: وقيل: أجابهم، وعول السهيلي على أن المراد بقوله: {قل الروح من أمر ربي} أي: من شرعه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r4.speaker: السهيلي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r4.claim: Al-Suhayli describes the spirit as a subtle substance flowing through the body like water through a tree; joined to the body it becomes the soul, acquiring praiseworthy or blameworthy qualities, and soul and spirit are one aspectually, not wholly. Ibn Kathir calls this a good account.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116/r4.anchor: فحاصل ما يقول أن الروح أصل النفس ومادتها، والنفس مركبة منها ومن اتصالها بالبدن، فهي هي من وجه لا من كل وجه (4)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that scholars have written on the spirit's nature and rulings, and singles out Hafiz Ibn Manda's book as among the best discussions, which he had heard.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p116#2/r1.anchor: ومن أحسن من تكلم على ذلك الحافظ ابن منده، في كتاب سمعناه في: الروح (5)

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r1.claim: Ruh derives from wind; its pattern is fa'l or another derived noun with the same meaning. Abu Ali says the waw becomes ya in rih with kasra, and the plural is arwah.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r1.anchor: الروح: أصله من الريح، وبناؤه من الفعل فعل بضم الفاء

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r2.speaker: مشايخنا
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r2.claim: The author's theological teachers define the human spirit as a subtle body that enters and exits through a person's openings.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r2.anchor: روح الإنسان، وهو جسم رقيق، أي: يدخل [مخارق] الإنسان ويخرج منه، هذا هو مذهب مشايخنا

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر أحمد بن علي الإخشيد
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r3.claim: The spirit is the human being, meaning the living person.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: الروح الإنسان، وهو الحي، عن أبي بكر أحمد بن علي الإخشيد

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r4.speaker: أبو الهذيل
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Hudhayl identifies the spirit with life.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: الروح: الحياة، عن أبي الهذيل

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r5.claim: Other views make the spirit a meaning in the heart, something shared with the body, Gabriel, or the Qur'an, which gives life to religion.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: الروح في الإنسان، وهو معنى في القلب

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r8.claim: One occasion is Jews asking the Prophet what the spirit is.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r8.anchor: قيل: قالت اليهود للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: أخبرنا ما الروح؟ فنزلت الآية، عن ابن عباس.

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r9.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r9.claim: The Jews told the polytheists to test the Prophet with the spirit, since their book said an answer would disprove his prophethood; they also proposed asking about the Cave youths and Dhul-Qarnayn, and verses on all three topics followed.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: قالت اليهود للمشركين: اسألوه عن الروح فإن أجابكم عنه فليس بنبي.

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r10.claim: The Prophet is agreed to be the person questioned, but the questioners may have been Jews; al-Zajjaj says they were polytheists.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r10.anchor: ولا خلاف أن المسئول محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، واختلفوا في السائل، قيل: قوم من اليهود، عن قتادة.

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r11.claim: Some identify the spirit as Gabriel; Ibn Abbas said they asked about his attributes and how he came, and Ali reports an account of Gabriel with innumerable faces and tongues praising God.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r11.anchor: قيل: هو جبريل، عن ابن عباس، والحسن، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r12.claim: Mujahid says the spirit is a created kind of being that eats and drinks.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: خلق من خلق الله يأكلون ويشربون، عن مجاهد.

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود، وابن عباس، وجماعة، وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r13.claim: The spirit may be the animal spirit or life about which they asked; Abu Ali supports this identification.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: الروح روح الحيوان وعنه سئل، عن ابن مسعود، وابن عباس وجماعة

JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r14.speaker: الحسن، والأصم، وأبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r14.claim: Another interpretation is the Qur'an, about its form, arrangement, and who brought it.
JISHUMI:v6p4291#2/r14.anchor: وقيل: الروح: القرآن، سألوه عن كيفيته ونظمه وترتيبه ومن أتاه به

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r1.claim: If the question concerns the animal spirit, some say they asked its definition; others ask how perception differs despite one spirit, or why life needs it. Their books said inability to answer was a prophetic sign.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r1.anchor: ومن قال: السؤال وقع عن روح الحيوان اختلفوا، فقيل: السؤال وقع عن تفسير الروح

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r2.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r2.claim: The spirit may be something whose full account God knows; the Prophet declined to explain it.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r2.anchor: قيل: من الأمر الذي يعلمه ربي ولم يجبهم، عن أبي علي.

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r3.claim: If the spirit is the Qur'an, its miraculous composition belongs to God's knowledge alone.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r3.anchor: وقيل: القرآن من أمر ربي، والعلم بكيفية نظمه حتى صار معجزا يختص به القديم تعالى، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r4.claim: If the spirit is human life, it is created by God; this reading answers that it is created.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r4.anchor: وقيل: من خلق ربي أي الروح الذي يحيا به الإنسان خلق الله، عن أبي صالح.

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r5.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r5.claim: Another interpretation calls the Qur'an God's revelation.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r5.anchor: وقيل: القرآن من وحي ربي، عن الحسن.

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r6.claim: Gabriel, too, can be called a spirit created by God; each proposed referent is something no one besides God can bring about.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r6.anchor: وقيل: جبريل من خلق ربي، وجميع ذلك ما لا يقدر عليه غير الله تعالى.

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r7.claim: The limited-knowledge address may apply to everyone or specifically the Jews; their Torah is little compared with God's knowledge.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r7.anchor: وما أوتيتم أعطيتم من العلم قيل: خطاب عام للجميع، وقيل: خطاب لليهود

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r10.claim: Given the surrounding references to the Qur'an, the author prefers that the question concerned the Qur'an rather than another spirit.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r10.anchor: والصحيح أن المراد به القرآن؛ لأن ما قبل الآية وما بعدها في ذكر القرآن

JISHUMI:v6p4294/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r11.claim: The reply that it is from God's command means it is originated; something that can be taken away cannot be eternal, since the eternal cannot cease to exist.
JISHUMI:v6p4294/r11.anchor: وتدل على حدث القرآن [*]؛ لأنه من أمر الله، ولأن ما جاز أن يذهب به يكون محدثا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r1.claim: Most interpreters say the spirit is the spirit within animals; asked about its reality, the Prophet said it is God's command, meaning knowledge God reserved to Himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r1.anchor: الأكثر على أنه الروح الذي في الحيوان . سألوه عن حقيقته فأخبر أنه من أمر الله ، أي مما استأثر بعلمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r2.claim: Ibn Burayda reports that the Prophet died without knowing the spirit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r2.anchor:
وعن عبد الله بن بريدة .
( 633 ) لقد مضى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يعلم الروح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r3.claim: Other interpretations identify the spirit as a vast spiritual creation greater than an angel, Gabriel, or the Qur'an; on the Qur'an interpretation, God's command means His revelation and speech rather than human speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r3.anchor: وقيل : هو خلق عظيم روحاني أعظم من الملك . وقيل : جبريل عليه السلام . وقيل : القرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r4.claim: A report says Jews told Quraysh to ask about the Sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the spirit; Muhammad answered the stories but left the spirit's nature obscure, as it was obscure in Torah, and they regretted asking.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r4.anchor: بعثت اليهود إلى قريش أن سلوه عن أصحاب الكهف ، وعن ذي القرنين ، وعن الروح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r5.claim: The address in you were given little knowledge is general.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r6.claim: When asked whether the limited knowledge included only Jews or also the Muslims, the Prophet said it included both.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r6.anchor: فقال : بل نحن وأنتم لم نؤت من العلم إلا قليلا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r7.claim: The objection that this contradicts the verse calling wisdom great good is mistaken: greatness and smallness are relative; wisdom is abundant in itself but little beside God's knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r7.anchor: لأن القلة والكثرة تدوران مع الإضافة ، فيوصف الشيء بالقلة مضافا إلى ما فوقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r8.claim: Another interpretation addresses the Jews alone because they boasted of Torah wisdom; its knowledge is little compared with God's knowledge.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p645/r8.anchor: وقيل : هو خطاب لليهود خاصة ؛ لأنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : قد أوتينا التوراة وفيها الحكمة

FARRA:v2p129/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p129/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p129/r8.claim: The Spirit is from God’s knowledge and outside human knowledge.
FARRA:v2p129/r8.anchor: وقوله: قل الروح من أمر ربي [85] يقول: من علم ربي، ليس من علمكم.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r1.claim: The spirit is Gabriel, as in the verse describing the trustworthy Spirit descending with revelation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r1.anchor: أنه جبريل عليه السلام , قاله ابن عباس . كما قال تعالى ^ { نزل به الروح الأمين } ^

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r2.claim: The spirit is an angel with seventy thousand faces, each bearing seventy thousand tongues that glorify God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r2.anchor: ملك من الملائكة له سبعون ألف وجه , لكل وجه سبعون ألف لسان يسبح الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r3.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r3.claim: The spirit is the Quran, from God’s command and revelation, not Muhammad’s own production.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r3.anchor: أنه القرآن , قاله الحسن , كما قال تعالى ^ { وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا } ^

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r4.claim: Another interpretation identifies the spirit as Jesus: he is from God’s command, not God’s son as Christians claim or illegitimate as Jews allege.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r4.anchor: أنه عيسى ابن مريم هو من أمر الله تعالى وليس كما ادعته النصارى أنه ابن الله ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r5.claim: A fifth interpretation takes the spirit as the animating spirit of living beings, whose name derives from wind.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r5.anchor: أنه روح الحيوان , وهي مشتقة من الريح . قال قتادة سأله عنها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r6.claim: A group of Jews asked about the spirit; their scripture reportedly said that answering would show Muhammad was not a prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r6.anchor: قال قتادة سأله عنها قوم من اليهود وقيل في كتابهم أنه إن أجاب عن الروح فليس بنبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r7.claim: The unanswered question may have been left open to confirm something actually stated in the Jews’ book.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r7.anchor: أحدها : تحقيقا لشيء إن كان في كتابهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r8.claim: The questioners may have intended to make the Prophet struggle, as they did when demanding signs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r8.anchor: الثاني : أنهم قصدوا بذلك الإعنات كما قصدوا اقتراح الآيات .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r9.claim: The spirit may be knowable through reason rather than transmitted revelation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r9.anchor: الثالث : لأنه قد يتوصل إلى معرفته بالعقل دون السمع .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r10.claim: Not answering may prevent this from opening the way to irrelevant questions.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r10.anchor: الرابع : لئلا يكون ذلك ذريعة إلى سؤال ما لا يعني .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r11.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r11.claim: Some theologians say a physical description of the spirit would sound like philosophers’ discourse rather than prophetic speech.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r11.anchor: الخامس : قاله بعض المتكلمين , أنه لو أجابهم عنها ووصفها ؛ بأنها جسم رقيق تقوم معه الحياة ,

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r12.claim: On this reading, “from my Lord’s command” means God alone has power over the spirit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r12.anchor: فقال { من أمر ربي } أي هو القادر عليه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r13.claim: The question may seek to determine whether the spirit is created or eternal; the answer says it is created by God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r13.anchor: السادس : أن المقصود من سؤالهم عن الروح أن يتبين لهم أنه محدث أو قديم , فأجابهم بأنه محدث

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r14.claim: “Only a little knowledge” can mean little of all that God knows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r14.anchor: أحدهما : إلا قليلا من معلومات الله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r15.claim: Alternatively, people receive only the little knowledge required as needs arise over time.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r15.anchor: الثاني : إلا قليلا بحسب ما تدعو الحاجة إليه حالا فحالا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r16.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r16.claim: Qatada says the warning about limited knowledge addresses the Jews in particular.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r16.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم اليهود خاصة , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r17.claim: Alternatively, it addresses the Prophet and all other people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p269/r17.anchor: الثاني : النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وسائر الخلق .

MUJAHID:v1p369#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p369#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
MUJAHID:v1p369#4/r1.claim: Qatada reports that Jews challenged the Prophet with questions about the spirit, the Cave Companions, and Dhul-Qarnayn; revelation answered the spirit and recounted the latter stories, addressing the Jews as having little knowledge.
MUJAHID:v1p369#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة قال لقي اليهود النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فتعنتوه قالوا إن كان نبيا سيعلم

MUQATIL:17:85-87/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r1.claim: The question about the spirit was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and his companions; the spirit is a mighty human-shaped angel, greater than all creatures except the Throne and guardian of angels.
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r1.anchor: { ويسألونك عن الروح } ، نزلت في أبي جهل وأصحابه، { قل الروح من أمر ربي } ، وهو ملك عظيم على صورة إنسان

MUQATIL:17:85-87/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r2.speaker: اليهود
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r2.claim: The Jews said the Torah held all knowledge and accused Gabriel of being their enemy; they challenged whether the limited-knowledge statement applied to all people, including Muhammad.
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r2.anchor: أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إن في التوراة علم كل شىء، وقال الله تبارك وتعالى للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:17:85-87/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r3.claim: He said the limitation applies to everyone; the Jews challenged this against the abundant good of wisdom.
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r3.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم " بل الناس كلها عامة " ، فقالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولا أنت ولا أصحابك؟

MUQATIL:17:85-87/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r4.claim: In answer to the challenge, the verses of the earth's trees as pens and the sea as ink were revealed.
MUQATIL:17:85-87/r4.anchor: ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام...

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r1.claim: Most authorities take the spirit to mean the life-giving spirit in animals; they were asked about its reality, and the answer reserves its knowledge to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r1.anchor: الجمهور على أنه الروح الذي في الحيوان سألوه عن حقيقته فأخبر أنه من مر الله أي مما استأثر بعلمه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r2.claim: A report says the Prophet died without knowing the spirit's reality.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r2.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة لقد مضى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وما يعلم الروح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r3.claim: Earlier thinkers failed to grasp the spirit's reality despite long inquiry; this incapacity to know a nearby creature shows the greater incapacity to know its Creator.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r3.anchor: وقد عجزت الأوائل عن إدراك ما هيته بعد انفاق الأعمار الطويلة على الخوض فيه والحكمة في ذلك تعجيز العقل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r4.claim: The proposed definition of spirit as a fine airy body present in every part of an animal is rejected.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r4.anchor: ولذا رد ما قيل في حده أنه جسم دقيق هوائي في كل جزء من الحيوان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r5.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r5.claim: Another view calls it a great spiritual creation, greater than an angel.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r5.anchor: وقيل هو خلق عظيم روحانى أعظم من الملك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the spirit as Gabriel, the trustworthy spirit who brought revelation to the Prophet's heart.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هو جبريل عليه السلام نزل به الروح الأمين على قلبك

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the spirit as the Qurʾān, which gives life to hearts and is God's revelation and speech, not human speech; he cites the Qurʾān's description as a spirit from God's command.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r7.anchor: وعن الحسن القرآن دليله وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ولأن به حياة القلوب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r8.claim: Jews prompted Quraysh to ask about the Cave Companions, Dhū al-Qarnayn, and the spirit; the Prophet answered the two stories but left the spirit ambiguous as it is in the Torah, and they regretted asking.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r8.anchor: أن اليهود بعثت إلى قريش أن سلوه عن اصحاب الكهف وعن ذي القرنين وعن الروح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r9.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r9.claim: Another view says they asked whether the spirit was created; 'from my Lord's command' answers that it is created.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r9.anchor: وقيل كان السؤال عن خلق الروح يعنى أهو مخلوق أم لا وقوله من أمر ربى دليل خلق الروح

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r10.claim: The knowledge limit may address everyone: when asked whether it included the Prophet, he answered that both he and they had received little knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r10.anchor: فقد روى أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قال لهم ذلك قالوا نحن مختصون بهذا الخطاب أم انت معنا فيه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r11.claim: Alternatively it addresses the Jews alone, whose Torah knowledge is little beside God's; knowledge is relative, so their wisdom is much in itself but little compared with divine knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p298#2/r11.anchor: وقيل هو خطاب لليهود خاصة لأنهم قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أوتينا التوارة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he rested in a field; he paused without answering until revelation came with the response.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r1.anchor: في حرث وهو متكىء على عسيب إذ مر اليهود

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r2.claim: Qatada says the spirit asked about was Gabriel, and Ibn Abbas used to conceal this interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r2.anchor: هو جبريل قاله قتادة. قال: وكان ابن عباس يكتمه.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r3.claim: Other identifications say the spirit was Jesus or the Qurʾān; the latter is discussed in al-Shura.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r3.anchor: على ما يأتي بيانه في آخر الشورى.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r4.claim: A report attributed to Ali describes the spirit as an angel with 70,000 faces, each with 70,000 tongues and languages, praising God and generating an angel with every glorification.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r4.anchor: هو ملك من الملائكة له سبعون ألف وجه...

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya doubts that the elaborate angel report is authentic from Ali, though Qurtubi cites a chain for it through Ibn Abbas and another attribution to Ali.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وما أظن القول يصح عن علي رضي الله عنه.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r6.speaker: عطاء وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r6.claim: A report from Ataa via Ibn Abbas instead describes an angel with eleven thousand wings and a thousand faces, praising God until the Resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r6.anchor: وروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: الروح ملك له أحد عشر ألف جناح

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the spirit as a host of God's creatures with hands and feet who eat food; Abu Salih similarly calls them creatures like humans but not humans.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r7.anchor: وعنه: جند من جنود الله لهم أيد وأرجل يأكلون الطعام

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r8.claim: Abu Salih says the spirit is a created species resembling human beings but not human beings.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r8.anchor: وقال أبو صالح: الروح خلق كخلق بني آدم وليسوا ببني

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r9.speaker: أكثر أهل التأويل
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r9.claim: Most exegetes say the question concerns the spirit that gives the body life; rationalists understand it as asking how spirit moves through and joins the body, an unknown matter.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85/r9.anchor: وذهب أكثر أهل التأويل إلى أنهم سألوه عن الروح الذي يكون به حياة الجسد.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi prefers leaving the identity unspecified: calling spirit God's command marks its greatness while withholding detail, showing people cannot know the essence of even their own selves and are still less able to comprehend their Creator.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r1.anchor: والصحيح الإبهام لقوله: «قل الروح من أمر ربي» دليل على خلق الروح

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r2.claim: Exegetes disagree whether “you were given little knowledge” addresses only the questioners, Jews collectively, or all humankind; Qurtubi prefers all people and the majority reading “you were given.”
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r2.anchor: اختلف فيمن خوطب بذلك فقالت فرقة: السائلون فقط.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r3.claim: A reading attributed to Ibn Masʿud says “they were given” little knowledge, referring to Jews as a whole; it is also transmitted from the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا هي قراءة ابن مسعود «وما أوتوا» ورواها عن النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r4.claim: Jews objected that they possessed the Torah and wisdom, but the Prophet answered by comparison with God's knowledge and defeated them; when asked whether Jews or his community were meant, he said “No,” meaning everyone.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r4.anchor: كيف لم نؤت من العلم إلا قليلا

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r5.claim: The verse's point about limited human knowledge is linked to the image of all trees on earth becoming pens in 31:27.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r5.anchor:
وفي هذا المعنى نزلت:
ولو أنما في الأرض من شجرة أقلام

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r6.claim: Another account says Quraysh asked about the spirit after Jews suggested asking about the sleepers, Dhul-Qarnayn, and spirit; the first two stories were answered while the spirit was referred to God's knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r6.anchor: وقد قيل: إن السائلين عن الروح هم

QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by al-Mahdawi and other exegetes, says that the spirit is of God's command, known only to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:85#2/r7.anchor: ذكره المهدوي وغيره من المفسرين عن ابن عباس.

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r1.claim: The question about the spirit follows the claim that each person acts according to the pattern of the soul; the discussion therefore turns to the spirit’s nature.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r1.anchor: وجب البحث ها هنا عن ماهية الروح وحقيقته فلذلك سألوا عن الروح

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r2.claim: The most apparent interpretation is the life-giving human spirit; al-Rāzī recounts the report that Jews told Quraysh to ask about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r2.anchor: أظهرها أن المراد منه الروح الذي هو سبب الحياة ، روى أن اليهود قالوا لقريش

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r3.claim: In the report, the Prophet promised an answer the next day without saying “if God wills”; revelation then ceased for forty days before the exception in 18:23–24 was revealed.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r3.anchor: ولم يقل إن شاء / الله فانقطع عنه الوحي أربعين يوما ثم نزل الوحي بعده

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r4.claim: The same report says he later related the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn stories but left the spirit question ambiguous, prompting this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r4.anchor: ثم فسر لهم قصة أصحاب الكهف وقصة ذي القرنين وأبهم قصة الروح

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that the spirit is not greater or higher than God; since knowledge of God is possible, there is no apparent barrier to knowing the spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r5.anchor: أن الروح ليس أعظم شأنا ولا أعلى مكانا من الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r6.claim: He objects that answering stories about the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn cannot prove prophethood: before belief, Quraysh could simply disbelieve the stories; after belief, the stories add nothing, and silence about the spirit is no proof either.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r6.anchor: قصة أصحاب الكهف وقصة ذي القرنين ليست إلا حكاية من الحكايات

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r7.claim: If even junior philosophers and low-ranking speculative theologians know about the spirit, a Prophet’s professed ignorance would invite contempt and repel people.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r7.anchor: مسألة الروح يعرفها أصاغر الفلاسفة وأراذل المتكلمين

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r8.claim: The Qurʾān says God taught the Prophet the Book and what he did not know, commands him to seek more knowledge, and says all things are recorded; the Prophet prayed to see things as they are, so al-Rāzī asks how he could lack this knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r8.anchor: وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī’s preferred answer is that ruh can prompt many questions—about substance, spatiality, eternity, survival after death, or the soul’s happiness and misery—and the verse does not specify which one was asked.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r9.anchor: ليس فيه ما يدل على أنهم عن هذه المسائل سألوا

RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r10.claim: The reply that the spirit is from God’s command suits questions about its essence or whether it is originated; al-Rāzī says these are the two issues to which the answer applies.
RAZI-FULL:v21p30#2/r10.anchor: وهذا الجواب لا يليق إلا بمسألتين من المسائل التي ذكرناها

RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r1.claim: For the question about essence, al-Rāzī says the spirit is distinct from bodies and accidents: it is a simple, immaterial substance, brought into being by God’s creative “Be.”
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r1.anchor: بل هو جوهر بسيط مجرد لا يحدث إلا بمحدث

RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r2.claim: The spirit is created by God’s command and gives life to the body; ignorance of its particular reality does not negate it, since many realities are unknown.
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r2.anchor: موجود يحدث بأمر الله وتكوينه وتأثيره في إفادة الحياة لهذا الجسد

RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī illustrates with sikangabīn: people know it cuts yellow bile, though the specific reality of that property remains unknown, so ignorance does not prove nonexistence.
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r3.anchor: نعلم أن السكنجبين له خاصية تقتضي قطع الصفراء فأما إذا أردنا أن نعرف ماهية تلك الخاصية

RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r4.claim: Amr can mean an act, as in the Qurʾānic descriptions of Pharaoh’s conduct and God’s deed in 11:97 and 11:66.
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r4.anchor: لفظ الأمر قد جاء بمعنى الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r5.claim: On this reading, “the spirit is from my Lord’s act” answers whether the spirit is eternal or originated: it is originated through God’s creation and bringing it into being.
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r5.anchor: أي من فعل ربي وهذا الجواب يدل على أنهم سألوه

RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r6.claim: The spirit begins without knowledge, then gains knowledge and changes from one state to another; this change indicates origination, which al-Rāzī takes as the force of the verse’s statement that people received little knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v21p31/r6.anchor: الأرواح في مبدأ الفطرة تكون خالية عن العلوم والمعارف ثم يحصل فيها العلوم والمعارف

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r1.claim: One view identifies the spirit as the Qurʾān, which God calls a spirit in 42:52 and 16:2 because it gives life to souls and minds through knowledge of God, angels, scripture, and messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r1.anchor: أن المراد من هذا الروح هو القرآن قالوا وذلك لأن الله تعالى سمى القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r2.claim: The Qurʾān reading fits the context: 17:82 and 17:86–88 discuss the Qurʾān, and the questioners may have asked whether it was poetry or soothsaying; the answer says it is divine revelation, not human speech.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r2.anchor: فلما كان قبل هذه الآية في وصف القرآن وما بعدها كذلك وجب أيضا أن يكون المراد

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r3.claim: Another view identifies the spirit with the greatest of the heavenly angels, citing the spirit standing with the angels in 78:38.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r3.anchor: الروح المسؤول عنه في هذه الآية ملك من ملائكة السموات وهو أعظمهم قدرا وقوة

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r4.claim: A report attributed to ʿAlī describes this angel as having 70,000 faces, each with 70,000 further faces and tongues and languages praising God; each praise creates an angel, and no creation is greater except the Throne.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r4.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه قال : هو ملك له سبعون ألف وجه

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r5.speaker: author
