RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r5.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that if ʿAlī knew this description, the Prophet should have known it too; ʿAlī could only have learned it from the Prophet, so it is unclear why the Prophet would tell him and not others.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r5.anchor: هذا التفصيل لما عرفه علي ، فالنبي أولى أن يكون قد عرفه

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r6.claim: The multiplied languages serve no purpose if one creature speaks them all; if a different creature speaks each language, the account describes many angels rather than one.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r6.anchor: إن كان حيوانا واحدا وعاقلا واحدا لم يكن في تكثير تلك اللغات فائدة

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī says the immense angel is an unknown being, an unlikely subject of inquiry; the familiar life-giving human spirit is the likelier referent.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r7.anchor: أما الروح الذي هو سبب الحياة فهو شيء تتوفر دواعي العقلاء على معرفته

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r8.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda identify the spirit as Gabriel, whom God calls the trustworthy spirit and “Our spirit”; Gabriel says that he descends only by his Lord’s command.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r8.anchor: وهو قول الحسن وقتادة أن هذا الروح جبريل والدليل عليه أنه تعالى سمى جبريل

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r9.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the spirit is a creation outside the angels, resembling human beings and having hands, feet, heads, and the ability to eat.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد : الروح خلق ليسوا من الملائكة على صورة بني آدم يأكلون

RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r10.speaker: أبو صالح
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r10.claim: Abū Ṣāliḥ says these beings resemble people but are not people; al-Rāzī finds no Qurʾānic or sound-report evidence for this unknown interpretation and considers it an unlikely question.
RAZI-FULL:v21p32/r10.anchor: وقال أبو صالح يشبهون الناس وليسوا بالناس ولم أجد في القرآن ولا في الأخبار الصحيحة

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī starts from certain self-awareness: when a person says “I” while knowing, thinking, seeing, hearing, or feeling, what is that self—body, accident, their combination, something distinct, or a combination with that third thing?
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r1.anchor: العلم الضروري حاصل بأن ها هنا شيئا إليه يشير الإنسان بقوله أنا

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r2.speaker: جمهور المتكلمين
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r2.claim: Most speculative theologians identify the human with the visible bodily structure and say no formal definition is needed; al-Rāzī rejects this identification.
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r2.anchor: القائلون بأن الإنسان عبارة عن هذه البنية المحسوسة وعن هذا الجسم المحسوس

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r3.claim: The body’s parts change through growth, aging, weight gain, and loss, while the enduring self remains; since change differs from what persists, the person is not the sum of the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r3.anchor: أجزاء هذه الجثة متبدلة بالزيادة والنقصان تارة بحسب النمو والذبول

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r4.claim: When focused on one matter, a person may be unaware of every body part yet remain aware of self and say “I was angry” or “I heard”; the self therefore differs from the body and its parts.
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r4.anchor: فهو في تلك الحالة عالم بنفسه المخصوصة وغافل عن جملة بدنه

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r5.claim: People call body parts “my head,” “my eye,” and “my hand”; the owner is distinct from what is owned, so the human differs from the body and its parts.
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r5.anchor: كل أحد يحكم عقله بإضافة كل واحد من هذه الأعضاء إلى نفسه فيقول رأسي وعيني

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r6.claim: The objection that saying “my self” makes the person distinct from himself is answered by distinguishing the body, which is other than the human essence, from the specific reality meant by “I,” which cannot be re-added to itself.
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r6.anchor: فإذا قال نفسي وذاتي فإن كان المراد البدن فعندنا أنه مغاير لجوهر الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r7.claim: Any proof that a human cannot be a body also shows that the human cannot be identified with this particular body; al-Rāzī says he will detail such proofs later.
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r7.anchor: كل دليل على أن الإنسان يمتنع أن يكون جسما فهو أيضا يدل على أنه يمتنع

RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r8.claim: A person remains alive when the body is dead: the Qurʾān calls slain martyrs alive with their Lord, while the senses show their bodies are dead, so the person differs from the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p33/r8.anchor: ولا تحسبن الذين قتلوا في سبيل الله أمواتا بل أحياء عند ربهم يرزقون

RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r1.claim: Qurʾānic descriptions of the dead exposed to Fire and of those drowned entering Fire, along with reports that prophets move between abodes, graves are gardens or pits, and death begins one’s Hour, show the person survives the dead body; identifying that person with a living corpse would make every inanimate thing potentially alive.

RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r2.claim: A long sermon attributed to the Prophet says the dead person’s spirit hovers over the bier, warns family not to be deceived by worldly life, and laments that wealth gathered lawfully and unlawfully goes to others while the liability remains with him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r2.anchor: قوله عليه السلام في خطبة طويلة له ( حتى إذا حمل الميت على نعشه

RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī infers that the person is still alive and aware while the body lies dead on the bier, proving that the human differs from the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r3.anchor: كان ذلك الإنسان حيا باقيا فاهما وذلك تصريح بأن الإنسان شيء مغاير لهذا الجسد

RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r4.claim: The command to the tranquil soul to return to its Lord addresses it at death and describes it as content and accepted; the surviving, living soul is the human, distinct from the dead body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p34/r4.anchor: ارجعى إلى ربك راضية مرضية } ( الفجر : 27 ، 28 ) والخطاب بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r1.claim: At death, the messengers take a person and the dead are returned to God, their true Master; because the body is dead, the one returned must differ from it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r1.anchor: توفته رسلنا وهم لا يفرطون * ثم ردوا إلى الله مولاهم الحق

RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r2.claim: People across nations and religions give charity for their dead, pray for them, and visit their graves; these practices would be pointless unless the person survived the body, which al-Rāzī says accords with sound original human nature.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r2.anchor: يتصدقون عن موتاهم ويدعون لهم بالخير ويذهبون إلى زياراتهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r3.claim: Many people dream that a deceased parent or child reveals hidden treasure or requests repayment of a debt, then find the information correct; al-Rāzī takes this as evidence the person survives bodily death.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r3.anchor: كثيرا من الناس يرى أباه أو ابنه بعد موته في المنام ويقول له اذهب إلى الموضع الفلاني

RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r4.claim: If hands, legs, eyes, or ears are lost, a person still experiences himself as the same person as before; this proves the self differs from those body parts and refutes identifying the human with the bodily structure.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35/r4.anchor: فإن ذلك الإنسان يجد من قلبه وعقله أنه هو عين ذلك الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r1.claim: If a transformed human either perished and a new pig was created, or persisted while its bodily structure changed, the human is distinct from the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r1.anchor: إن ذلك الإنسان هل بقي حال ذلك المسخ أو لم يبق

RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r2.claim: Gabriel and Satan could appear in human form without being human in essence, so the human is not identical with the visible bodily form.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r2.anchor: كان يرى جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام في صورة دحية الكلبي

RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r3.claim: In adultery the sexual organ acts while the back receives punishment; the experiencing subject is distinct from both organs.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r3.anchor: أن الزاني يزني بفرجه فيضرب على ظهره

RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r4.claim: The addressee of commands is no particular body part; identifying it with the whole body also fails, since one cognition cannot inhabit many parts and each part is not independently knowing.
RAZI-FULL:v21p35#2/r4.anchor: المخاطب بهذا الخطاب والمأمور والمنهي ليس هو جبهة زيد

RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r1.claim: Free choice requires knowledge, which Razi locates in the heart by introspection and scripture; therefore the human subject is something in the heart, not the bodily frame.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r1.anchor: العلم لا يحصل إلا في القلب فيلزم أن يكون الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r2.claim: Since a human essence is neither surface nor color, while everything visible is one of those, the human essence is not visible or otherwise sensible.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36/r2.anchor: حقيقة الإنسان شيء مغاير للسطح واللون وكل ما هو مرئي

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r1.claim: A bodily candidate within a human must be a mixture of the four elements; no pure elemental body occurs in the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r1.anchor: لا بد وأن يكون الحاصل جسما متولدا من امتزاجات هذه الأربعة

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r2.speaker: القائلون بأن الإنسان شيء مغاير لهذا الجسد
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r2.claim: No proponent who distinguishes the human from the body identifies the person with a dense earthy organ such as bone, nerve, flesh, or skin.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r2.anchor: لم يقل أحد من العقلاء بأن الإنسان عبارة عن أحد هذه الأعضاء

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r3.claim: Among the humors, some identify the human spirit with blood because its departure entails death.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r3.anchor: إلا في الدم فإن منهم من قال إنه هو الروح بدليل أنه إذا خرج

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r4.speaker: منهم من يقول
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r4.claim: One bodily theory identifies the human with airy spirits mixed with innate heat, generated either in the heart or brain.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r4.anchor: أجسام هوائية مخلوطة بالحرارة الغريزية متولدة إما في القلب أو في الدماغ

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r5.speaker: منهم من يقول
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r5.claim: One view locates the human spirit in the heart; another makes it an indivisible part in the brain.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r5.anchor: فمنهم من يقول الإنسان هو الروح الذي في القلب

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r6.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r6.claim: Another view makes the person the fiery innate heat mixed with the cardiac and cerebral spirits.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r6.anchor: الروح عبارة عن أجزاء نارية مختلطة بهذه الأرواح القلبية والدماغية

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r7.speaker: من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r7.claim: Razi calls worthy of reflection a theory of imperishable, luminous celestial bodies entering the prepared body like oil in sesame; thick humors later block them and cause death.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r7.anchor: فهذا مذهب قوي شريف يجب التأمل فيه

RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r8.claim: Razi knows of no one who says the human is a body located outside the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p36#2/r8.anchor: وأما أن الإنسان جسم موجود خارج البدن فلا أعرف أحدا ذهب إلى هذا القول

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r1.claim: The human cannot be an accident in the body: the human is a substance described by knowledge, power, deliberation, and action.
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r1.anchor: من المعلوم بالضرورة أن الإنسان جوهر لأنه موصوف بالعلم والقدرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r2.speaker: جمهور الأطباء ومنكري بقاء النفس وأبو الحسين البصري
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r2.claim: Humanity is a particular mixture of elemental bodies and temperament, just as other mixture-ranges yield other species; its advocates include most physicians, deniers of soul-survival, and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri.
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r2.anchor: هذا قول جمهور الأطباء ومنكري بقاء النفس وقول أبي الحسين البصري

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r3.speaker: أكثر شيوخ المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r3.claim: Most early Mu'tazilite authorities deny a separate soul and define the human as bodies bearing life, knowledge, and power.

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r4.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r4.claim: A view distinguishes humans from animals by bodily shape, but Razi rejects it: angels can assume human forms and transformed humans retain humanity without that form.
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r4.anchor: فقد بطل اعتبار هذا الشكل في حصول معنى الإنسانية طردا وعكسا

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r5.speaker: أكثر الإلهيين من الفلاسفة
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r5.claim: Most philosophers affirm an immaterial soul that survives for spiritual resurrection, reward, punishment, and reckoning; Razi also names al-Raghib, al-Ghazali, Mu'ammar b. 'Abbad, al-Mufid, and some Karramites.
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r5.anchor: وذهب إليه جماعة عظيمة من علماء المسلمين مثل الشيخ أبي القاسم الراغب الأصفهاني والشيخ أبي حامد الغزالي

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r6.speaker: المحققون
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r6.claim: The investigators identify the human with a particular immaterial substance, neither inside nor outside the world, related to the body through governance and direction.
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r6.anchor: الإنسان عبارة عن هذا الجوهر المخصوص ، وهذا البدن

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r7.speaker: الفريق الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r7.claim: A second soul theory says soul and body unite into the human; at death the union ends, the body decays, and the soul remains.
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r7.anchor: فصارت النفس عين البدن ، والبدن عين النفس

RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r8.speaker: ثابت بن قرة
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r8.claim: Thabit ibn Qurra says the soul is connected to subtle, luminous celestial bodies that permeate the body and leave it at death.
RAZI-FULL:v21p37/r8.anchor: وكان ثابت بن قرة يثبت النفس ويقول إنها متعلقة بأجسام سماوية نورانية لطيفة

RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r1.claim: If the human substance occupied space, spatial extension would be essential to it; yet one knows oneself without conceiving extension, so the human is not a spatial body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r1.anchor: أنا قد نعرف ذاتنا حال كوننا جاهلين بالتحيز والامتداد في الجهات الثلاثة

RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r2.claim: Against the objection that self-knowledge should reveal an immaterial nature, Razi answers that being nonspatial is a negative property, not the known essence itself.
RAZI-FULL:v21p38/r2.anchor: كونه مجردا معناه أنه ليس بمتحيز ولا حالا في المتحيز

RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r1.claim: The self signified by each person's I is immediately known to be one, though this alone does not decide whether it is internally composite.
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r1.anchor: كان ذلك المشار إليه واحدا غير متعدد

RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r2.claim: Anger and desire require awareness of what is harmful or pleasing, so the subject who responds must itself perceive.
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r2.anchor: فالذي يغضب لا بد وأن يكون هو بعينه مدركا

RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r3.claim: If perception, anger, and desire belonged to independent substances, engaging one would not impede another; since they do interfere, they are states of one substance.
RAZI-FULL:v21p39/r3.anchor: فعلمنا أن هذه الأمور الثلاثة ليست مباديء مستقلة بل هي صفات مختلفة بجوهر واحد

RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r1.claim: When perception causes desire or anger, the perceiver must be the very same subject that desires and becomes angry.
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r1.anchor: صاحب الإدراك بعينه هو صاحب الشهوة بعينها وصاحب الغضب بعينه

RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r2.claim: Because voluntary movement requires awareness of good and harm, one human soul is the subject of all senses, imagination, thought, memory, desire, anger, and voluntary action.
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r2.anchor: أن النفس الإنسانية شيء واحد وثبت أن ذلك الشيء هو المبصر والسامع

RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r3.claim: The soul is not the entire body or a bodily part: capacities such as sight and hearing are assigned to particular organs, and no one part bears every perception and action.
RAZI-FULL:v21p40/r3.anchor: ليس في البدن جزء واحد وهو بعينه موصوف بالأبصار والسماع والفكر والذكر

RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r1.claim: Seeing, knowing, desiring, and moving toward an object belong to one subject; assigning them to different subjects breaks the causal sequence.
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r1.anchor: الذي أبصر هو الذي عرف وأن الذي عرف هو الذي اشتهى

RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r2.claim: Speech likewise requires one agent to understand and intend meaning, produce sounds through vocal organs, and move the body; this unified agent is distinct from the various organs.
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r2.anchor: محل العلوم والإرادات هو القلب لزم أيضا أن يكون محل الصوت هو القلب

RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r3.claim: The organs are instruments: the distinct soul sees with the eye, hears with the ear, thinks with the brain, and reasons with the heart, governing the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p40#2/r3.anchor: والنفس جوهر مغاير لها مفارق عنها بالذات متعلق بها تعلق التصرف والتدبير

RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r1.claim: If life and knowledge belonged separately to every bodily part, one body would contain many independent humans who might will conflicting movements; if one property belonged to all parts, one accident would occupy many substrates.
RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r1.anchor: والقسمان باطلان فبطل القول بكون الإنسان عبارة عن هذا الجسد

RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r2.claim: The proposed fix that life in one part makes the whole body alive fails: a single property across the whole body is impossible, while separate properties make many humans.
RAZI-FULL:v21p41/r2.anchor: إن حصل في مجموع جثة مجموع حياة واحدة وعالمية واحدة فقد حصلت الصفة الواحدة

RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r1.claim: Unlike material forms, which replace one another, acquired intelligible forms make further learning easier and accumulate without weakening the soul.
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r1.anchor: ثم إن النفس لا تزال تقبل صورة بعد صورة من غير أن تضعف ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r2.claim: Careful thought perfects the soul but dries and weakens the body; one entity cannot thereby be perfected and damaged, alive and dying, at once.
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r2.anchor: هذه الأفكار توجب حياة النفس وشرفها وتوجب نقصان البدن وموته

RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r3.claim: A weak body can become fearless and powerful when sacred light or a hidden divine mystery appears to the person, indicating a distinct soul.
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r3.anchor: فإذا لاح له نور من الأنوار القدسية وتجلى له سر من أسرار عالم الغيب

RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r4.claim: Ascetic discipline weakens bodily powers while strengthening spiritual powers and divine knowledge; indulgence instead leaves a person beastlike and without reason.
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r4.anchor: كلما أمعنوا في قهر القوى البدنية وتجويع الجسد قويت قواهم الروحانية

RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r5.claim: The soul uses organs for sensation and movement, yet retains knowledge without bodily instruments; closing eyes or ears blocks sight or hearing, not what one already knows.
RAZI-FULL:v21p42/r5.anchor: لا يمكنه البتة أن يزيل عن قلبه العلم بما كان عالما به

RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r1.claim: Forgetting oneself in ignorance cannot mean forgetting the visible body, so the self mentioned in the verse is other than the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r1.anchor: أن أحدا من العقلاء لا ينسى هذا الهيكل المشاهد

RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r2.claim: The command to bring forth the selves is explicit evidence that the self differs from the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r2.anchor: وهذا صريح أن النفس غير البدن

RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r3.claim: The stages through which the body develops differ from the subsequent breathing of spirit; the objection that humans are part of clay fails because min marks origin, not composition.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r3.anchor: من التغيرات الواقعة في الأحوال الجسمانية

RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r4.claim: God distinguishes bodily fashioning from breathing His spirit and attributes the spirit to Himself, showing that spirit and body have different essences.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43/r4.anchor: ميز تعالى بين البشرية وبين نفخ الروح

RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r1.claim: The soul is one subject capable of cognition and action, whereas neither the whole body nor a bodily part bears both descriptions; the verse supports a distinct substance.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r1.anchor: وهذه الآية صريحة في وجود شيء موصوف بالإدراك والتحريك حقا

RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r2.claim: The single human tested by divine duties and described as hearing and seeing cannot be the body as a whole or any one part, so the soul differs from both.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r2.anchor: فهذا تصريح بأن الإنسان شيء واحد وذلك الشيء هو المبتلي بالتكاليف الإلهية

RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r3.claim: Numerous reports about souls before embodiment and after bodily separation also show that the soul is distinct from the body.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r3.anchor: الأحاديث الواردة في صفة الأرواح قبل تعلقها بالأجساد

RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r4.claim: Razi calls it astonishing that someone can read these verses and reports yet claim the Prophet died without knowing the spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v21p43#2/r4.anchor: ثم يقول توفى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وما كان يعرف الروح

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r1.claim: If spirit were a body progressing through states, the answer would describe its formation as it does the body's; calling it from God's command and created by Be instead identifies it as a holy, immaterial substance.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r1.anchor: دل ذلك على أنه جوهر ليس من جنس الأجسام بل هو جوهر قدسي مجرد

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r2.speaker: الواسطي
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti reports that God created spirits from beauty and radiance; if their glory were unveiled, every disbeliever would prostrate.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : خلق الله الأرواح من بين الجمال والبهاء

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r3.claim: The spirit first relates to the heart, then its influence reaches all bodily members, as Razi explained under the verse about the Trustworthy Spirit.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r3.anchor: أن تعلقه الأول بالقلب ثم بواسطته يصل تأثيره إلى جملة الأعضاء

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r4.speaker: المنكرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r4.claim: Opponents argue that a nonbodily, nonaccidental soul would match God's essence; Razi replies that sharing a negative property does not entail likeness or identity.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r4.anchor: المساواة في أنه ليس بمتحيز ولا حال في المتحيز مساواة في صفة سلبية

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r5.speaker: المنكرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r5.claim: Opponents cite the human created from a drop, dying and buried, as proof that the human is the body; Razi answers that ordinary usage calls the body the human.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r5.anchor: لما كان الإنسان في العرف والظاهر عبارة عن هذه الجثة أطلق عليه اسم الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r6.speaker: المنكرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r6.claim: Opponents say the provision and joy promised to slain believers are bodily qualities; Razi says this provision is knowledge and love of God, while their buried bodies and spirits beneath the Throne demonstrate the soul's difference.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r6.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الروح غير البدن وليكن هذا آخر كلامنا في هذا الباب

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r7.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r7.claim: Exegetes report that listeners asked whether the Prophet alone had little knowledge; he replied that both they and he had received little, prompting their comparison with the promise of abundant good.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r7.anchor: بل نحن وأنتم لم نؤت من العلم إلا قليلا

RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r8.claim: There is no contradiction: human knowledge is little beside God's knowledge and the realities of things, yet abundant beside bodily desires and pleasures.
RAZI-FULL:v21p44/r8.anchor: فالعلوم الحاصلة عند الناس قليلة جدا بالنسبة إلى علم الله

NAHHAS:v2p439/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p439/r1.speaker: بعض العلماء
NAHHAS:v2p439/r1.claim: One view says God knew it was better not to explain the soul, since the Jews claimed explaining it would disprove the Prophet's mission while refusing to explain it would prove it.
NAHHAS:v2p439/r1.anchor: فقيل : علم الله جل وعز أن الأصلح لهم أن لا يخبرهم ما الروح

NAHHAS:v2p439/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p439/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
NAHHAS:v2p439/r2.claim: Another view says they asked about Jesus; the reply means the soul is something God commanded and created, contrary to the Christian claim.
NAHHAS:v2p439/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنهم سألوا عن عيسى [ & ] فقال لهم الروح من أمر ربي

STUDYQURAN:17:85/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r1.speaker: many Muslim thinkers
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r1.claim: The Spirit may be the source of human life, knowledge, perception, spiritual ability, and religious, moral, and spiritual responsibility.
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r1.anchor: The Spirit here and elsewhere in the Quran may refer to the Spirit that is the source of human life

STUDYQURAN:17:85/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r2.claim: Alternatively, the Spirit may be Gabriel, the angel of revelation called the Holy Spirit.
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r2.anchor: The Spirit may also refer, according to some, to the Archangel Gabriel

STUDYQURAN:17:85/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r3.speaker: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r3.claim: A tradition attributed to ʿAlī describes the Spirit as an angel with seventy thousand heads, each with seventy thousand tongues praising God.
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r3.anchor: According to a tradition from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, the Spirit is an angel with seventy thousand heads

STUDYQURAN:17:85/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r4.claim: Another opinion interprets the Spirit as the Quran; the verse is also used to identify the Spirit with the realm of Divine Command.
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r4.anchor: Another opinion interprets Spirit here as a reference to the Quran

STUDYQURAN:17:85/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r5.speaker: some reports
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r5.claim: Reports say the verse was revealed after either Madinan Jews or Makkan idolaters asked the Prophet about the Spirit.
STUDYQURAN:17:85/r5.anchor: Various reports indicate that the present verse was revealed in response to a group of either Madinan Jews or Makkan idolaters

TAB-FULL:v15p66/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r1.claim: The questioners are Jewish People of the Book asking what the spirit is; the response says that all people have received only a little knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r1.anchor: ويسألك الكفار بالله من أهل الكتاب عن الروح ما هي؟ قل لهم: الروح من أمر ربي،

TAB-FULL:v15p66/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r2.claim: Ibn Masud recounts Jews asking about the spirit while the Prophet walked in a Medina field; revelation came, and the Jews reproached one another for asking.
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r2.anchor: قال: كنت مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث بالمدينة، ومعه عسيب يتوكأ عليه، فمر بقوم من اليهود،

TAB-FULL:v15p66/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r3.claim: Ikrima reports that the People of the Book objected that they possessed the Torah and its wisdom; the Prophet answered that knowledge is little relative to God's, though useful knowledge is good.
TAB-FULL:v15p66/r3.anchor: قالوا: أتزعم أنا لم نؤت من العلم إلا قليلا، وقد أوتينا التوراة، وهي الحكمة

TAB-FULL:v15p69/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r1.claim: Ibn Masud recounts that a Jew asked the Prophet in a Medina field what the spirit was; the Prophet fell silent until revelation instructed him to answer.
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r1.anchor: قال: إني لمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث بالمدينة، إذ أتاه يهودي، قال: يا أبا القاسم، ما الروح؟

TAB-FULL:v15p69/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r2.claim: Qatada says Jews challenged the Prophet with questions about the spirit, the People of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Qur'an answered them all.
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} [الإسراء: 85] لقيت اليهود نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فتغشوه وسألوه

TAB-FULL:v15p69/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r3.claim: Mujahid says Jews were the ones asking about the spirit.
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح،} [الإسراء: 85] قال: يهود تسأل عنه

TAB-FULL:v15p69/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jews asked what the spirit is and how it is punished in the body; after Gabriel conveyed God's answer, they accused Gabriel of being their enemy, prompting the response in 2:97.
TAB-FULL:v15p69/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح،} [الإسراء: 85] . . الآية: وذلك أن اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

TAB-FULL:v15p70/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked about the spirit; after revelation, they said the answer matched what they found in their scripture.
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r1.anchor: قال: كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات يوم، فمررنا بأناس من اليهود، فقالوا: يا أبا القاسم ما الروح؟

TAB-FULL:v15p70/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the spirit as Gabriel and says Ibn Abbas used to conceal this interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r2.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة، { ويسألونك عن الروح،} [الإسراء: 85] قال: هو جبرائيل، قال قتادة: وكان ابن عباس يكتمه

TAB-FULL:v15p70/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the spirit as an angel.
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r3.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح،} [الإسراء: 85] قال: الروح: ملك

TAB-FULL:v15p70/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r4.claim: Ali describes the spirit as an angel with seventy thousand faces, each with seventy thousand tongues and languages, whose glorifications generate angels until Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r4.anchor: أنه قال في قوله: {ويسألونك عن الروح} [الإسراء: 85] قال: هو ملك من الملائكة له سبعون ألف وجه،

TAB-FULL:v15p70/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r5.claim: Here, from God's command means the spirit belongs to matters God knows exclusively; people do not know what it is, but God does.
TAB-FULL:v15p70/r5.anchor: فإنه يعني: أنه من الأمر الذي يعلمه الله عز وجل دونكم، فلا تعلمونه ويعلم ما هو

TAB-FULL:v15p72/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r1.claim: Arabic may address a group in the second person when the statement concerns both present addressees and absent people.
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r1.anchor: لأن العرب كذلك تفعل إذا اجتمع في الكلام مخبر عنه غائب ومخاطب أخرجوا الكلام خطابا للجمع

TAB-FULL:v15p72/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq reports that the verse was revealed in Mecca, then Jewish scholars in Medina asked whether it referred to them or the Prophet's people; he said it included all and Torah knowledge is little by God's measure.
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r2.anchor: قال: نزلت بمكة {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} [الإسراء: 85] فلما هاجر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المدينة أتاه أحبار يهود،

TAB-FULL:v15p72/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the address includes Muhammad and all people.
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قوله عز وجل {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} [الإسراء: 85] قال: يا محمد والناس أجمعون

TAB-FULL:v15p72/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r4.claim: Qatada restricts the intended audience of the little-knowledge statement to the Jews who asked about the spirit.
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} [الإسراء: 85] يعني: اليهود

TAB-FULL:v15p72/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r5.claim: Al-Tabari prefers that the direct address includes all creation: each person's knowledge, however extensive, is little beside God's knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v15p72/r5.anchor: أن يقال: خرج الكلام خطابا لمن خوطب به، والمراد به جميع الخلق، لأن علم كل أحد سوى الله، وإن كثر في علم الله قليل.

TABATABAI:17:85/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85/r1.claim: Mullā Ṣadrā sharpens the account of causation: an effect's very essence is dependence on its cause; otherwise it would first exist independently and cease to be an effect.
TABATABAI:17:85/r1.anchor: فذاته عين الفقر والتعلق فليس له من الوجود إلا الرابط غير المستقل

TABATABAI:17:85/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85/r2.claim: The Quran treats every thing as a sign of God; created things mirror divine existence and attributes only as dependent signs, not as possessing God's identity.
TABATABAI:17:85/r2.anchor: الأشياء بما هي مخلوقة له تعالى أفعاله

TABATABAI:17:85/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85/r3.claim: In ordinary language spirit is the source of life enabling sensation and voluntary movement; figuratively it can name what gives desired life to souls, such as knowledge.
TABATABAI:17:85/r3.anchor: الروح على ما يعرف في اللغة هو مبدء الحياة الذي به يقوى الحيوان على الإحساس والحركة الإرادية

TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r1.speaker: جماعة
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r1.claim: Some interpreters take ‘spirit’ figuratively for revelation or the Quran because it gives life to spiritually dead souls, as bodily spirit gives life to bodies.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r1.anchor: لأن به حياة النفوس الميتة كما أن الروح المعروف به حياة الأجساد الميتة

TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r2.claim: Across the Quran's many uses, spirit does not mean the animal life-principle; in some passages it is a distinct being accompanying angels in revelation.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r2.anchor: ولم يرد في جميعها المعنى الذي نجده في الحيوان وهو مبدء الحياة

TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r3.speaker: علي عليه السلام
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī recalls ʿAlī's argument that the spirit mentioned with angels is distinct from the angels themselves.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r3.anchor: وقد تقدم الحديث عن علي عليه السلام أنه احتج بقوله تعالى ينزل الملائكة بالروح من أمره

TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r4.claim: Gabriel descends with the distinct Spirit, which carries the recited Quran; therefore ‘a spirit from Our command’ in 42:52 means the Spirit's descent, not the Quran itself.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#5/r4.anchor: فجبريل ينزل بالروح والروح يحمل هذا القرآن المقرو المتلو

TABATABAI:17:85#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r1.claim: Jesus is called God's word and a spirit from Him; a created being can be called a divine word, and Jesus was created by the command ‘Be’ without ordinary procreation.
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r1.anchor: فعد الروح كلمة دالة على المراد فمن الجائز أن يعد الروح وحيا كما عد كلمة

TABATABAI:17:85#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r2.claim: The phrase ‘from my Lord's command’ identifies spirit as belonging to the kind of divine command, as in other Quranic descriptions of spirit.
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r2.anchor: لتبيين الجنس كما في نظائرها من الآيات

TABATABAI:17:85#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r3.claim: God's command is His creative ‘Be’: existence considered solely in relation to God, without intermediary causes, time, or place; gradual creation through causes belongs to creation rather than command.
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r3.anchor: فالأمر هو وجود الشيء من جهة استناده إليه تعالى وحده والخلق هو ذلك من جهة استناده إليه مع توسط الأسباب الكونية فيه

TABATABAI:17:85#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r4.claim: The one, instantaneous divine command is likened to a blink to deny temporal progression; created processes have a timeless aspect in their direct dependence on God.
TABATABAI:17:85#2/r4.anchor: شبه أمره بعد عده واحدة بلمح بالبصر وهذا النوع من التشبيه لنفي التدريج

TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r1.claim: Embryological stages mediated by causes are distinguished from the human's final creation as another creation, directly attributed to God and thus belonging to command.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r1.anchor: فعد إيجاده المنسوب إلى نفسه من غير تخلل الأسباب الكونية إنشاء خلق آخر

TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r2.claim: Divine command is God's special creative act, above material existence and unmediated by natural causes or temporal and spatial limits.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r2.anchor: الأمر هو كلمة الإيجاد السماوية وفعله تعالى المختص به الذي لا تتوسط فيه الأسباب

TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r3.claim: Every thing has a command and a malakut, its more encompassing kingdom; spirit belongs to this elevated, nonmaterial order.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r3.anchor: فقد بان بما مر أن الأمر هو كلمة الإيجاد وهو فعله تعالى الخاص به

TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r4.claim: The Quran describes several spirits: one with angels, one breathed into humans, one supporting believers, one sent to prophets, and spirit associated with animal and plant life.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r4.anchor: ومنه ما هو منفوخ في الإنسان عامة

TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#6/r5.claim: The Quran sometimes names Spirit separately alongside angels, showing that it is a distinct kind within the spiritual order.

TABATABAI:17:85-86/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r1.claim: Some exegetes identify the questioned spirit with the being who stands with angels or ascends with them; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says they offer no proof.
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r1.anchor: فقال بعضهم إن المراد بالروح المسؤول عنه

TABATABAI:17:85-86/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r2.claim: Some identify the spirit as Gabriel because he is called a spirit, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects inferring that every use names him; Jesus is also called spirit.
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به جبريل فإن الله سماه روحا

TABATABAI:17:85-86/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r3.claim: Some say the question concerns the Quran and whether it comes from God or Muhammad, with the answer asserting its miraculous divine origin; the author says the name ‘spirit’ elsewhere does not establish that meaning here.
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به القرآن لأن الله سماه روحا

TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.claim: The following verse about removing revelation does not uniquely support the Quran interpretation; it also fits other proposed meanings of spirit.
TABATABAI:17:85-86/r4.anchor: على أن الآية التالية لا تتعين تأييدا لهذا الوجه بل تلائم بعض الوجوه الأخر أيضا

TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r1.claim: Some take spirit as the human soul and the answer as refusing to disclose its essence; they disagree among themselves whether it is an airy body, bodily part, accident, or the body itself.
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به الروح الإنساني فهو المتبادر من إطلاقه

TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects relying on ordinary-language presumption or treating the answer as a ban on inquiry; Quranic verses about spirit disprove these accounts.
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r2.anchor: وفيه أن التبادر في كلامه تعالى ممنوع

TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r3.claim: Some say the question asks whether spirit is eternal or created, and the answer means it is created by God's act; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī finds no textual basis for this question.
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم إن المراد به مطلق الروح الواقع في كلامه والسؤال إنما هو عن كونه قديما أو محدثا

TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r4.claim: Exegetes also disagree whether ‘spirit is from my Lord's command’ answers the question or turns away from it; which reading fits depends on their different identifications of spirit.
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r4.anchor: ثم إن لهم اختلافا في معنى

TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r5.claim: The context favors addressing the questioners themselves, likely Jews, since they were known for learning; Quraysh and other Arabs are elsewhere called people who do not know.
TABATABAI:17:85-86#2/r5.anchor: والأنسب بالسياق أن يكون الخطاب متوجها إلى السائلين والكلام من تمام قول النبي

TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r6.claim: A report says Quraysh asked Jews for a question to pose to Muhammad; they suggested asking about spirit, and the reply led them to cite the Torah before revelation about the sea as ink for God's words.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قالت قريش لليهود أعطونا شيئا نسأل هذا الرجل

TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r7.claim: Other reports place the question among Jews in Medina, but al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says that conflicts with the sura's Meccan setting and unified context.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r7.anchor: وكون السورة مكية واتحاد سياق آياتها لا يلائم ذلك

TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī and other compilers transmit ʿAlī's account of a many-faced, many-tongued angel called Spirit; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it because Quranic usage distinguishes Spirit from angels.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#7/r8.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب في قوله

TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r1.claim: The report making Spirit an angel conflicts with Quranic passages that place Spirit alongside angels; an earlier report from ʿAlī likewise argues against identifying them.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r1.anchor: كون الروح من الملائكة لا يوافق ظاهر عدة من آيات الكتاب

TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r2.claim: A report in al-Kāfī calls Spirit a creation greater than Gabriel and Michael, accompanying Muhammad and the Imams and belonging to the malakut; the author says this agrees with his reading.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r2.anchor: قال خلق أعظم من جبرائيل وميكائيل كان مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r3.claim: The preceding report accords with the Quranic account of Spirit as an order-of-command being with multiple levels.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r3.anchor: والرواية توافق ما تقدم توضيحه من مدلول الآيات

TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r4.claim: A report says Spirit is a created being with sight, power, and support that God places in the hearts of prophets and believers; its opening denies that God has an interior or hollow core.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r4.anchor: قال إن الله تبارك وتعالى أحد صمد والصمد الشيء الذي ليس له جوف

TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r5.claim: The report's opening guards against taking ‘I breathed into him of My spirit’ to mean God has a cavity or a portion of Himself that was breathed out.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r5.anchor: دفعا لما يتوهم من مثل قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r6.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r6.claim: A report identifies the spirit in animals and people as coming from the malakut and divine power; the author says it supports a broad, multi-level account and implies animal spirit is immaterial.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r6.anchor: التي في الدواب والناس قلت وما هي

TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r7.claim: A report recounts Quraysh leaders meeting Muhammad at the Kaaba after sunset to argue and excuse their opposition, accusing him of insulting ancestors, attacking religion, dividing the community, and cursing their gods; they offer wealth, leadership, kingship, or medical help if he seeks them or suffers from a jinn.
TABATABAI:17:82-100#8/r7.anchor: اجتمعوا بعد غروب الشمس عند ظهر الكعبة فقال بعضهم لبعض ابعثوا إلى محمد وكلموه وخاصموه

TABRISI:17:85/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85/r1.claim: Ẓahīr means helper, as if allies strengthen one another back-to-back; taṣrīf turns things through directions and speech through different meanings.
TABRISI:17:85/r1.anchor: الظهير المعين وهو المظاهر وأصله من الظهر

TABRISI:17:85/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:17:85/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī favors the view that they asked about the human spirit; the Prophet withheld an answer because they were obstinate and an answer would deepen their defiance.
TABRISI:17:85/r4.anchor: واختاره الجبائي وعلى هذا فإنما عدل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جوابهم

TABRISI:17:85/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس
TABRISI:17:85/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and others say they asked what the spirit in a human body is.
TABRISI:17:85/r5.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وجماعة واختاره الجبائي

TABRISI:17:85/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85/r6.claim: A reported Jewish strategy told Quraysh to ask about the spirit as a test: answering would disprove prophethood, while silence would confirm it from their scripture.
TABRISI:17:85/r6.anchor: وقد قيل إن اليهود قالت لكفار قريش سلوا محمدا عن الروح

TABRISI:17:85/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85/r7.claim: Another view says they asked whether the spirit was created; the answer that it is from God’s command means it is His act and creation.
TABRISI:17:85/r7.anchor: أنهم سألوا عن الروح أهي مخلوقة محدثة أم ليست كذلك

TABRISI:17:85/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:17:85/r8.claim: The spirit may be the animating soul, as Ibn ʿAbbās says; alternatives are Gabriel, a vast many-faced angel in a report from ʿAlī, or Jesus, also called spirit.
TABRISI:17:85/r8.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون الروح الذي سألوه عنه هو الذي به قوام الجسد

TABRISI:17:85/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85/r9.claim: A third interpretation takes spirit as the Qurʾān and asks how the angel conveyed it or how its arrangement differs from human speech; God elsewhere calls the Qurʾān a spirit.
TABRISI:17:85/r9.anchor: أن المشركين سألوه عن الروح الذي هو القرآن كيف يلقاك به الملك

TABRISI:17:85-87/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85-87/r1.claim: On the Qurʾān interpretation, revelation is God’s act and proof of prophethood, beyond created beings’ capacity; on the human-spirit view, it means knowledge God withheld.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r1.anchor: إن الروح الذي هو القرآن من أمر ربي أنزله دلالة على دلالة نبوتي

TABRISI:17:85-87/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r2.speaker: أكثر المتكلمين
TABRISI:17:85-87/r2.claim: Most theologians, with al-Murtaḍā’s preference, define spirit as a subtle airy body moving through an animal’s passages.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r2.anchor: فقيل إنه جسم رقيق هوائي متردد في مخارق الحيوان

TABRISI:17:85-87/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r3.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:17:85-87/r3.claim: ʿAlī b. ʿĪsā calls it an airy body shaped as an animal, with life in every part; animals have body and spirit, though one may predominate.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r3.anchor: عن علي بن عيسى قال فلكل حيوان روح وبدن

TABRISI:17:85-87/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r4.speaker: المفيد والبلخي
TABRISI:17:85-87/r4.claim: Al-Mufīd, al-Balkhī, and Baghdadi Muʿtazilites regard spirit as an accident: life enabling a subject to possess power, knowledge, and choice.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r4.anchor: وهو مذهب الشيخ المفيد أبي عبد الله محمد بن محمد بن النعمان والبلخي

TABRISI:17:85-87/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r5.speaker: الأسواري
TABRISI:17:85-87/r5.claim: Al-Aswārī says spirit is a meaning located in the heart.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r5.anchor: وقيل هو معنى في القلب عن الأسواري

TABRISI:17:85-87/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r6.speaker: ابن الإخشيد والنظام
TABRISI:17:85-87/r6.claim: Ibn al-Ikhshīd and al-Naẓẓām identify spirit with the human being, the living morally responsible person.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r6.anchor: عن ابن الإخشيد والنظام وقال بعض العلماء إن الله تعالى خلق الروح

TABRISI:17:85-87/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r7.speaker: بعض العلماء
TABRISI:17:85-87/r7.claim: Some scholars say God created spirit from light, purity, permanence, life, knowledge, and elevation; martyrs remain alive with God after bodily decay.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r7.anchor: إن الله تعالى خلق الروح من ستة أشياء من جوهر النور والطيب

TABRISI:17:85-87/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:85-87/r8.claim: One reading takes limited knowledge to address the Prophet and everyone else: only a little is explicitly disclosed, while God’s knowledge has no end.
TABRISI:17:85-87/r8.anchor: قيل هو خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وغيره إذا لم يبين له الروح

TABRISI:17:85-87/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:85-87/r9.speaker: اليهود
TABRISI:17:85-87/r9.claim: Another reading addresses the Jews who asked, and they objected that God had given them the Torah, so how could their knowledge be little?
TABRISI:17:85-87/r9.anchor: وقيل خطاب لليهود الذين سألوه فقالت له اليهود عند ذلك

TABRISI:17:88-89/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:88-89/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:17:88-89/r4.claim: Abū Muslim also sees evidence that the question about spirit concerned the Qurʾān, since the challenge follows that discussion.
TABRISI:17:88-89/r4.anchor: قال أبو مسلم: وفي هذا أيضا دلالة على أن السؤال بالروح وقع عن القرآن

THALABI:v6p130/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130/r1.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v6p130/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports Jews asking the Prophet about the spirit in Medina; the answer was that the spirit belongs to God's command and human knowledge is little.
THALABI:v6p130/r1.anchor: الأعمش عن إبراهيم عن علقمة عن عبد الله قال: كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة

THALABI:v6p130/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p130/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Jews asked what the spirit was and how it is punished in the body, and Gabriel then brought this verse.
THALABI:v6p130/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: قالت اليهود للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخبرنا ما الروح وكيف يعذب الروح في الجسد

THALABI:v6p130/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p130/r3.claim: Another account says Jews coached Quraysh to ask about the spirit, the youths of ancient times, and a world-traveling man; the answers came in the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn passages and this verse.
THALABI:v6p130/r3.anchor: ويروى أن اليهود اجتمعوا فقالوا لقريش حين سألوهم عن شأن محمد وحاله سألوا محمدا عن الروح

THALABI:v6p130/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
THALABI:v6p130/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada identify the spirit in question as Gabriel.
THALABI:v6p130/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في هذا الروح المسئول عنه ما هو: فقال الحسن وقتادة: هو جبرئيل

THALABI:v6p130#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p130#2/r1.claim: Qatada says Ibn Abbas used to conceal his interpretation of the spirit.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: وكان ابن عباس يكتمه

THALABI:v6p130#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v6p130#2/r2.claim: Ali describes a mighty angel with seventy thousand faces, each with seventy thousand tongues and languages, who glorifies God and generates an angel from each glorification.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r2.anchor: وروى أبو الميسرة ممن حدثه عن علي بن أبي طالب (رضي الله عنه) أنه قال: في قوله ويسئلونك

THALABI:v6p130#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p130#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the spirit is a created being shaped like humans, accompanying every angel who descends from heaven.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r3.anchor: ابن عباس: الروح خلق من خلق الله صورهم على صور بني آدم، وما نزل من السماء ملك

THALABI:v6p130#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r4.speaker: أبو صالح
THALABI:v6p130#2/r4.claim: Abu Salih describes the spirit as human-shaped but not human.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r4.anchor: أبو صالح: الروح كهيئة الإنسان وليسوا بناس

THALABI:v6p130#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p130#2/r5.claim: Mujahid says the spirits resemble humans, with limbs and heads and eating, but are not angels.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r5.anchor: مجاهد: الروح على صورة بني آدم لهم أيد وأرجل ورؤوس يأكلون الطعام

THALABI:v6p130#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v6p130#2/r6.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says the spirit is God's greatest creation after the Throne, with immense reach, an angelic body and human face, and a role interceding for monotheists.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r6.anchor: سعيد بن جبير: لم يخلق الله خلقا أعظم من الروح غير العرش ولو شاء أن بلغ السماوات

THALABI:v6p130#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r7.speaker: قوم
THALABI:v6p130#2/r7.claim: Some identify the spirit as the animating spirit composed within creatures.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r7.anchor: وقال قوم: هو الروح المركب في الخلق الذي يفقده

THALABI:v6p130#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p130#2/r8.speaker: قوم
THALABI:v6p130#2/r8.claim: Some interpret the spirit as the Qur'an, since the question was who brought it; the answer explains it came from God.
THALABI:v6p130#2/r8.anchor:
وقال بعضهم: أراد بالروح القرآن وذلك
أن المشركين قالوا: يا محمد من أتاك بهذا القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Quraysh, judging Muhammad truthful, consulted Jews of Yathrib, who told them to ask about lost youths, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; answering two while withholding one would prove prophethood. After he promised an answer the next day without exception and revelation paused forty days, he answered the first two questions in the Cave chapter and left the Spirit unexplained because the Torah gave only its name. Ikrima reports similarly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: اجتمعت قريش فقال بعضهم لبعض: والله ما كان محمد بكذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r2.claim: Ibn Masud says the Jews asked the Prophet about the Spirit; Mujahid gives a similar account.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r2.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: سألته اليهود عن الروح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r3.claim: One view identifies the Spirit as an angel with seventy thousand faces, tongues, and languages, each glorifying God so a new angel is created from every glorification; Said ibn Jubayr similarly calls it the greatest created being after the Throne, able to swallow heavens and earth. This is the Spirit in 78:38.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p460/r3.anchor: وهو قول علي -رضي الله عنه- قال: هو ملك من الملائكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r1.claim: Hasan and Qatada say the Spirit is Gabriel; Abu Ishaq cites 26:193–194, where the faithful Spirit brings revelation to the Prophet's heart.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r2.claim: Mujahid says the Spirit is a created kind unlike angels, having human form, hands, feet, and heads; Abu Salih says they resemble people but are not people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الروح: خلق ليسوا بالملائكة على سورة بني آدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r3.claim: Some identify the Spirit as the Quran because polytheists asked who brought it; 42:52 calls revelation a spirit from God's command, since Quran gives life to hearts and souls toward good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: هو القرآن (¬3)، وذلك أن المشركين قالوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r4.claim: Others identify the Spirit as the animal soul, the most immediate sense in context; it may be named from wind or breath, as in Dhu al-Rumma's verse about reviving a fire by blowing and God's breathing His spirit into Adam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: هو روح الحيوان (¬3)، وهو الأظهر في الكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r5.claim: Another etymology derives Spirit from its movement, expansion, and spread through the body, illustrated by a broad-footed person, shallow wide bowl, and wine called rah for the body's motion and lightness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: سمي روحا لأنه يهتز وينبسط وينتشر في جميع البدن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r6.claim: Some say the Spirit is blood because losing blood causes death; others say it is inhaled air because a strangled person dies without it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p462/r6.anchor: فقال قوم: إن الروح هو الدم، ألا ترى أن من نزف دمه مات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r1.claim: Further views place the Spirit in the brain, in the blood, or throughout the body, with the last citing 14:17; the author calls these speculative because God has left the matter obscure.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r1.anchor: وقال آخرون: مسكنها الدماغ، وقيل: مسكنه الدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن بريدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r2.claim: Ibn Burayda says jinn, humans, angels, and devils cannot know the Spirit, and that the Prophet died without knowing it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r2.anchor: قال عبد الله بن بريدة: ما يبلغ الجن والإنس والملائكة والشياطين علم الروح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r3.claim: Farra says the Spirit is what sustains human life, whose knowledge God has not disclosed to any creature; min amri rabbi means from my Lord's knowledge, or alternatively it is a created thing belonging to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p469/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: الروح هو الذي يعيش به الإنسان، لم يخبر الله به أحدا من خلقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r1.claim: The small amount of human knowledge is relative to God's knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r1.anchor: أي: بالإضافة إلى علم الله تعالى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r2.claim: The Jews claimed to know everything because of what their Torah contained.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r2.anchor: وذلك أن اليهود كانت تدعى علم كل شيء بما في كتابهم التوراة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r3.claim: Little and much are relational terms: a thing is little beside what exceeds it and great beside what is less.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r3.anchor: وقليل وكثير لا يصلح إلا بالإضافة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.claim: Alternatively, the address may concern the Prophet and believers, whose knowledge of the spirit was not disclosed; the following threat to withdraw revelation supports this reading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p470/r4.anchor: لم يبين الله له ذلك، قال له:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r3.claim: The questioners are Jews asking about the spirit that gives the body life, its reality, manner, and place; God has disclosed this knowledge to no servant.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r3.anchor: { ويسألونك } يعني: اليهود { عن الروح } والروح: ما يحيا به البدن، سألوه عن ذلك وحقيقته وكيفيته، وموضعه من البدن

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r4.claim: The spirit is from God's knowledge, meaning people do not know it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r4.anchor: { قل الروح من أمر ربي } أي: من علم ربي، أي: إنكم لا تعلمونه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r5.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r5.claim: An alternative explanation says the spirit is from God's creation, meaning it is created by Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r5.anchor: وقيل: من خلق ربي، أي: إنه مخلوق له.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r6.claim: Although Jews claimed knowledge of everything from their scripture, their knowledge is slight beside God's.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:84-85/r6.anchor: وكانت اليهود تدعي علم كل شي بما في كتابهم، فقيل لهم: وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا بالإضافة إلى علم الله تعالى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r3.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r3.claim: Mujahid reports that some Jews met the Prophet while he rode his mule and asked him about the spirit, prompting this revelation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r3.anchor: يحيى، عن صاحب له، عن الأعمش، عن مجاهد، أن ناسا من اليهود لقوا نبي الله وهو على بغلته، فسألوه عن الروح

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r4.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi recounts that Quraysh sent envoys to Jewish scholars in Medina to ask about Muhammad; a Jewish scholar recognized the description as that of the expected prophet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r4.anchor: وفي تفسير الكلبي أن المشركين بعثوا رسلا إلى المدينة فقالوا لهم: سلوا اليهود عن محمد، وصفوا لهم نعته وقوله،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r5.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r5.claim: When Quraysh disparaged Muhammad as poor, orphaned, and lacking elite followers, the Jewish scholar replied that this matched their expected prophet.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r5.anchor: فقالت لهم رسل قريش: إنه فقير، عائل، يتيم، لم يتبعه من قومه من أهل الرأي أحد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r6.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r6.claim: After Quraysh accused him of great claims and mentioned Musaylima, the Jews advised three questions: the Cave, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the spirit; knowing the first two would verify prophethood, while the third was beyond ordinary knowledge.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r6.anchor: فقالت لهم اليهود: اذهبوا فسلوا صاحبكم عن خلال ثلاث، فإن الذي باليمامة قد عجز عنهن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r7.speaker: الكلبي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r7.claim: Quraysh’s envoys returned, told them the questions, and the Quraysh then approached the Prophet with the challenge.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p159/r7.anchor: فرجعت رسل قريش إليهم فأخبروهم بذلك، فأرسلوا إلى النبي فلقيهم، فقالوا: يابن عبد المطلب،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r1.claim: Asked about the three matters, the Prophet requested time for his Lord’s answer; Gabriel did not come for three days.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r1.anchor: فقال لهم رسول الله: «وما هن؟» . قالوا: أخبرنا عن أصحاب الكهف فإنا قد أخبرنا عنهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r2.claim: Gabriel explained that he descends only by God’s command, citing 19:64, and then delivered the answer about the spirit and its limited human knowledge.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r2.anchor: قال له جبريل: {وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك له ما بين أيدينا وما خلفنا وما بين ذلك وما كان ربك نسيا} [مريم: 64]

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r3.claim: The Prophet also recited the revelations about the Cave and Dhul-Qarnayn; Quraysh were amazed but Satan kept them from believing him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r3.anchor: ثم قال له جبريل: إن الله قال: {ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} [الإسراء: 85] .

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas explained the spirit once and then stopped interpreting it, as Qatada reports through Hisham.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r4.anchor: هشام، عن قتادة، أن ابن عباس فسر الروح مرة واحدة ثم كف عن تفسيرها.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r5.claim: Yahya tentatively says Hisham or someone else may have reported that Qatada too explained the spirit once and then stopped.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r5.anchor: وأحسب أن هشاما أو غيره ذكر أن قتادة فسرها مرة ثم كف

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r6.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r6.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the spirit as an immense angel beneath the Throne, with a human-shaped face and angelic body, guarding the angels by the Throne; 78:38 calls this angel the Spirit.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r6.anchor: وقال السدي: الروح ملك من الملائكة في السماء السابعة، ووجهه على صورة الإنسان وجسده على صورة الملائكة،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r7.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r7.claim: Hasan identifies the spirit as the Qur’an and takes its being from God’s command as being from His revelation.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r7.anchor: وتفسير الحسن أن الروح القرآن. قال: {قل الروح من أمر ربي} [الإسراء: 85] من وحي ربي

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r8.claim: The limited knowledge in the verse means the knowledge God gives people is small in comparison with His knowledge.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p160/r8.anchor: {وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا} [الإسراء: 85] ، أي: إن علمكم الذي أتاكم الله قليل في علم الله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r1.speaker: بعض أصحابه التابعين
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r1.claim: An unnamed Successor reported through al-Aʿmash that the spirit is a created being with hands and legs.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r1.anchor: وبلغني عن الأعمش، عن بعض أصحابه التابعين قال: الروح خلق من خلق الله لهم أيد وأرجل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r2.claim: Qatada says the Jews tested the Prophet with questions about the spirit, the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p161/r2.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: لقيت اليهود نبي الله فتعنتوه وسألوه عن الروح، وعن أصحاب الكهف، وعن ذي القرنين.

ELMALILI:17:85/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r1.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:17:85/r1.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s sira account, Quraysh sent Nadr ibn al-Harith and Uqba ibn Abi Mu‘ayt to Medina; Jews advised asking about the Cave Companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and spirit, which Torah left obscure. The Prophet answered two stories and gave a concise answer about spirit, so they regretted asking.
ELMALILI:17:85/r1.anchor: Siyerde İbn Abbas’tan nakledildiğine göre Kureyş Nadr b. Hâris ile

ELMALILI:17:85/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r2.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:17:85/r2.claim: Another report says Quraysh asked the Jews for a question to pose, they chose spirit, and this verse was revealed; this account treats the verse as Meccan.
ELMALILI:17:85/r2.anchor: Ahmed, Nesâî, Tirmizî ve Hâkim ve İbn Hibbân ve daha birtakımlarının İbn Abbas’tan tahrîcinde ise Kureyş Yehûde demişler ki

ELMALILI:17:85/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r3.speaker: Abdullah b. Mes‘ud
ELMALILI:17:85/r3.claim: A report in Bukhari and Muslim places the question in Medina: Jews asked the Prophet about spirit, he fell silent as revelation came, and then recited the verse.
ELMALILI:17:85/r3.anchor: Buhârî’de ve Müslim’de vesâirede tahric edildiğine göre Abdullah b. Mes‘ud radıyallâhu anh demiştir ki

ELMALILI:17:85/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r4.claim: The conflicting Meccan and Medinan reports led some to say that this verse was revealed twice, once in each place.
ELMALILI:17:85/r4.anchor: Bundan dolayı bazıları bu âyetin biri Mekke’de biri Medine’de olmak üzere iki defa nâzil olduğuna kāil olmuşlardır

ELMALILI:17:85/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r5.claim: Spirit can mean the source of movement, broadly a force contrasted with matter; in this sense even electricity or any motive force may be called spirit.
ELMALILI:17:85/r5.anchor: Hareket mebde’i mülâhazasıyla rûh, maddenin tam mukābili olarak kuvvet demek olur

ELMALILI:17:85/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r6.claim: Spirit can also mean the source of life: broadly it includes plant life, while its familiar narrower sense is animal life culminating in humans and includes plant life.
ELMALILI:17:85/r6.anchor: Birisi e‘am mânasıyla hayattır ki nebâtî hayâta da şâmil olur

ELMALILI:17:85/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r7.claim: In its most distinctive sense, spirit is the source of perception and consciousness, from sensation through knowledge, reason, will, and speech; its clearest manifestation is the human spirit.
ELMALILI:17:85/r7.anchor: Sonra idrak mebde’i, yani ihsâsa iktiran eden vicdân-ı basîtten marifet, ta‘akkul, ilim, irade, kelâm vesâire gibi en yüksek derecelere kadar ale’l-umûm şuur hâdisâtının

ELMALILI:17:85/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r8.claim: The human spirit distinguishes human knowledge from animal life and lets one know oneself and others and reach truth; Qur’an calls it God’s spirit breathed into Adam.
ELMALILI:17:85/r8.anchor: Nefs-i insânîyi rûh-i hayvânîden temyiz ettiren ve insânî marifeti

ELMALILI:17:85/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r9.claim: We know this spirit through hearing and through its effects in conscience, will, reasoning, and inner speech; all humans have a spark, although whether spirit and human self are identical is disputed.
ELMALILI:17:85/r9.anchor: Biz bunu kendisiyle duyar; vicdan, irade, ta‘akkul, kelâm-ı bâtınî gibi âsârıyla tanırız

ELMALILI:17:85/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r10.claim: Because humans remain ignorant of much while knowing something, the spirit is a source breathed into the self’s spiritual life as air, light, or heat is breathed into bodily life; its degree shapes disposition toward guidance or error.
ELMALILI:17:85/r10.anchor: mebde’-i idrak olan rûh, insanın hayât-ı cismâniyesinde bedenine nefh olunan hava, ziyâ, harâret gibi

ELMALILI:17:85/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r11.claim: Many commentators take min as explanatory or partitive and amr as affair: the spirit is a matter only God knows, an answer suited to asking why souls differ by God’s will.
ELMALILI:17:85/r11.anchor: Rûh, ancak Rabbimin bileceği iştendir, rûhun hakikati öyle umûrdandır ki ilmini Allah teâlâ kendisine tahsis etmiştir

ELMALILI:17:85/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85/r12.claim: If the question concerns spirit’s nature, the answer gives a definition: God’s command is His unconditioned creative act, saying be, an instantaneous act like a blink; some commentators choose this reading.
ELMALILI:17:85/r12.anchor: Rabbin emri, bir şeyi irade edince Allah’ın işi başka hiçbir şart ve sebebe muhtaç olmaksızın

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r1.claim: On this reading amr is annexed to its agent: initiatory min makes spirit a distinct simple substance produced by the command, while explanatory min makes it a special pure act or effect of that command.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r1.anchor: ibtidâiye olduğu takdirde rûh, emrin eseri olan basît

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r2.claim: To distinguish spirit from any created thing, he reads 7:54 as contrasting creation, which gives measure and brings matter and bodies into being, with command, which produces immaterial forces and affairs.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r2.anchor: Görülüyor ki bunda “emr” “halk”a tekabül ettirilmiştir. Bunda ise iki vecih vardır

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r3.claim: The creation-command distinction is illustrated by Adam being created from dust and then told to be.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r3.anchor: Nitekim Âdem hakkında خَلَقَهُۥ مِن تُرَابٍۢ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
