ELMALILI:17:85#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r4.claim: If amr means governance, it is God’s sovereignty and the acts that administer and influence all creatures, manifesting Lordship; creation provides the locus while command cultivates creatures by compulsion or choice.

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r5.claim: The attribution to Lord distinguishes spirit from the broad class of all forces; the particular phrase my Lord supplies its individual defining feature and its relation to the self.

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r6.claim: Spirit is an act from the Lord who owns and nurtures me, revealing myself and my Lord; spirit therefore involves self, command, and Lord, and self-awareness depends on this special relation.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r6.anchor: Demek ki bir rûh tasavvurunda esas şu üç şuurdur: Ene, emr, Rab. Ve rûh, işte eneye Rabbin bir te’sîr-i mahsûsu ile izâfetini ifade eden emirdir

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r7.claim: This answer corrects those who identify spirit with God or call God a spirit: neither the self nor spirit is Lord; spirit is a command belonging to the self’s Lord.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r7.anchor: Onun için مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّى cevâbında bu galatlar da tashih olunarak anlatılmıştır ki

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r8.claim: The first-person my in my Lord refers initially to the Prophet; the special divine relation to Muhammad also encompasses Gabriel, called the Holy and Trustworthy Spirit.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r8.anchor: hitâbında Rabbin muzâfun ileyhi olan nefs-i mütekellim zamîri olan

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r9.claim: For the Prophet, spirit is a command from the Lord who nurtures him, gives revelation, grants Isra and Mi‘raj and the Praised Station, and sends the Qur’an, through which he knows himself and God.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r9.anchor: Rûh beni terbiye eden, ezcümle bana vahiy ve risalet veren, beni İsrâ ile Mi‘râc’a i‘lâ eyleyen

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r10.claim: Human knowledge is not zero but remains little and relative: people know some truths and enough to know God and their duties, though not all depths of reality; knowledge of spirit is limited likewise.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r10.anchor: haktan bazı şeyler bilirsiniz amma hakikatin bütün derinliğiyle değil, bazı vücûh ile, rûhunuzun mertebesine göre

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r11.speaker: bazı müfessirîn
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r11.claim: Some commentators say the address about little knowledge is limited to the questioners because it more naturally completes the answer within the command to say.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r11.anchor: bu hitâbın suâli soranlara ait olduğunu söylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r12.claim: A report says the Jews asked whether the address was only for them; the Prophet answered that it meant both them and the Muslims, then explained that their knowledge was little relative to God’s and useful if acted upon.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r12.anchor: rivayet olunuyor ki Yehûd, bu cevabı işitince

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r13.claim: He concludes that the phrase is an independent continuation addressed to all humanity, not part of the command to say; all human knowledge is finite and relative to God’s infinite, encompassing knowledge.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r13.anchor: Şu hâlde bu hitap, قُلِ emrinde dâhil olmayıp istînâfen ona tezyil edilmiş bir cümle olarak bütün insanlara âm bir hitap demektir

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r14.claim: Teaching Adam all the names in 2:31 does not mean teaching all realities of the named things; this remains little knowledge relative to God and may ground the philosophical nominalist school.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r14.anchor: Âdem’e bütün esmânın tâlimi, bütün hakāyık-ı müsemmeyâtın tâlimi demek değildir

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r15.claim: Claims that the Qur’an explains everything mean everything people need in religion and law, not the realities of all things; the scope is relative.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r15.anchor: bütün eşyânın hakāyıkı mânasına olmayıp insanların din ve ahkâm nokta-i nazarından muhtaç oldukları her şey mânasına izâfî

ELMALILI:17:85#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r16.claim: Human knowledge is little beyond the subject of spirit too, since spirit is the means by which people know other things.
ELMALILI:17:85#2/r16.anchor: İlm-i beşerin kılleti yalnız ilm-i rûh nokta-i nazarından zannedilmemelidir

ELMALILI:17:85#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r1.claim: The address honors humans by granting them a share of knowledge while breaking scientific pride and calling them to humility before God.
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r1.anchor: Bu hitapta insanlara ilimden hisse veren bir şeref ve aynı zamanda beşerin gurûr-ı ilmîsini kıran bir darbe

ELMALILI:17:85#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r2.claim: Divine knowledge’s infinity is not a reason for despair about human learning; it enables limitless progress, so people should pursue knowledge with love and faith while remaining humble.
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r2.anchor: ilmin nâmütenâhîliği insanlar için her hususta ilmin imkânını selb eden bir yeis delîli değil, ilimde terakkī imkânının nâmütenâhîliğini temin eden bir mebde’-i marifettir

ELMALILI:17:85#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r3.claim: However far people advance, human knowledge remains tiny beside God’s knowledge, like a drop beside the seas, and they must never be proud.
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r3.anchor: ilm-i beşerin az yine az, ilmullâha nisbetle bir katrenin denizlere nisbetinden bile az olduğunu bilerek hiçbir zaman mağrur olmamak lâzımdır

ELMALILI:17:85#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r4.claim: Human knowledge is given but can be taken away instantly, even at its highest spiritual degree; this truth prepares the warning that follows in 17:86.
ELMALILI:17:85#3/r4.anchor: ilm-i beşer verilme olduğu gibi kābil-i zevâldir de. Bir insana en büyük rûhun en yüksek mertebe-i ilmin verildiği de farz edilse

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r1.claim: Ruh means life, breath, or power; as a technical term it is usually understood as the immaterial essence that makes a human what they are, though early theologians sometimes defined it as a subtle body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r1.anchor: Terim olarak çoğunlukla “bedenin zıddı olan, yani insanın mânevî cevherini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r2.claim: The Qur’an uses ruh for Gabriel, revelation, and the life-giving force or human spiritual essence.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r2.anchor: Kelimenin Kur’an’da başlıca üç anlamda kullanıldığı söylenebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r3.speaker: müfessirlerin büyük çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r3.claim: Although interpreters also identify this ruh as Gabriel, a named angel, Jesus, revelation, the Qur’an, or creation, most commentators understand it here as the spiritual essence that makes a human alive and governs the body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r3.anchor: müfessirlerin büyük çoğunluğu buradaki ruhu, “insanı canlı varlık yapan, bedeni yöneten

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r4.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r4.claim: Shawkani says ruh is the human’s essential self; questioners asked about it because knowing the essence matters more than knowing its states and qualities.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r4.anchor: Şevkânî, ruhun insanı insan yapan asıl ve öz varlık olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r5.claim: Philosophy, theology, and ethics often use nafs for ruh in this sense; Muslims affirm such a soul, but scholars differ about its nature.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r5.anchor: Daha çok felsefe, kelâm ve ahlâk kitaplarında bu anlamdaki ruh için nefis

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r6.claim: Some theologians call the soul a subtle body like air; most scholars, especially philosophers, regard it as an independent immaterial reality, individually distinctive and the basis of personal responsibility.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r6.anchor: bazı kelâm âlimleri ruhu hava gibi “latîf bir cisim” kabul ederken başta filozoflar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r7.claim: One argument for the soul is that the body changes and develops while a person’s identity remains stable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r7.anchor: İnsanın bedeni değişmekte, gelişmekte, başkalaşmaktadır; halbuki onun kişiliği daima aynı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r8.claim: A second argument is that moral and legal responsibility would make no sense without a soul, unlike inanimate objects.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r8.anchor: Herkes, insanın ahlâkî, hukukî yönden sorumluluğunu kabul eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r9.claim: A third argument is that consciousness, will, and freedom to choose are not bodily properties; the soul exercises them and moves or stops the body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r9.anchor: İnsandaki bilinç, irade, seçme özgürlüğü gibi yetenek ve kapasitelerin bedene ait

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r10.claim: A fourth argument is that human superiority over physically stronger beings comes from the soul’s reason, mind, judgment, will, and freedom to choose.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r10.anchor: akıl, zihin, muhâkeme, irade, seçme ve karar verme özgürlüğü gibi ruha ait yeteneklerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r11.claim: A fifth argument is that everyone accepts a real human ceases to exist as a person at death because the soul has left the body.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r11.anchor: ölümle birlikte artık cesedin insan olarak varlığının son bulduğunu herkes kabul eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r12.claim: Despite these arguments, science has not proved the soul’s existence or fully grasped its nature; the verse says humans have been given little knowledge about it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r12.anchor: ruhun varlığını bilimsel ölçülerle kanıtlamak ve mahiyetini tam olarak kavramak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r13.claim: Another broad interpretation takes “you have been given little knowledge” to mean all people possess little knowledge in every field relative to God’s limitless knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:85/r13.anchor: Bütün insanlara her konuda az bir bilgi verildi

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that in Medina, while walking with the Prophet, Quraysh asked him about the Spirit; after a pause for revelation, he recited that the Spirit is from God's command.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r2.anchor: مسعود قال كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالمدينة وهو متوكىء على عسيب

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked Jews what to ask the Prophet, and they suggested the Spirit; the verse was revealed in answer.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r3.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي عن ابن عباس قال قالت قريش لليهود علمونا شيئا نسأل هذا الرجل فقالوا سلوه عن الروح

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وابن حجر
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Hajar reconcile the two Spirit reports by repeated revelation; Ibn Hajar also suggests the Prophet's silence anticipated further clarification, while Suyuti prefers Ibn Masʿud's firsthand report as more reliable than Ibn Abbas's.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p139#2/r4.anchor: قلت ويرجح ما في الصحيح بأن راوية حاضر القصة بخلاف ابن عباس

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r2.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he was in a Medina field; revelation answered that the spirit is from God's command and human knowledge is little. Al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: إني مع النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في حرث بالمدينة وهو متكئ على عسيب، فمر بنا ناس من اليهود

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r3.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r3.claim: ʿIkrima reports Ibn ʿAbbās's account that Quraysh asked Jews for a question to pose, and they told them to ask about the spirit.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r3.anchor: (2) - وقال عكرمة عن ابن عباس: قالت قريش لليهود: اعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه هذا الرجل، فقالوا: سلوه عن الروح

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r4.claim: Commentators say Jews proposed a three-part test about the spirit, the youths of old, and a man reaching east and west: answering all or none disqualified Muhammad, while answering some identified him as prophet; revelations then addressed each question.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p291/r4.anchor: وقال المفسرون: إن اليهود اجتمعوا فقالوا لقريش حين سألوهم عن شأن محمد وحاله سلوا محمدا عن الروح، وعن فتية فقدوا

SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r1.claim: ‘Of knowledge’ attaches to ‘you were given’; it cannot be an omitted circumstantial of ‘little,’ because material within إلا’s scope cannot precede it.
SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { من العلم }: متعلق ب " أوتيتم " ، ولا يجوز تعلقه بمحذوف على أنه حال من " قليلا "؛

SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r2.speaker: عبد الله والأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r2.claim: ‘Abdullah and al-A‘mash read ‘and they were not given’ with a third-person plural pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:17:85/r2.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله والأعمش " وما أوتوا " بضمير الغيبة.

ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r2.claim: The Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit, expecting an answer outside what he had been taught; God told him it belongs to God’s command.
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r2.anchor: سألت إليهود النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -عن الروح وهم مقدرون أن يجيبهم بغير ما علم من تفسيرها، فأعلمهم أن الروح من أمر الله.

ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r3.claim: The Jews cited their Torah and the verse about whoever receives wisdom receiving great good; God explains that Torah knowledge is little relative to His knowledge.
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r3.anchor: فقالوا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قد أوتينا التوراة، وفيها الحكمة، وقد تلوت:

ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r4.claim: ‘Little’ and ‘much’ are comparative terms: something is little only in relation to something greater, and much in relation to something lesser.
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r4.anchor:
وقليل وكثير لا يصح إلا بالإضافة، فإنما يقل الشيء عندما يعلم أكثر
منه، وكذلك يكثر عند معلوم هو أقل منه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r5.claim: One interpretation identifies the spirit as Gabriel, supported by the verse saying the Faithful Spirit brought it to the Prophet’s heart.
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r5.anchor:
وقد اختلف الناس في تفسير الروح فقيل إن الروح جبريل ومن تأول
ذلك فدليله قوله: (نزل به الروح الأمين (193) على قلبك).

ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r6.claim: Another interpretation says the spirit is a created being for Adam’s descendants in heaven.
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r6.anchor: وقيل إن الروح خلق لخلق بني آدم في السماء

ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r7.claim: Some exegetes identify the spirit with the Qur’an, citing revelation of a spirit from God’s command; the Qur’an gives life to hearts and souls through the good they attain with God.
ZAJJAJ:v3p257/r7.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: إن الروح إنما يعنى به القرآن.

ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r1.speaker: some commentators
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r1.claim: Some commentators understand ruh here specifically as the revelation of the Qur'an.
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r1.anchor: Some commentators are of the opinion that it refers here, specifically, to the revelation of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r2.speaker: other commentators
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r2.claim: Other commentators understand ruh as the human soul.
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r2.anchor: others understand by it the "soul", in particular the soul of man

ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r3.claim: Asad rejects the soul interpretation because the surrounding verses explicitly concern the Qur'an and divine revelation.
ASAD-NOTES:17:85#n101/r3.anchor: This latter interpretation is, however, unconvincing inasmuch as the preceding as well as the subsequent verses relate explicitly to the Qur'an

QIRAAT-ER:17:85:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:85:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:85:2#1/r1.claim: Some readers pronounce a full hamza where standard Hafs uses tashīl; meaning does not change.
QIRAAT-ER:17:85:2#1/r1.anchor: Without hamza softening — standard Hafs has tashīl (softened hamza); some readers pronounce full hamza

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r1.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan identify the Spirit as Gabriel; Qatāda adds that Ibn ʿAbbās kept this interpretation private.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة والحسن في قوله تعالى ﴿ ويسألونك عن الروح ﴾ قال هو جبريل قال قتادة وكان ابن عباس يكتمه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the Spirit as one angel with ten thousand wings, many faces, and tongues, eyes, and lips glorifying God until the Resurrection.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r2.anchor: عن عطاء عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ ويسألونك عن الروح قل الروح من أمر ربي ﴾ قال هو ملك واحد له عشرة آلاف جناح

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the span between Gabriel's shoulders equals five hundred years of a bird's flight.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ما بين منكبي جبريل خفق طائر خمس مائة عام

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Preserved Tablet is a hundred years' journey, with red-ruby covers; God looks into it 360 times daily, erasing and confirming what He wills, while the Mother of the Book remains with Him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p388#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال لله لوح محفوظ مسيرة مائة عام له دفتان من ياقوت أحمر والدفتان لوحان الله ينظر فيه كل يوم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r1.speaker: أبو بكر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r1.claim: Abu Bakr called the verse about God forgiving sin and accepting repentance the most hopeful, because forgiveness precedes acceptance of repentance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r1.anchor: لم أر في القرآن آية أرجى من التي فيها غافر الذنب وقابل التوب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r2.speaker: عثمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r2.claim: Uthman called the command to tell God's servants He is the Forgiving, Merciful the most hopeful verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r2.anchor: لم أر آية أرجى من نبئ عبادي أني أنا الغفور الرحيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r3.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r3.claim: Ali called the verse telling sinful servants not to despair of God's mercy the most hopeful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r3.anchor: لم أر آية أرجى من يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r4.speaker: القرطبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi is also reported to identify the verse about believers who did not mix faith with wrongdoing as most hopeful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r4.anchor: لم أر آية أرجى من الذين آمنوا ولم يلبسوا إيمانهم بظلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r5.claim: Al-Razi says souls differ: pure, luminous souls receive increasing light from the Qur'an, while dark souls find misguidance and punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r5.anchor: الأرواح والنفوس مختلفة بماهيتها فبعضها مشرقة صافية يظهر فيها من القرآن نور على نور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r6.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he leaned on a palm stalk; he remained silent as revelation came, then this verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r6.anchor: فسكت ثم ماج فأمسكت بيدي على جبهته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r7.speaker: اليهود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r7.claim: A report says Jews told Quraysh to ask about the spirit, the young men of old, and a man who reached east and west; answering all or none would discredit the Prophet, while answering some and declining some would confirm him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r7.anchor: وروي أن يهود قالوا لقريش: سلوه عن الروح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r8.claim: Versions differ about whether the test was to answer all three or to decline the spirit question; the cave and Dhul-Qarnayn passages were also revealed in response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r8.anchor: فنزل في شأن الفتية أم حسبت أن أصحاب الكهف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r9.claim: Ibn Masud's report points to a Medinan setting, whereas the Quraysh question report points to a Meccan setting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r9.anchor: والظاهر من حديث ابن مسعود أن الآية مدنية ومن سؤال قريش أنها مكية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r10.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r10.claim: The majority take ruh here as the life-giving spirit in animals, a generic term and the apparent sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r10.anchor: والروح على قول الجمهور هنا الروح التي في الحيوان وهو اسم جنس وهو الظاهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r11.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r11.claim: Qatada says the spirit is Gabriel, and reports that Ibn Abbas kept this interpretation concealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p105/r11.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو جبريل عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r1.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r1.claim: Ali is said to have identified the spirit as an angel, with descriptions that Abu Hayyan says are unsoundly attributed to him.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r2.claim: Other interpretations identify the spirit as the Qur'an, a great spiritual creature greater than an angel, or a divine troop that eats and has limbs.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r3.speaker: أبو صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r3.claim: Abu Salih describes the spirits as creatures like Adam but not human, with limbs; each angel descending from heaven is accompanied by one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r3.anchor: وقال أبو صالح خلق كخلق آدم وليسوا بني آدم لهم أيد وأرجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers the first interpretation, the human spirit; the question concerns its essence or how it enters and animates the body, which only God knows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r4.anchor: والصحيح من هذه الأقوال القول الأول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects a Sufi writer's claim that ordinary people receive only the answer that spirit is from God's command while initiates know its reality; Muslim scholars agree the spirit is created.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r5.anchor: وأجمع علماء الإسلام على أن الروح مخلوقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r6.claim: Philosophical unbelievers and many who affiliate with Islam say the spirit is eternal; reports count as many as seventy views and dispute whether spirit and soul are identical.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r6.anchor: وذهب كفرة الفلاسفة وكثير ممن ينتمي إلى الإسلام إلى أنها قديمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r7.claim: Min amri rabbi means God's act in creating the spirit, which shows it is originated; alternatively amr means one of God's affairs whose knowledge He reserves.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r8.claim: Other glosses take the spirit as revelation from God or God's knowledge; the revelation reading fits those who identify it with the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r8.anchor: وقيل: من وحي ربي، وكلامه ليس من كلام البشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the address about limited knowledge is to all people, since the command to answer is for the whole world and human knowledge is bounded.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r9.anchor: وهذا هو الصحيح لأن قوله قل الروح إنما هو أمر بالقول لجميع العالم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود والأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r10.claim: Ibn Masud and al-Amash read the phrase in the third person, referring to the questioners.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p106/r10.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله بن مسعود والأعمش: وما أوتوا

TABATABAI:16:1-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r1.claim: The Spirit is an independent living, knowing, powerful existent, not an attribute or state inhering in things; the separation of Spirit from angels in other verses supports this.
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r1.anchor: يوم يقوم الروح والملائكة صفا النبأ 38، وقوله تعرج الملائكة والروح إليه المعارج 4 وغيرهما أنه موجود مستقل ذو حياة وعلم وقدرة

TABATABAI:16:1-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r2.claim: The Spirit belongs to God's Command; the Command is His creative word by which He brings things into existence, meaning existence bestowed directly from Him without matter, time, or place.
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r2.anchor: أنه من سنخ أمره، وعرف أيضا أمره بمثل قوله إنما أمره إذا أراد شيئا أن يقول له كن فيكون

TABATABAI:16:1-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r3.claim: The description of the Command as one, like a glance, marks an event without gradual process, matter, or motion.
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r3.anchor: وما أمرنا إلا واحدة كلمح بالبصر القمر 50، فإن هذا التعبير إنما يورد فيما لا تدريج فيه أي لا مادة ولا حركة له

TABATABAI:16:1-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r4.claim: The Spirit is the word of life that God casts into things to make them live by His will, and revelation to the Prophet is consequently called Spirit.
TABATABAI:16:1-21/r4.anchor: فتحصل أن الروح كلمة الحياة التي يلقيها الله سبحانه إلى الأشياء فيحييها بمشيئته، ولذلك سماه وحيا وعد إلقاءه وإنزاله على نبيه إيحاء

BURHAN:v3p53/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p53/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p53/r1.claim: One report says Jews challenged the Prophet’s statement that people had little knowledge, citing the Torah’s divine words, rulings, light, and guidance; he replied that the Torah was little of much, and the verse about the sea as ink was revealed.
BURHAN:v3p53/r1.anchor: سببها أن اليهود جاءوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURHAN:v2p165/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p165/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p165/r2.claim: A third class comprises matters known only to God, including the spirit, the Hour, rain, wombs, disconnected letters, and every ambiguous verse according to the people of truth; interpretation needs transmitted authority.
BURHAN:v2p165/r2.anchor: نحو الآى المتضمنة قيام الساعة ونزول الغيث وما فى الأرحام وتفسير الروح والحروف المقطعة

BURHAN:v2p165/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p165/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p165/r3.claim: For what God has reserved, interpretation is admissible only through Qur'anic text, the Prophet's explanation, or consensus; without one of these, the matter remains God's alone.
BURHAN:v2p165/r3.anchor: ولا طريق إلى ذلك إلا بالتوقيف من أحد ثلاثة أوجه إما نص من التنزيل أو بيان من النبى

BURHAN:v2p165/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p165/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p165/r4.claim: A fourth class is open to scholarly reasoning and is generally called interpretation: the exegete transmits, while the interpreter derives rulings, clarifies ambiguity, and specifies general wording.
BURHAN:v2p165/r4.anchor: فالمفسر ناقل والمؤول مستنبط وذلك استنباط الأحكام وبيان المجمل وتخصيص العموم

BURHAN:v2p165/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p165/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p165/r5.claim: Scholars may exercise judgment over words with multiple possible meanings, but must rely on evidence and indications rather than bare personal opinion.
BURHAN:v2p165/r5.anchor: وكل لفظ احتمل معنيين فصاعدا فهو الذى لا يجوز لغير العلماء الاجتهاد فيه وعلى العلماء اعتماد الشواهد والدلائل

BURHAN:v2p165/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p165/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p165/r6.claim: When one of two possible meanings is more apparent, it governs unless evidence shows that the less apparent meaning is intended.
BURHAN:v2p165/r6.anchor: أن يكون أحدهما أظهر من الآخر فيجب الحمل على الظاهر إلا أن يعوم دليل على أن المراد هو الخفي

BURHAN:v4p44/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p44/r3.speaker: صاحب الإيضاح
BURHAN:v4p44/r3.claim: The Jews asked to confound the Prophet because spirit can denote the human spirit, Gabriel, another angel, a class of angels, the Qur’an, or Jesus; the general answer frustrates their trap.
BURHAN:v4p44/r3.anchor: إن اليهود إنما سألوا تعجيزا وتغليظا إذا كان الروح يقال بالاشتراك

BURHAN:v4p44/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p44/r4.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p44/r4.claim: One view says they asked whether the spirit is created; saying it is from the Lord’s command answers that it is God’s act and creation.
BURHAN:v4p44/r4.anchor: وقيل إنما سألوا عن الروح هل هي محدثة مخلوقة أم ليست كذلك فأجابهم بأنها من أمر الله

BURHAN:v4p44/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p44/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v4p44/r5.claim: Another view identifies the spirit as the Qur’an, which God revealed to the Prophet as evidence of his truth, beyond the work or capacity of creatures.
BURHAN:v4p44/r5.anchor: وقيل أنهم سالوه عن الروح الذي هو في القرآن فقد سمى الله القرآن روحا في مواضع من الكتاب

BURHAN:v4p44/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p44/r6.speaker: الحسن البصري
BURHAN:v4p44/r6.claim: Al-Murtaḍā transmits this Qur’an interpretation from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and supports it with the next verse: God could remove what He revealed, showing the Qur’an is from His command.
BURHAN:v4p44/r6.anchor: وحكاه الشريف المرتضى في الغرر ( 2 ) عن الحسن البصري قال

ITQAN:v4p480/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p480/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p480/r3.claim: Matters of the unseen, the Hour, the spirit, disconnected letters, and other ambiguous passages are known only to God according to the orthodox; interpretation requires transmitted evidence or consensus.
ITQAN:v4p480/r3.anchor: وأما ما لا يعلمه إلا الله تعالى فهو ما يجري مجرى الغيوب نحو الآي المتضمنة قيام الساعة وتفسير الروح والحروف المقطعة

ITQAN:v2p414/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p414/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p414/r18.claim: Rūḥ can mean the spirit that inhabits the body, the sense raised by the question about the rūḥ.

ITQAN:v1p49/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p49/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p49/r5.claim: The sūra's cited Medinan exceptions include the Spirit question, the passage about the unbelievers nearly tempting the Prophet, the challenge to bring a similar Qur'an, the vision, and 'those given knowledge before it'.
ITQAN:v1p49/r5.anchor: الإسراء استثني منها ﴿ ويسألونك عن الروح ﴾ الآية لما أخرج البخاري عن ابن مسعود

ITQAN:v1p96/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p96/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p96/r3.claim: When two sound occasion reports conflict, al-Suyuti prefers the one whose transmitter witnessed the event. Ibn Masud's Bukhari account places the Spirit question in Medina among Jews, outweighing Ibn Abbas's report that Quraysh asked Jews for a question and implies Mecca; Bukhari's report is also stronger.
ITQAN:v1p96/r3.anchor: وقد رجح بأن ما رواه البخاري أصح من غيره وبأن ابن مسعود كان حاضر القصة

ITQAN:v2p575/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p575/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p575/r1.claim: A question may be left without a fully specified answer when the questioner seeks only to provoke, as with the answer about the Spirit being from God's command.
ITQAN:v2p575/r1.anchor: قد يعدل عن الجواب أصلا إذا كان السائل قصده التعنت

ITQAN:v2p575/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p575/r2.speaker: صاحب الإفصاح
ITQAN:v2p575/r2.claim: The Jews meant to confound the Prophet because rūḥ can denote the human soul, Qur'an, Jesus, Gabriel, another angel, or a class of angels; the deliberately general answer defeated their trap since any specific sense could be rejected.
ITQAN:v2p575/r2.anchor: قال صاحب الإفصاح إنما سأل اليهود تعجيزا وتغليظا إذ كان الروح يقال بالاشتراك على روح الإنسان والقرآن وعيسى

ITQAN:v2p578/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p578/r1.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p578/r1.claim: Al-Raghib says an information-seeking question may take its second object directly or with ʿan, more often with ʿan, as in the Spirit question.
ITQAN:v2p578/r1.anchor: قال الراغب السؤال إذا كان للتعريف تعدى إلى المفعول الثاني

ITQAN:v1p18/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p18/r1.claim: Human learning cannot exhaust the Qur’an’s sciences; God placed within it knowledge and guidance from which every discipline draws.
ITQAN:v1p18/r1.anchor: وإن كتابنا القرآن لهو مفجر العلوم ومنبعها ودائرة شمسها ومطلعها أودع فيه سبحانه وتعالى علم كل شيء

ITQAN:v1p18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p18/r2.claim: The jurist derives rulings, the grammarian builds rules of syntax, and the rhetorician learns eloquence and composition from the Qur’an; it also contains stories, admonitions, and parables.
ITQAN:v1p18/r2.anchor: فالفقيه يستنبط منه الأحكام ويستخرج حكم الحلال والحرام والنحوي يبني منه قواعد إعرابه

ITQAN:v1p18/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p18/r3.claim: The Qur’an’s eloquent wording, powerful style, and inimitable arrangement overwhelm minds and hearts, and only God can produce such arrangement.
ITQAN:v1p18/r3.anchor: هذا مع فصاحة لفظ وبلاغة أسلوب تبهر العقول وتسلب القلوب وإعجاز نظم لا يقدر عليه إلا علام الغيوب

DAMGHANI:v1p212/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p212/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p212/r4.claim: In this verse, rūḥ means the life present in animals and other living beings.
DAMGHANI:v1p212/r4.anchor: السادس : الروح يعني الحياة في الحيوان وذوات الأرواح قوله تعالى في سورة الإسراء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r1.claim: Ibn Qutayba says rūḥ, rawḥ, and rīḥ share an origin and have closely related meanings differentiated through their vowel patterns.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الروح والروح والريح : من أصل واحد اكتنفته معان تقاربت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r2.claim: He compares this to related forms for fire/light, inclination, the tongue, and carrying or pregnancy, whose vowel differences distinguish disposition, action, eloquence, blame, language, or what is borne.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r2.anchor: والنار والنور من أصل واحد ، كما قالوا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r3.claim: Breath used to revive a fire is called rūḥ because it is a wind that comes from the soul; Dhu al-Rumma’s poem uses rūḥ for blowing on the fire.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r3.anchor: ويقال للنفخ [ روح ] لأنه ريح خرج عن الروح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r4.claim: The poem’s glossary calls ṭalsāʾ a dirty rag or tinder, says to regulate the breath neither strongly nor weakly, and explains fine and thick kindling.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r4.anchor: والطلساء : خرقة وسخة ، وهي الحراق . والروح : النفخ

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r5.claim: One Quranic sense is the spirit of living beings, as in the question about the spirit and the creation of Adam.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p321#2/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير [ أن ] الروح في القرآن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r11.claim: The source says ambiguity can sometimes be beneficial, as when God left the answer about the spirit unexplained.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p108/r11.anchor: بل قد تكون المصلحة تارة في الإبهام وتارة في التبيين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r1.claim: روح and ريح share an origin and have closely related senses distinguished by changes in the word pattern or vowel, as in ميل, لسن, and حمل.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r1.anchor: والريح والروح: من أصل واحد اكتنفته معان تقاربت، فبني لكل معنى اسم من ذلك الأصل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r2.claim: روح can denote the soul of a body, which God takes at death.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r2.anchor: وأما الروح: فروح الأجسام الذي يقبضه الله عند الممات

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r3.claim: روح can refer to Gabriel: the Spirit of holiness and the trustworthy Spirit are identified as Gabriel.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r3.anchor: والروح: جبريل عليه السلام. قال الله تعالى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r4.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r4.claim: Commentators identify the Spirit who stands with the angels as a great angel who stands alone in one rank while the angels form another.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r4.anchor: والروح- فيما ذكر المفسرون-: ملك عظيم من ملائكة الله

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r5.claim: Angels are called روحانيون because they are spirits; the alif-and-nun ending marks their created nature, like رقباني and شعراني.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r5.anchor: ويقال للملائكة: الروحانيون، لأنهم أرواح، نسبوا إلى الروح- بالألف والنون-

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r6.claim: روح can mean breath or blowing, since wind exits from the spirit; in Dhu al-Rumma’s poem أحيها بروحك means revive the fire by blowing on it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p265/r6.anchor: والروح: النفخ، سمي روحا لأنه ريح تخرج عن الروح. قال ذو الرمة

IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r1.claim: After the Prophet came to Medina, Jewish scholars asked whether the statement about little knowledge addressed them or Muhammad's people; he said neither, and they objected that Torah contains all things.
IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وحدثت عن ابن عباس، أنه قال: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة

IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r2.claim: The Prophet answered that the Torah's knowledge is little beside God's knowledge, though it is enough for its holders if they follow it; 31:27 illustrates that God's words cannot be exhausted, and the Torah is a small part of His knowledge.
IBNHISHAM:v1p308#2/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنها في علم الله قليل، وعندكم في ذلك ما يكفيكم لو أقمتموه

BINTSHATI:v2p9/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r1.claim: Reports about occasions of revelation often mistakenly attach a verse to whatever someone thought caused it; the claimed cause is not necessarily indispensable to revelation.
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r1.anchor: وهذا هو معنى قول علماء القرآن: إن المرويات في أسباب النزول يكثر فيها الوهم. ونقدر معه أن السببية فيها ليست بمعنى العلية

BINTSHATI:v2p9/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r2.claim: The default is to apply a verse’s general wording unless explicit text or clear contextual evidence requires considering the specific occasion.
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r2.anchor: وأن العبرة في كل حال، بعموم اللفظ

BINTSHATI:v2p9/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r3.claim: The order of revelation also matters for understanding the Qur’an’s overall context, word meanings, and rhetorical features across the muṣḥaf.
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r3.anchor: والأخرى: أن ترتيب النزول موضع اعتبار كذلك، لفهم السياق العام لما نتدبر من آيات القرآن

BINTSHATI:v2p9/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r4.claim: Tafsīr cannot supply a word that is equivalent or synonymous with a Qur’anic word in its setting; humans cannot produce a comparable verse.
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r4.anchor: لا يعني بحال ما، تقديم كلمة يمكن أن تقوم مقام الكلمة القرآنية في سياقها، على وجه المماثلة والترداف

BINTSHATI:v2p9/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r5.claim: Tafsīr is only an effort to understand and explain approximately; the lack of an equivalent helps explain exegetes’ lengthy discussions and many interpretive possibilities.
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r5.anchor: التفسير ليس إلا محاولة للفهم على وجه الشرح والتقريب، بالكلمات المفسرة

BINTSHATI:v2p9/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r6.claim: The author acknowledges that her effort is limited and leaves future generations of scholars and students an open field to discover what she could not.
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r6.anchor: على تدبر كتابنا الأكبر فتدرك منه ما فاتنا أن ندركه

BINTSHATI:v2p9/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r7.claim: The verse that says human knowledge is only a little underscores the limits of human effort and the Qur’an’s inexhaustible secrets.
BINTSHATI:v2p9/r7.anchor: ويبقى من أسراره ما يفوت ظاقة البشر

BUKHARI:125/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:125/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BUKHARI:125/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the Spirit; after pausing for revelation, he answered that it is from God’s command and human knowledge is limited.
BUKHARI:125/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ بَيْنَا أَنَا أَمْشِي، مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فِي خَرِبِ الْمَدِينَةِ

BUKHARI:4721/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4721/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BUKHARI:4721/r1.claim: Ibn Masud recounts Jews asking about the Spirit; the Prophet withholds an answer while revelation comes, then recites that the Spirit is from God’s command and human knowledge is limited.
BUKHARI:4721/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ بَيْنَا أَنَا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ

BUKHARI:7297/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7297/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BUKHARI:7297/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the Spirit; he recognized the Prophet receiving revelation, after which the Prophet said the Spirit is from his Lord’s command.
BUKHARI:7297/r1.anchor: عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ قَالَ كُنْتُ مَعَ النَّبِيِّ

BUKHARI:7456/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7456/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BUKHARI:7456/r1.claim: Ibn Masud recounts that Jews asked about the Spirit despite some advising against it; the Prophet answered that it is from God’s command and human knowledge is limited.
BUKHARI:7456/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، قَالَ كُنْتُ أَمْشِي مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم

BUKHARI:7462/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7462/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BUKHARI:7462/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports a Jew asking the Prophet about the Spirit; after silence and revelation, the Prophet answers that it is from God’s command and that human knowledge is limited.
BUKHARI:7462/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ، قَالَ بَيْنَا أَنَا أَمْشِي، مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم

BUKHARI:7462/r2.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7462/r2.speaker: الأعمش
BUKHARI:7462/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash says their recitation has “they were given little knowledge” in the third person, rather than the verse’s second-person “you were given little knowledge.”

IBNHIBBAN:97/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:97/r1.speaker: عبد الله
IBNHIBBAN:97/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit while he was in a Medina garden, and revelation instructed him to answer that the spirit is from God’s command and human knowledge is slight.
IBNHIBBAN:97/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: "بينما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض حيطان المدينة متوكئا على عسيب إذ جاءته اليهود فسألته عن الروح

IBNHIBBAN:97/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:97/r2.speaker: author
IBNHIBBAN:97/r2.claim: Ibn Ḥibbān presents the report as evidence that a learned person may withhold some knowledge when he knows listeners’ hearts cannot bear it.
IBNHIBBAN:97/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: "بينما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في بعض حيطان المدينة متوكئا على عسيب إذ جاءته اليهود فسألته عن الروح

IBNHIBBAN:98/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:98/r1.speaker: عبد الله
IBNHIBBAN:98/r1.claim: A second Ibn Masʿūd account says Jews debated whether to ask about the spirit; the Prophet paused for revelation, then recited the verse’s answer.
IBNHIBBAN:98/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: كنت أمشي مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث1 بالمدينة وهو متكئ على عسيب فمر بنفر من اليهود

IBNHIBBAN:99/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:99/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNHIBBAN:99/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Quraysh asked Jews for a question to pose to Muhammad; after the spirit answer, they objected that Torah gave them much knowledge, and the verse about the sea as ink followed.
IBNHIBBAN:99/r1.anchor: عن بن عباس قال قالت قريش لليهود أعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه هذا الرجل فقالوا سلوه عن الروح

MUSLIM:7059/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7059/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
MUSLIM:7059/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit; he paused for revelation, then answered that the spirit is by God’s command and human knowledge is slight.
MUSLIM:7059/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال بينما أنا أمشي، مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث وهو متكئ على عسيب إذ مر بنفر من اليهود

MUSLIM:7060/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7060/r1.speaker: author
MUSLIM:7060/r1.claim: Muslim notes a wording difference in this parallel report: Wakiʿ’s transmission has “you were given,” while ʿIsa ibn Yunus’s has “they were given.”
MUSLIM:7060/r1.anchor: في حديث وكيع وما أوتيتم من العلم إلا قليلا

MUSLIM:7061/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7061/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
MUSLIM:7061/r1.claim: Ibn Masud’s parallel account places the Prophet in a date grove leaning on a palm stalk; it repeats the question about the spirit and the response that knowledge is limited.
MUSLIM:7061/r1.anchor: عن مسروق، عن عبد الله، قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في نخل يتوكأ على عسيب

MUSNAD-AHMAD:2309/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2309/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2309/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Quraysh asked the Jews for a test question; they proposed asking Muhammad about the spirit, and 17:85 was revealed. After the Jews claimed abundant knowledge through the Torah, 18:109 was revealed about God's inexhaustible words.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:2309/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " قالت قريش لليهود: أعطونا شيئا نسأل عنه هذا الرجل، فقالوا: سلوه عن الروح

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3688/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3688/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3688/r1.claim: Ibn Masud recalls Jews in a Medina field asking the Prophet about the spirit; he leaned on his staff, and Ibn Masud thought revelation was coming before the Prophet recited 17:85.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3688/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: " كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث بالمدينة، وهو متكئ

MUSNAD-AHMAD:3898/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3898/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3898/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit; after falling silent, he recited 17:85 to them.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:3898/r1.anchor: عن مسروق، عن عبد الله، قال: بينما النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث، متوكئا على عسيب

MUSNAD-AHMAD:4248/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4248/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4248/r1.claim: Ibn Masud recounts Jews asking the Prophet what the spirit is; he thought revelation came before the Prophet recited 17:85, and some Jews said they had warned against asking.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4248/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، في حرث بالمدينة، فمر على قوم من اليهود

TIRMIDHI:3140/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3140/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TIRMIDHI:3140/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Quraysh, prompted by Jews, asked the Prophet about the spirit and 17:85 was revealed; after they claimed the Torah gave them much knowledge, God revealed that the sea would run out before His words.

TIRMIDHI:3140/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3140/r2.speaker: author
TIRMIDHI:3140/r2.claim: Tirmidhi grades this route hasan sahih gharib.
TIRMIDHI:3140/r2.anchor: قال هذا حديث حسن صحيح غريب من هذا الوجه

TIRMIDHI:3141/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3141/r1.speaker: عبد الله
TIRMIDHI:3141/r1.claim: Abdullah reports that Jewish men asked the Prophet about the Spirit; after receiving revelation, he answered with 17:85. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
TIRMIDHI:3141/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال كنت أمشي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حرث بالمدينة
